mech.mallefisk.interets.title: "Intérêts" effect: shared power, then shields below 50% HP
mech.mallefisk.interets.summary: From the start of the fight until his death, Malléfisk has the "Intérêts" effect (cannot be debuffed): he and the character attacking him permanently gain power. Once Malléfisk drops to half of his maximum vitality, every damage line he takes gives him shield points.
mech.mallefisk.interets.notes.0: The "Intérêts" effect itself is described as non-debuffable; only the shields he gains are presented as removable by debuff.
mech.mallefisk.interets.unknownAspects.0: The page carries a banner saying it needs revision and that information may be wrong or missing.
mech.mallefisk.interets.unknownAspects.1: Undated page: impossible to know whether the mechanic matches the current version (Dofus 3).
mech.mallefisk.interets.unknownAspects.2: Duration of the gained shields is not stated.
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Bring Malléfisk down to 50% of his vitality.
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The shield gain only applies from half of his vitality.
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Then hit with few damage lines but powerful blows (the guide mentions Colère de Iop).
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Every damage line he takes below 50% gives him shields.
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If his shields stack up, remove them with a debuff.
mech.mallefisk.interets.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The guide states that his shield points can be removed by debuffing him.

mech.mallefisk.vagues.title: Waves arrive every 5 turns
mech.mallefisk.vagues.summary: Single-room fight with 5 waves: the boss is present from the start; the following waves arrive on turns 6, 11, 16 and 21, or immediately if the current wave is fully eliminated.
mech.mallefisk.vagues.turnConditions: Waves 2 to 5 on turns 6, 11, 16 and 21 (earlier if the previous wave is eliminated).
mech.mallefisk.vagues.unknownAspects.0: The page carries a 'needs revision' banner.

mech.phossile.abime.title: "Abîme": instant death within 3 cells on turn 5, then every 4 turns
mech.phossile.abime.summary: At the start of his turn, from turn 5 and then every 4 turns (T5, T9, T13…), the Phossile instantly kills all characters within a circle of radius 3 around him.
mech.phossile.abime.turnConditions: Turns 5, 9, 13… (every 4 turns from turn 5), at the start of the Phossile's turn.
mech.phossile.abime.notes.0: Any character within 3 cells of the Phossile at the start of his Abîme turn is killed (one-shot).
mech.phossile.abime.sequences.0.label: Avoid Abîme
mech.phossile.abime.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Ideally, kill the Phossile before his turn 5.
mech.phossile.abime.sequences.0.steps.2.action: If he is still alive on turn 4, move all characters more than 3 cells away from him before he plays his turn 5.
mech.phossile.abime.sequences.0.steps.2.position: More than 3 range from the Phossile

mech.phossile.centrage.title: "Centrage": bonus to distant enemies at end of turn
mech.phossile.centrage.summary: When a character ends their turn, enemies more than 8 range away from them gain 1 MP for 1 turn (not stackable) and a shield equal to 150% of their level; that character's allies within a radius of 4 around them also receive the shield.
mech.phossile.centrage.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.phossile.centrage.sequences.0.steps.1.action: End your turns within 8 range of the Phossile.
mech.phossile.centrage.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Within 8 range of the Phossile (but more than 3 range away because of Abîme)
mech.phossile.centrage.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Phossile then does not benefit from the Centrage bonus.

mech.phossile.glyphiphi.title: "Glyphiphi": red glyph on push/pull
mech.phossile.glyphiphi.summary: Every time a character or a monster (except the Phossile) is pushed or pulled, a one-cell red glyph appears under them; it lasts 3 turns and increases damage taken by whoever stands on it by 30%.

mech.phossile.vagues.title: Waves every 5 turns, invulnerable for 1 turn on arrival
mech.phossile.vagues.summary: Waves 2 to 5 arrive on turns 6, 11, 16 and 21, or earlier if the current wave is eliminated. An arriving wave is invulnerable for 1 turn.

mech.roi-nidas.boubourse.title: Boubourse: switches sides at 1 HP for 2 turns
mech.roi-nidas.boubourse.summary: The Boubourse starts adjacent to Roi Nidas; it is not a summon and it plays last. It has a threshold at 1 HP: once reached, it joins your side for 2 turns, then returns to the enemy side, adjacent to Roi Nidas. On the enemy side, its "Cadeau Empoisonné" spell buffs the monsters (Roi Nidas even more); on your side, it gives shields to your characters, reduces the duration of their effects and kills summons adjacent to the target.
mech.roi-nidas.boubourse.expectedStateChange: The Boubourse joins the players' side for 2 turns.
mech.roi-nidas.boubourse.notes.0: On the enemy side, Cadeau Empoisonné gives 200 power and 30% critical to the monsters, and 300 power and 50% critical to Roi Nidas (guide values).

mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.title: "Confusion" and the Zizanie state
mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.summary: Roi Nidas's "Confusion" spell applies the Zizanie state. On Nidas's next turn, each character under Zizanie deals damage in a 2-range circle around themselves, and the targets hit lose 2 turns of effects.
mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before Roi Nidas's next turn, move characters under Zizanie away from their allies.
mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.sequences.0.steps.1.position: No ally within 2 range of a character under Zizanie
mech.roi-nidas.zizanie.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Otherwise they are hit and debuffed by 2 turns.

mech.roi-nidas.mon-precieux.title: "Mon Précieux": swaps position with the Boubourse
mech.roi-nidas.mon-precieux.summary: Roi Nidas can swap positions with the Boubourse up to 10 range without line of sight, from turn 3 and then every 2 turns.

mech.roi-nidas.vagues.title: Waves on turns 1, 6, 11, 16, 21; new waves invulnerable
mech.roi-nidas.vagues.summary: The first wave is present on turn 1, then a wave arrives every 5 turns (6, 11, 16, 21). Monsters from new waves appear on the monsters' starting cells, have 25% less vitality and stay invulnerable until they have played at least one turn.
mech.roi-nidas.vagues.unknownAspects.0: The page does not specify here whether a wave arrives earlier when the previous one is eliminated (stated generally for dimension dungeons on other pages).

mech.toxoliath.toxmose.title: "Toxmose": poison per MP used after hitting the Toxoliath
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.summary: The Toxoliath has no invulnerable state. Throughout the fight, every direct damage line he takes inflicts on the attacker a water poison (not stackable) of 700 damage per MP used, for 2 turns. The poison disappears if the Toxoliath dies.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.notes.0: The character who finishes off the Toxoliath can use their MP normally, since the poison disappears on his death.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.notes.1: Using your MP before hitting does not avoid the poison (according to the guide).
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.notes.2: The poison can be debuffed, but it stays active for the current turn even if one turn of effects is removed.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Position yourself before you start hitting the Toxoliath (possibly kill one or more monsters first).
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Once the Toxoliath has been hit, using MP costs 700 damage per MP.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.steps.2.action: After hitting him, move only with spells (teleport, leap…) rather than with MP.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Option: kill him in a single turn with one character.
mech.toxoliath.toxmose.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The poison disappears when the Toxoliath dies.

mech.toxoliath.poison-volatile.title: "Poison Volatile" from turn 6
mech.toxoliath.poison-volatile.summary: From turn 6 (4-turn cooldown), the Toxoliath casts "Poison Volatile": for 2 turns all characters gain 2 MP, lose 2 AP and suffer a start-of-turn fire poison, and a size-8 inverted circle glyph increases damage taken. The guide advises killing the Toxoliath before turn 6.
mech.toxoliath.poison-volatile.unknownAspects.0: The glyph's exact effect is worded differently depending on the section: "increases damage taken by 50% for 2 turns" (boss spells) vs "increases damage taken by 50% for each poison suffered" (Relation toxique achievement).

mech.toxoliath.venin-salvateur.title: "Venin Salvateur": purple target that heals its attackers
mech.toxoliath.venin-salvateur.summary: Once per turn, at infinite range, the Toxoliath puts a character in the "Venin Salvateur" state for 1 turn: they take 50% more damage, lose 1 turn of effects each time they take damage, and heal those who attack them for 150% of the damage dealt. The "Jouvence" state prevents them from being targeted again for 2 turns.

mech.reine-des-voleurs.bombes-reduction.title: 10% less damage taken per Bonbombe present; immune to bombs
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bombes-reduction.summary: The Reine des Voleurs takes 10% less damage for each Bonbombe on the map, and she is immune to bomb explosion damage.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bombes-reduction.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bombes-reduction.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Focus damage on the Reine when few Bonbombes are on the map.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bombes-reduction.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Her damage reduction depends on the number of bombs.

mech.reine-des-voleurs.bonbombes.title: Bonbombes summoned by players: red ones kill, blue ones heal
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bonbombes.summary: Every turn, each character summons a Bonbombe 2 range in front of them (then clockwise if the cell is occupied). When a character has 2 Bonbombes, the oldest one explodes on their turn and chain-triggers those in line with it. A red bomb kills all characters in line up to 10 range; bombs diagonal to an explosion turn blue and then fully heal characters in line. Both colours deal about 1200 fire damage to monsters. Bonbombes are invulnerable, can be pushed but not carried.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bonbombes.notes.0: A blue bomb does not protect against a red bomb in the same line: the character still dies.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bonbombes.notes.1: Bonbombes are invulnerable: they cannot be killed, only moved by pushing (not by carry/throw).
mech.reine-des-voleurs.bonbombes.unknownAspects.0: The guide's 'autowin' placement relies on diagrams (images) that cannot be read in the extracted text.

mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.title: "Mort en Sursis": death after 6 turns without a Bonbombe heal
mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.summary: The "Mort en Sursis" spell (in line, up to 5 range) pulls the Reine towards the target and swaps their positions. An enemy hit receives the "Mort en sursis" state: they die after 6 turns, unless they have been healed by a (blue) Bonbombe or the Reine is killed first.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.sequences.0.label: Counters mentioned by the guide
mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Keep the Reine and the monsters at a distance.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Avoid Mort en sursis and the position swaps.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.mort-en-sursis.sequences.0.steps.2.action: If a character is under Mort en sursis, get them healed by a blue Bonbombe or kill the Reine within 6 turns.

mech.reine-des-voleurs.peche-mignon.title: "Péché Mignon": +50% damage taken after the Reine's death
mech.reine-des-voleurs.peche-mignon.summary: When the Reine des Voleurs dies, your characters take 50% more damage for the rest of the fight.

mech.reine-des-voleurs.brume.title: "Brume": invisibility in a glyph, 3 possible cells
mech.reine-des-voleurs.brume.summary: At the end of her turn, the Reine places a black glyph of radius 3 that makes her invisible (as well as the monsters inside it). She is always on one of the 3 cells of the glyph's upper edge. Not before turn 4, 3-turn cooldown.
mech.reine-des-voleurs.brume.unknownAspects.0: The diagram of the 3 possible cells is an image that cannot be read in the extracted text.

mech.fraktale.auroraire.title: Auroraire: rotation direction depends on distance to the boss
mech.fraktale.auroraire.summary: On the first turn, Fraktale summons an Auroraire on cell I of the floor clock. If it moves clockwise, your attacks deal damage; if it moves back (counter-clockwise), your damaging spells heal enemies and allies. Above 50% of the boss's vitality: boss more than 4 range from the Auroraire → clockwise, boss within 4 range → counter-clockwise. Below 50%: the effect is reversed. It moves at the start of each player's turn.
mech.fraktale.auroraire.unknownAspects.0: Undated page; the boss's spells are listed as "under study and coming soon".
mech.fraktale.auroraire.unknownAspects.1: Exact behaviour at exactly 4 range is worded as "within the 4-range zone"; not specified further.
mech.fraktale.auroraire.sequences.0.label: Managing distance
mech.fraktale.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.1.action: While Fraktale has more than 50% of his vitality: keep him more than 4 range from the Auroraire.
mech.fraktale.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Auroraire then moves clockwise and your damage hits.
mech.fraktale.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.2.action: When Fraktale drops below 50% of his vitality: keep him within 4 range of the Auroraire.
mech.fraktale.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Check the heart-shaped state icon above the Auroraire before hitting.

mech.fraktale.vagues.title: Waves arrive every 5 turns
mech.fraktale.vagues.summary: Waves 2 to 5 arrive on turns 6, 11, 16 and 21, unless the current wave is eliminated earlier.

mech.xlii.auroraire.title: Auroraire: damage modifier based on the hour
mech.xlii.auroraire.summary: XLII has no invulnerable state. His Auroraire starts at 12 o'clock and moves forward one hour on each ally's turn. From 12 to 5 o'clock, you and the monsters hit less; from 6 to 11 o'clock, everyone hits harder (see the guide's table). The Auroraire is invulnerable and cannot be moved; hitting it teleports you symmetrically. Killing XLII makes the Auroraire and its bonuses/penalties disappear.
mech.xlii.auroraire.notes.0: The more characters in the fight, the faster the Auroraire turns.
mech.xlii.auroraire.unknownAspects.0: Detailed values per hour (x40% to x150%) come from a table on the page predating Dofus 3; to be rechecked in game.
mech.xlii.auroraire.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.xlii.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.1.action: During the unfavourable hours (12 to 5 o'clock), buff up and get into position.
mech.xlii.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.2.action: From the 6th hour, kill the monsters (Trantroa first according to the guide).
mech.xlii.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Around the 9th-10th hour, start on XLII so as to kill him before the 12th hour.
mech.xlii.auroraire.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: At the 12th hour, damage dealt is heavily reduced again.

mech.xlii.dereglement.title: Dérèglement state: position swap if XLII is moved
mech.xlii.dereglement.summary: XLII is in the Lourd state for the whole fight. If he is moved, he enters the Dérèglement state, which lets him cast "Dérèglement": a position swap with an ally at infinite range (2 times per turn).
mech.xlii.dereglement.notes.0: Pushing him back can let him get closer via an ally; the guide advises, if you push him, to also move his allies away or apply the Pesanteur state to him.

mech.xlii.pacifiste.title: "Souffle démoniaque": Pacifiste state within 3 range
mech.xlii.pacifiste.summary: XLII can hit and apply the Pacifiste state for 1 turn (prevents attacking) up to 3 range without line of sight. The state can be debuffed.
mech.xlii.pacifiste.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.xlii.pacifiste.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Stay more than 3 range from XLII.

mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerability: permanently eliminate the 5 waves
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.summary: The Vortex loses all his MP at the start of the fight, cannot be moved, is invulnerable, and resurrects every monster killed. To make him vulnerable, you must permanently eliminate the 5 waves: each monster must be killed a second time at the same Auroraire hour as one of its previous deaths. Since 3.7, a monster killed twice at the same hour is no longer resummoned.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: The Vortex loses the Invulnerable state one turn after the last monster's permanent death.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.prerequisites.0: All monsters of the 5 waves must have been permanently eliminated (killed a second time at an hour when they had already been killed).
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.notes.0: A monster killed at a different hour from the previous one is resurrected again and can then be permanently eliminated at either of those hours.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.notes.1: During or just after the transition turn, the Vortex uses "Heurage" (teleport adjacent to the Auroraire) if it is available.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: Vulnerability duration not stated (the guide does not mention a return to invulnerability).
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Make the Vortex vulnerable
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill a monster and note the Auroraire's hour at that moment.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Vortex resurrects it with that hour's bonus.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill it again when the Auroraire comes back to that same hour.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.requiredState: Yellow star above the monster (indicates the right hour)
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Repeat for all monsters of the 5 waves.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: After the last monster's permanent death: a turn where the Vortex stays invulnerable without playing and the characters return to their starting positions; use it to buff up and get into position.
mech.vortex.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: On the next turn, the Vortex loses invulnerability and plays; stay out of range of his line spells (8 range without line of sight).

mech.vortex.auroraire.title: Auroraire: hourly bonuses for resurrected monsters
mech.vortex.auroraire.summary: The Auroraire moves forward one hour at the start of each character's turn. Each hour gives a specific (stackable) bonus to the monster killed at that hour for its resurrection; the Vortex also gains these bonuses, only once per hour. An entity on the Auroraire's destination cell swaps places with it.
mech.vortex.auroraire.notes.0: With a number of characters that divides 12 (2, 3, 4, 6), the Auroraire's cycle is regular: the same character will be able to re-kill a monster they killed.

mech.vortex.en-temps-et-en-heure.title: "En temps et en heure": hits in the Auroraire's lines
mech.vortex.en-temps-et-en-heure.summary: On each of the Vortex's turns, this spell automatically hits characters and summons in line with the Auroraire and applies 20% erosion to them.
mech.vortex.en-temps-et-en-heure.sequences.0.label: Positioning
mech.vortex.en-temps-et-en-heure.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Do not end your turn in line with the position the Auroraire will occupy on the Vortex's turn.
mech.vortex.en-temps-et-en-heure.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: With 4 players it is only at 4, 8 and 12 o'clock on his turn; with 6, at 6 and 12 o'clock; with 3, at 3, 6, 9 and 12 o'clock (if no glyph is stepped on).

mech.vortex.glyphes.title: Monster glyphs: place swap and Auroraire advance
mech.vortex.glyphes.summary: At the start of its turn, each monster leaves a glyph on its cell. Walking into it swaps places with that monster, moves the Auroraire forward one hour and gives a bonus (depending on the monster) to the monster and the character.
mech.vortex.glyphes.notes.0: Stepping on a glyph shifts the Auroraire's cycle and therefore the hours planned for re-killing the monsters.

mech.vortex.heurage.title: "Heurage": teleport adjacent to the Auroraire
mech.vortex.heurage.summary: Once he has recovered his MP, the Vortex can teleport adjacent to the Auroraire (3-turn cooldown). The guide describes it as the main danger of the Vortex when alone.
mech.vortex.heurage.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.vortex.heurage.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Remember the turn he uses Heurage, then move away from the Auroraire every 3 turns.

mech.pounicheur.pupuces.title: Match the state of the 3 pupuces to hit without reflection
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.summary: At the start of the fight, the Pounicheur summons three invulnerable fleas (Tipoune, Tipoune, Tipoude) in state I, II or III; the boss carries his fleas' states. If you hit him while the fleas do not all have the same state, he reflects the damage onto the whole team. Hitting a flea from an adjacent cell increments its state (I→II→III→I) and pushes you back 2 cells, while the other two fleas decrement.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.expectedStateChange: The Pounicheur has only one state number left; the damage reflection does not apply.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.turnConditions: The Pounicheur changes his fleas' state at the start of each of his turns.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.prerequisites.0: The three pupuces must have the same state number (I, II or III).
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.notes.0: According to the guide, poisons are not reflected.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.notes.1: According to the guide, the reflection does not happen if the Pounicheur dies from a single damage line.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.notes.2: Depending on the states, it is not always possible to align the three fleas within the turn; the guide then advises waiting a turn.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.notes.3: When the three fleas are in the same state, the Pounicheur casts "Pourrification", which removes one turn of effects "from all allies".
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.unknownAspects.0: Inconsistent reflection value on the page: "almost double" in the Boss section, "200%" in the achievement section.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.unknownAspects.1: For Pourrification, the page does not specify whether "allies" means the Pounicheur's allies or the players' characters.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.unknownAspects.2: Undated page: game version not confirmed.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.label: Disable the damage reflection
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Read the state (I, II or III) of each pupuce.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit a pupuce from an adjacent cell (not necessarily with your weapon).
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Its state goes up one step and the other two go down one step; the character is pushed back 2 cells.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Repeat until the three pupuces have the same state.
mech.pounicheur.pupuces.sequences.0.steps.4.requiredState: All 3 pupuces in the same state

mech.ush-galesh.partage-dommages.title: Two Ush Galesh sharing damage
mech.ush-galesh.partage-dommages.summary: The fight has two Ush Galesh. Damage dealt to one is halved and applied to each of the two.
mech.ush-galesh.partage-dommages.unknownAspects.0: Undated page: game version not confirmed.

mech.ush-galesh.alternance.title: Alternate ranged hits and melee hits
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.summary: Ush only takes damage if you alternate hit types: after a ranged hit, the next one must be dealt from an adjacent cell (not necessarily with a weapon), then ranged again, and so on. Each hit taken changes his state; red state = hit in melee, black state = hit at range.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.notes.0: Two ranged hits in a row: the second deals no damage (guide example).
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.notes.1: Ush locks well and both Ush share the Lourd state: getting out of melee with him or pushing him is not always possible.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.unknownAspects.0: Partly contradictory state description: the "Rouge et Noir" spell is described as applying both the Rouge state and the Noir state to one of the Ush, whereas the hit rule depends on a single state.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.unknownAspects.1: It is unknown whether the alternation is tracked per Ush or shared by both, or whether it depends on the character hitting.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.unknownAspects.2: Undated page: game version not confirmed.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.label: Deal damage
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Check the state of the targeted Ush.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Red state: hit him from an adjacent cell.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.steps.2.when: The targeted Ush is in the Rouge state.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Black state: hit him at range.
mech.ush-galesh.alternance.sequences.0.steps.3.when: The targeted Ush is in the Noir state.

mech.chaloeil.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerable until turn 21 (survival)
mech.chaloeil.invulnerabilite.summary: The Chaloeil cannot be made vulnerable by any action: he becomes vulnerable automatically after 20 turns (on turn 21), at the same time as the 5th wave arrives. He then gains 200 MP dodge and the Inébranlable state for the rest of the fight. The waves therefore always arrive on turns 1, 6, 11, 16 and 21.
mech.chaloeil.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: The Chaloeil loses invulnerability and gains 200 MP dodge and the Inébranlable state.
mech.chaloeil.invulnerabilite.notes.0: Wave 5 arrives at the same time; the guide describes it as very dangerous if monsters from previous waves are still alive.
mech.chaloeil.invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: Vulnerability duration: the guide only says "for the rest of the fight" for the bonuses; it does not mention a return to invulnerability.

mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.title: Dice cells: Dé summons and healing glyphs
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.summary: Every cell of the map has a die value from 1 to 6. Depending on the value of the cell where the Chaloeil ends his turn, he summons Dés (static summons, 2000 HP) on cells of the same value at an even distance from him, and places white glyphs (full heal at end of turn) on those at an odd distance. The Dés disappear at the start of his turn. Each entity takes the Dé state of the cell where it ends its turn.
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.notes.0: Dés are not summoned on an already occupied cell.
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.notes.1: The diagrams of the 12 possible placements are images that cannot be read in the extracted text.
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Remove MP from the Chaloeil (he only has 4) to choose the cell where he ends his turn.
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Control where the Dés and glyphs go.
mech.chaloeil.des-et-glyphes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: End your turn on a white glyph to be fully healed.

mech.chaloeil.malus-meme-etat.title: Monsters hitting characters with the same Dé state
mech.chaloeil.malus-meme-etat.summary: From turn 2, every turn, each monster (except the Chaloeil) hits for 450 in a random element and applies 20% erosion for 1 turn to all characters and summons that have the same Dé state as it.

mech.chaloeil.gros-yeux.title: "Gros Yeux": buffs based on Dé state (turns 3, 6, 9…)
mech.chaloeil.gros-yeux.summary: From turn 3 and then every 3 turns, the Chaloeil buffs himself and the monsters for 1 turn according to their Dé state: Dé 1 MP dodge, Dé 2 range, Dé 3 cannot be moved, Dé 4 MP, Dé 5 heals, Dé 6 power. The guide flags Dé 4 (3 MP) and Dé 6 (600 power) as the most dangerous.

mech.nileza.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state
mech.nileza.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: The Nileza has no invulnerable state: he can be hit from the start. The difficulty comes from the mechanics of his "Cohobation" passive (one-shot when adjacent, place swap, reflection, Pacifiste).

mech.nileza.chifouchimie.title: "Chifouchimie": ending your turn adjacent to an ally kills them
mech.nileza.chifouchimie.summary: Throughout the fight, a character who ends their turn adjacent to another character instantly kills that character. Summons are not affected.
mech.nileza.chifouchimie.notes.0: Ending your turn next to an ally = instant death of that ally.

mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.title: Place swap and damage reflection when hit at range
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.summary: Each ranged damage line the Nileza takes makes him swap places with the attacker (a pink glyph appears under the character). Then he applies 40% erosion for 1 turn and reflects 200% of the damage taken as air damage to all entities (allies and enemies alike) in a 2-range circle around his destination cell. The reflection always happens after the swap. In melee, his "Liqueur de Fée Ling" (active 2 turns out of 3) heals and buffs him.
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.label: Guide's tactical tips
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Stand within 2 range of the monsters, then hit the Nileza at range.
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: After the swap, the 200% reflection hits the monsters around him.
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Never be within 2 range of an ally when hitting the Nileza.
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The reflection would hit the ally and erode them.
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Only hit in melee on turns 3, 6, 9…
mech.nileza.ogavodra-molalite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Liqueur de Fée Ling is active on the other turns.

mech.nileza.pacifiste-distance.title: Pacifiste state for distant characters (odd turns from turn 3)
mech.nileza.pacifiste-distance.summary: At the start of his turn, on odd turns from turn 3, the Nileza makes characters who are too far from him Pacifiste for 2 turns, with a shrinking radius: more than 11 range on turn 3, more than 9 range on turn 5, more than 7 range on turn 7, then more than 5 range on turn 9 and every 2 turns after that. Each step adds a penalty to all characters (dodge, lock, Pesanteur, then Insoignable). He flees after these spells; hitting him lets you bring him back through the place swap.
mech.nileza.pacifiste-distance.turnConditions: Odd turns from turn 3, at the start of the Nileza's turn.
mech.nileza.pacifiste-distance.notes.0: The Pacifiste, Pesanteur and Insoignable states cannot be debuffed.

mech.nileza.melange-instable.title: "Mélange Instable": effect based on the Nileza's HP
mech.nileza.melange-instable.summary: At the start of his turn, the Nileza applies to all characters an effect that depends on his HP percentage: Acide (76-100%) final damage gain but resistance loss on each attack; Amer (40-75%) increased heals but damage taken when healed; Aigre (0-39%) increased critical but MP loss on each critical hit.

mech.klime.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerability removed by indirect pushback damage (from turn 3)
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.summary: The Klime is invulnerable. Only from the start of turn 3, you remove this state for 1 turn by making him take indirect pushback damage: push an ally, a summon or an enemy into him.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: The Klime loses the Invulnerable state for 1 turn.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.notes.0: Once vulnerable, the Klime gets the "Cuir à feu doux" spell (monsters return to their start-of-turn position, loss of 6 MP, +300 damage).
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Guide strategy
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters accompanying the Klime first.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The guide advises killing the Klime last and not making him vulnerable before then.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Push an entity (ally, summon or enemy) into the Klime.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill him quickly during the vulnerability turn.
mech.klime.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The less HP he has, the harder he hits.

mech.klime.carcassetagne.title: "Carcassetagne": Pacifiste unless you end your turn on a white glyph
mech.klime.carcassetagne.summary: Characters are protected for 2 turns by the "Peau lisse" state. Then, from turn 3, any character who did not end their previous turn in a white glyph becomes Pacifiste for 1 turn. The Klime and each monster place a one-cell white glyph at the start of their turn (lasts 2 turns); it gives "Peau lisse" to characters who end their turn on it, but +300 damage to monsters who end theirs on it. A monster's glyphs disappear when it dies.
mech.klime.carcassetagne.notes.0: If all monsters are eliminated before turn 3, the Klime only applies Pacifiste from turn 4.
mech.klime.carcassetagne.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.klime.carcassetagne.sequences.0.steps.1.action: From turn 2, have the characters who need to hit end their turn in a white glyph.
mech.klime.carcassetagne.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Otherwise they will be Pacifiste on the next turn.
mech.klime.carcassetagne.sequences.0.steps.2.action: If there are not enough glyphs, a character playing later can move an ally out of the glyph to take their place.
mech.klime.carcassetagne.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Debuff the 300 damage gained by the Klime or a monster on a glyph.

mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerability removed by a Zombi monster's "Zombidule" explosion
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.summary: The Sylargh starts invulnerable (and stays Lourd for the whole fight). Any monster killed is resummoned in the "Zombi" state 6 range away by the next monster to play. When you kill a Zombi monster, its "Zombidule" effect makes the Sylargh vulnerable for 1 turn if he is between 5 and 10 range from that monster.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: The Sylargh loses invulnerability for 1 turn.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.notes.0: The Sylargh is also resummoned if he dies while monsters are still alive.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.notes.1: The Zombidule explosion directly kills the other Zombi monsters and gives +100 damage (stacks 3 times) to everyone.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Make the Sylargh vulnerable
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill a monster; it comes back as a Zombi (10% of its HP) 6 range from the next monster to play.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place the Sylargh between 5 and 10 range from a Zombi monster.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Too close, and he does not lose invulnerability.
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Finish off the Zombi while staying away from it (explosion of 1,200 fire damage in a circle of 5).
mech.sylargh.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Hit the Sylargh during his vulnerability turn.

mech.sylargh.pacifiste-90pv.title: Pacifiste for characters at 90% HP or more
mech.sylargh.pacifiste-90pv.summary: When a Zombi monster is killed, all characters with 90% or more of their max HP become Pacifiste for 1 turn (cannot be debuffed). So you must stay below 90% HP; the guide suggests hitting your allies if needed.

mech.sylargh.chaine-reinvocation.title: Resummon chain
mech.sylargh.chaine-reinvocation.summary: It is always the last monster killed that gets resummoned; several deaths create a chain of summoners. Killing the first resummoned monster also kills the ones it resummoned. Zombis cannot be moved for 1 turn, gain 300 damage for 2 turns and skip their first turn.

mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.title: Invulnerable: kill him by keeping him in the "Infection" state for 6 turns
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.summary: Like all Krobes, the Protozorreur stays invulnerable and cannot be moved. He dies after 6 consecutive turns in the "Infection" state. He enters this state (for 3 turns, +2 MP) by entering a purple glyph, which is placed under any character who takes damage. Only the first hit on him each turn, if the attacker is in line, pulls him adjacent: use this to pull him into a glyph, at least every 2 turns.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.expectedResult: The Protozorreur dies at the end of his 6th turn of Infection.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.notes.0: He still plays his 6th Infection turn before dying: keep protecting yourselves (MP removal, etc.).
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.notes.1: Hitting the Protozorreur deals the damage to the Malamibe, as with the other Krobes.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.label: Guide method
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.1.action: With the character who has initiative, create a purple glyph (by taking damage) between yourself and the Protozorreur, in line with him.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The guide recommends a class able to damage itself (e.g. Enutrof).
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit him in line with a cheap spell to pull him; he stops in the glyph.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Then hit him once while not in line.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Entering Infection resets his passive: another in-line hit would pull him again.
mech.protozorreur.infection-6-tours.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Repeat at least every 2 turns until 6 consecutive turns of Infection.

mech.protozorreur.malamibe.title: Malamibe: kill it before 2 full turns
mech.protozorreur.malamibe.summary: Since the Krobes are invulnerable, the Malamibe summoned at the start of the fight intercepts the damage dealt to them (2000 HP per living character). Hitting a Krobe deals normal damage to it; hitting it directly reduces damage by 50%. It is resummoned on each death by the next enemy. If it stays alive for 2 full turns, it kills all opponents and the fight is lost.
mech.protozorreur.malamibe.notes.0: Malamibe alive for 2 full turns = defeat.
mech.protozorreur.malamibe.unknownAspects.0: The number of consecutive turns needed to eliminate an ordinary Krobe is inconsistent on the page (3 in the text, 5 in the table header); for the Protozorreur, 6 turns are stated.

mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.title: No invulnerability, but "Horreur Cosmique" (place swaps)
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.summary: The boss has no invulnerable state. But every direct damage dealt to an enemy makes the attacker swap places with the nearest entity (excluding summons). Swapping 2 times with the same enemy in one turn makes it invulnerable until that ally's next turn and gives 1 Folie state; 2 times with the same ally gives 1 Folie state. The effect is limited to 10 triggers per turn.
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.notes.0: The swap is a forced movement: Pesanteur, Enraciné or Indéplaçable do not prevent it.
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Favour poisons and avoid spells with several damage lines.
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.horreur-cosmique.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Poisons do not trigger the place swap.

mech.larve-de-koutoulou.folie.title: "FOLIE !" states (1 to 10, death at 10)
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.folie.summary: Characters accumulate Folie states: Folie 2 makes allies within 2 range take your spells' damage, Folie 4 divides heals received, Folie 6 increases damage taken, Folie 10 kills. You gain them notably by ending your turn in the Koutoulou's line of sight or by being hit by his "Frappe Koutonienne". You lose one at the start of each turn, and one per damage line received from an ally.

mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.title: "Vacillement de l'Univers": teleport into melee
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.summary: From turn 2, at the start of each turn, the Koutoulou teleports all characters in his line of sight adjacent to him (except under Pesanteur, Indéplaçable or Enraciné). He hits very hard in melee. He can also swap places with 2 allies per turn (not on turn 1, blocked by Pesanteur).
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.sequences.0.steps.1.action: End your turn out of the Koutoulou's line of sight (obstacle or summon in front of him).
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Put the Koutoulou or nearby monsters under Pesanteur.
mech.larve-de-koutoulou.vacillement.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He can then no longer swap to get into melee.

mech.capitaine-meno.reduction-et-montee.title: No invulnerability: 50% reduction and +20% final damage per turn
mech.capitaine-meno.reduction-et-montee.summary: The Meno is not invulnerable but has a lot of HP (40,000 at loot 4, 60,000 at loot 8) and reduces damage received by 50% for the whole fight (except poisons). In return, all characters gain 20% final damage every turn (infinite, stackable). Damage dealt to characters by the monsters and the Meno heals him. The guide estimates it takes about ten turns to have enough damage.
mech.capitaine-meno.reduction-et-montee.sequences.0.label: Guide strategy
mech.capitaine-meno.reduction-et-montee.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Final damage goes up by 20% per turn.
mech.capitaine-meno.reduction-et-montee.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Preferably hit the Meno with poisons.

mech.capitaine-meno.invocations-mutation.title: Invulnerable monsters that die in 4 turns; summons from turn 2
mech.capitaine-meno.invocations-mutation.summary: At the start of the fight, the Meno makes all monsters (including those he summons) invulnerable, removes 1 MP from them and makes them lose 25% of their max HP per turn: they die on their own after 4 turns, becoming more dangerous (Mutation) as their HP drops. From turn 2, he summons 2 monsters per turn (3 at loot 5+), following a fixed pattern; a rune shows the location since 3.7.

mech.capitaine-meno.crystalisation.title: "Crystalisation" glyphs: shields and line damage
mech.capitaine-meno.crystalisation.summary: The "Crystalisation" spell places permanent one-cell glyphs. At the start of the Meno's turn, each occupied glyph triggers: 1300 fire damage to all characters in line with the entity on the glyph up to 5 range, and 1000 shield points for 1 turn to the character on the glyph.
mech.capitaine-meno.crystalisation.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.capitaine-meno.crystalisation.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Put each character on a glyph, with no ally in line within 5 range (stand diagonally).
mech.capitaine-meno.crystalisation.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Get the shield without hitting your allies.

mech.dantinea.grokillages.title: Linked Grokillages: damage halved while your Grokillage lives
mech.dantinea.grokillages.summary: Dantinéa has no invulnerable state. At the start of the fight she summons as many Grokillages (0 AP/MP, 1000 HP) as there are characters; each is linked to a character according to fixed positions. While their Grokillage is alive, a character only deals 50% of their damage (to monsters, Grokillages and Dantinéa) and loses 1 MP per turn. Killing their Grokillage restores the character's full damage; Dantinéa's death eliminates all Grokillages.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.expectedStateChange: The character whose Grokillage is eliminated no longer suffers the 50% damage reduction.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.notes.0: At the start of each turn, Dantinéa hits (600 water) all characters in line with the Grokillages and can teleport with them.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.unknownAspects.0: The diagram of the Grokillages' positions is an image that cannot be read in the extracted text.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Position yourself during preparation taking into account the order in which Grokillages are assigned (guide diagram; since 3.7 a rune shows their future location).
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Grokillages' positions and numbers are always the same.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.steps.2.action: First kill the Grokillages of the characters who hit hardest.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: They get their full damage back.
mech.dantinea.grokillages.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Then kill the monsters (Tryde, then Rilur, then Diondin), then Dantinéa, ideally before her turn 11.

mech.dantinea.os-tous-les-5-tours.title: Every 5 turns: one-shot of remaining Grokillages and their characters
mech.dantinea.os-tous-les-5-tours.summary: Every 5 turns, Dantinéa instantly kills her Grokillages that are still alive along with the characters linked to them, then summons a new set of Grokillages to be assigned. So all Grokillages must be eliminated by turns 6, 11, 16, etc.
mech.dantinea.os-tous-les-5-tours.notes.0: Any character whose Grokillage is still alive at that moment is killed (one-shot).

mech.dantinea.cooquillation.title: "Cooquillation": position swap with a Grokillage
mech.dantinea.cooquillation.summary: Dantinéa can swap places with one of her Grokillages up to 6 range without line of sight, from turn 2 and then every 2 turns.

mech.solar.nadir.title: Vulnerable only in the Nadir state (state cycle, sped up by Nécronyx)
mech.solar.nadir.summary: Solar goes through 4 states lasting 3 turns each: Aurore (turns 1-3), Zénith (4-6), Crépuscule (7-9), then Nadir from turn 10. He is invulnerable in Aurore, Zénith and Crépuscule and vulnerable only in Nadir. Applying Nécronyx to him moves him to the next state on his next turn (only one state at a time). If he plays again in Nadir without dying, he goes back to Aurore.
mech.solar.nadir.expectedStateChange: Solar becomes vulnerable in the Nadir state.
mech.solar.nadir.notes.0: Effects on your characters depending on the state: Aurore +1 AP, Zénith +2 AP, Crépuscule -1 AP, Nadir -2 AP; a glyph along the map border applies a different penalty depending on the state.
mech.solar.nadir.unknownAspects.0: The guide does not say how many turns Solar stays in Nadir when the state is reached via Nécronyx.
mech.solar.nadir.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.solar.nadir.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Apply Nécronyx to Solar every turn to cycle his states up to Nadir (at least 3 turns).
mech.solar.nadir.sequences.0.steps.2.action: In Nadir, hit him for one turn without Nécronyx while avoiding the reflection onto allies (size-1 square zone around him).
mech.solar.nadir.sequences.0.steps.3.action: On the next turn, apply Nécronyx to him with the first character in initiative, then finish him off.
mech.solar.nadir.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Nécronyx removes the reflection, and Solar must be under Nécronyx when he dies.

mech.solar.necronyx-obligatoire.title: Nécronyx mandatory before every death (otherwise team one-shot)
mech.solar.necronyx-obligatoire.summary: All monsters (Pyrozomb) resurrect their killed allies and reflect damage around them; on death they deal earth damage in a size-2 circle. Nécronyx (spell obtained from the L'arme fatale quest, castable every 2 turns) must be applied before killing each monster; if Solar dies without being under Nécronyx, the whole team is killed.
mech.solar.necronyx-obligatoire.prerequisites.0: Have the Nécronyx spell (L'arme fatale quest).
mech.solar.necronyx-obligatoire.notes.0: Solar killed without the Nécronyx state: the whole team is one-shot.
mech.solar.necronyx-obligatoire.notes.1: Since 3.7 (reminder from the guide), casting Nécronyx no longer ends the caster's turn.

mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.title: Only the Dagon on your side can damage Bethel
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.summary: Bethel and the Dagon des Profondeurs are invulnerable; the Monolithe is only vulnerable in melee. Killing the Monolithe resummons the Dagon on your side, controlled by the player closest to the Dagon at that moment. Only this Dagon can hit Bethel, in melee with "Souffle Chaud"; your characters cannot hit him. If your Dagon dies, Bethel resummons a Monolithe and a Dagon on his side.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.expectedStateChange: The Dagon joins the players' side and can deal damage to Bethel.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.notes.0: After the Monolithe's death, Bethel gains "Étoile de mer", a large star-shaped glyph that deals water damage and removes AP and MP.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.notes.1: A glyph around the edge of the map removes 100 MP and applies Pesanteur; Bethel pushes back if he is not under Nécronyx.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.unknownAspects.0: The "Vindicte" spell is described as "Lasts 2 turns. ???": unknown effect.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.unknownAspects.1: "Étoile de mer" damage is contradictory on the page (350 in the spell list, 700 in the fight overview).
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.sequences.0.label: Guide walkthrough
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the Monolithe in melee (it gains 20% of its max HP as a debuffable shield at the start of each turn and pushes back 2 cells when adjacent).
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Its death brings the Dagon over to your side.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place the allied Dagon adjacent to Bethel and buff it so it hits with "Souffle Chaud" every turn (about 1000 per turn).
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Apply Nécronyx to Bethel before the killing blow.

mech.bethel-akarna.necronyx.title: Nécronyx mandatory; Bethel removes it after 3 turns
mech.bethel-akarna.necronyx.summary: Nécronyx must be applied to each monster before killing it, and Bethel must be under Nécronyx when he dies, otherwise the whole team is killed. It is advised to apply it to him from turn 1 to stop him pushing you towards the border glyph. Since the 20/01/2026 update, Bethel removes his Nécronyx after 3 turns, on the turn of the character who applied it: it must be renewed (for example on turn 4).
mech.bethel-akarna.necronyx.turnConditions: Renew Nécronyx on Bethel every 3 turns (e.g. turns 1, 4, 7…).
mech.bethel-akarna.necronyx.prerequisites.0: Have the Nécronyx spell (L'arme fatale quest).
mech.bethel-akarna.necronyx.notes.0: Bethel killed without the Nécronyx state: fight lost.

mech.bethel-akarna.aquazomb.title: Aquazomb: end your turn within 6 range of a monster
mech.bethel-akarna.aquazomb.summary: From turn 2, each character must end their turn within 6 range of a monster (Bethel, the Monolithe, summons and resummoned monsters do not count). Otherwise, all monsters gain 2 MP and 1 range for 1 turn (stackable, debuffable) and each monster triggers its special effect.
mech.bethel-akarna.aquazomb.unknownAspects.0: The quoted sentence says both "(or Bethel)" and that Bethel does not count: contradiction on the page.

mech.bethel-akarna.dagon-ennemi.title: Enemy Dagon: push it every turn
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon-ennemi.summary: The enemy Dagon is Intaclable, hits hard in melee and can pull itself up to 8 range in line. Pushing it makes it Inébranlable for 1 turn (until the next turn of the character who pushed it), which prevents it from pulling itself.
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon-ennemi.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.bethel-akarna.dagon-ennemi.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Push the Dagon once per turn, preferably always with the same character playing early in initiative.

mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.title: Resistance removal by push/pull after Nimpatience 3
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.summary: Dazak has more than 100% resistance in every element. He gains a Nimpatience level each turn he does not hit a character. During the two turns after he reaches Nimpatience 3, each push or pull removes 5% resistance in all elements from him (infinite); pushback damage gives him back 10%. Removed resistances stay removed: the cycle can be repeated.
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.notes.0: At level 3, Nimpatience gives him 3 MP and +150% final damage for 2 turns.
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.notes.1: The guide mentions the Iop's "Friction" and "Coup par coup": each forced movement removes 5% resistance from him.
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.sequences.0.label: Guide principle
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Keep Dazak at a distance so he hits nobody and climbs to Nimpatience 3.
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.action: During the next 2 turns, push/pull him as much as possible without pushback damage (into an obstacle).
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: -5% resistance per movement; +10% if he takes pushback damage.
mech.dazak-martegel.resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Repeat until you can kill him.

mech.dazak-martegel.nimpatience.title: Nimpatience: monsters grow stronger if they do not hit
mech.dazak-martegel.nimpatience.summary: Each monster gains a Nimpatience level (3 levels, stackable) every time it cannot hit a character (hitting a summon is not enough). At level 3, it unlocks a new spell or an enhanced effect on the next turn, then returns to level 0 if it was able to cast it. The guide recommends killing the Tanklume before its Nimpatience 3 (it pulls the 4 nearest enemies adjacent to it).

mech.dazak-martegel.ninfiltration.title: "Ninfiltration" (5-cell leap) and "Nintrépidité"
mech.dazak-martegel.ninfiltration.summary: Dazak hits very hard in melee ("Empalement royal": erosion and infinite resistance penalty). He can leap 5 cells in line with "Ninfiltration" on even turns (2, 4, 6…), so keep a 5-cell margin. From turn 3 and then every 2 turns, "Nintrépidité" gives his allies 2 MP and 1500 shield points for 1 turn (debuffable).

mech.malice.battle-royale.title: Malice always invulnerable: fight between allies
mech.malice.battle-royale.summary: Malice can never be hit. The fight (4 characters minimum) is a battle between allies: you must be the last survivor. Most characters are invulnerable; only one or two are vulnerable at a time. Hitting a vulnerable character makes them invulnerable and gives them 200 power (infinite, stackable), then another character becomes vulnerable. All characters are healed at the start of the fight.
mech.malice.battle-royale.prerequisites.0: At least 4 characters; only during the Halouine period.
mech.malice.battle-royale.notes.0: The page states that Malice is not available for Halouine 2025 (technical issues); a Chaudron at [-1,20] gives a Badge de Malicien for 20 Graines de Citwouille Maudites.
mech.malice.battle-royale.unknownAspects.0: Undated page; Malice's availability for Halouine events after 2025 not stated.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Come with 4 characters in total to start the fight.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: You need at least 4 characters to face Malice (you and 3 friends).
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Do not worry about your HP before entering.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: As soon as the fight starts, all characters are automatically healed.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not hit Malice: fight among allies.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Malice always stays invulnerable. It is a kind of Battle Royale: you must be the last survivor.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Hit the vulnerable ally or allies (most are invulnerable).
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Only one or two allies are vulnerable, and not for long.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.5.action: After each hit, look for the new vulnerable ally and hit them in turn.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: A vulnerable character who is hit becomes invulnerable and gains 200 power (infinite and stackable), then another becomes vulnerable, and so on.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Make sure only one character remains before turn 15.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: If you are not alone in the fight before turn 15, everyone loses.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Aim for last place to maximise badges.
mech.malice.battle-royale.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The last survivor wins 5 Badges de Malicien, the others only 1.

mech.malice.tour-15.title: Everyone loses if more than one survivor on turn 15
mech.malice.tour-15.summary: The fight ends when only one character remains; this must happen before turn 15, otherwise everyone loses.
mech.malice.tour-15.notes.0: More than one character still in play on turn 15: everyone is defeated.

mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.title: Vulnerable after 3 Éclats de Kao die
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.summary: The Prêtresse is invulnerable from the start of the fight ("Artisanat du Kao"). Each Éclat de Kao killed increments a Roman numeral above her (I, II, III); at III, she becomes vulnerable. Each step makes her stronger: Forastero +52%, Trinitario +74%, Criollo +99% final damage (infinite). A summoned Éclat also makes its summoner invulnerable: if she summons one after III, you just need to kill it for her to become vulnerable again.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.expectedStateChange: The Prêtresse loses invulnerability (step III "Criollo", +99% final damage).
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.notes.0: While an Éclat is present, the Prêtresse is Intaclable.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.unknownAspects.0: Contradiction: the fight overview says she is vulnerable "for the rest of the fight", while the strategy says a new Éclat makes her invulnerable again.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.unknownAspects.1: Case of an Éclat dying on its own: the page gives two contradictory statements (no increment after 2 turns; increment tied to the loss of the HP bonus).
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Outside of achievements, kill the monsters first without killing the Éclats (poisons recommended: they ignore the 50% reduction).
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Each Éclat killed makes the Prêtresse stronger.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.sequences.0.steps.2.action: When only the Prêtresse remains, kill 3 Éclats, ideally in a single hit, with poison or from an external source (bomb, summon).
mech.pretresse-de-kao.eclats.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Focus her as soon as she is vulnerable; if she resummons an Éclat, kill it to make her vulnerable again.

mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolatomanie.title: Éclat de Kao: -50% damage taken by monsters
mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolatomanie.summary: All monsters can summon an Éclat de Kao (only one at a time; 2-turn cooldown per monster). While it is present, monsters take 50% less damage and receive a bonus specific to each one; the Éclat makes its summoner invulnerable. The Éclat has 1000 HP + 500 HP per character for 1 turn and dies automatically after 2 turns.

mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolathee.title: Chocolathée and "Cloches du Kao" on odd turns
mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolathee.summary: Hitting an Éclat directly gives the Chocolathée state for 3 turns (cannot be debuffed), unless the Éclat is killed in one hit, with poison or by an external source. On odd turns, "Cloches du Kao" hits all enemies on the map (300 neutral base) with +50 base damage per character under Chocolathée.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolathee.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolathee.sequences.0.steps.1.action: If you cannot kill the Éclat in a single hit, always hit it with the same character.
mech.pretresse-de-kao.chocolathee.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Limit the number of characters under Chocolathée.

mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.title: Thresholds at 75% and 50% HP: Ilyzaelle joins your side (invulnerable)
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.summary: The fight is won by removing half of Ilyzaelle's HP, in two phases. As soon as an attack takes her below 75% of her HP, she teleports to your side on a fixed cell for 2 turns: she becomes invulnerable, stops hitting you and places a size-3 orange glyph (your damage +400%, damage taken -30%); the monsters gain 2 MP and those entering the glyph take 15,000 neutral damage. She then returns to the enemy side, staying invulnerable for 1 turn. Below 50%, she comes back to your side: you just need to survive 2 turns, then she kills the monsters and the fight ends.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.expectedStateChange: Ilyzaelle switches sides and becomes invulnerable for 2 turns, then stays invulnerable for 1 turn after returning to the enemy side.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.expectedResult: After the 2 turns of the second phase, Ilyzaelle kills all the monsters: victory.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.vulnerabilityDuration: 2 turns on your side (+1 turn of invulnerability after the first phase).
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.notes.0: Do not erode Ilyzaelle: reducing her max HP forces you to deal more damage to reach the thresholds (guide tip).
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.notes.1: Avoid healing her while she is on your side and avoid a Chause sharing its damage with her in the second phase.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.unknownAspects.0: Guide predates Dofus 3 (published 01/11/2019, no update date): values to recheck.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.unknownAspects.1: The page says she cannot be moved in this phase but does not specify whether her HP can still drop during the 2 turns on your side.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.label: Fight walkthrough
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Bring Ilyzaelle below 75% of her HP.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: She joins your side for 2 turns and places her bonus glyph.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.2.action: During these 2 turns, pull/push the monsters into her glyph and hit from inside the glyph.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Monsters entering it take 15,000 damage; your damage is increased by 400% there.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.3.action: After she returns to the enemy side (invulnerable for 1 turn), bring her below 50%.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Survive 2 turns during the second phase.
mech.ilyzaelle.seuils-possession.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: She then kills all the monsters and the fight is won.

mech.ilyzaelle.possession.title: "Possession": +300% monster vitality and spawns every 3 turns
mech.ilyzaelle.possession.summary: Through her "Possession" spell, all monsters have 300% extra vitality for the whole fight, and Ilyzaelle spawns monsters every 3 turns: 2 monsters from turn 4 with 4 characters or fewer, 2 from turn 3 with 5 characters, 3 from turn 3 with 6 characters or more. Her HP also depends on the number of characters (42,000 with 4 or fewer, up to 60,000 with 8).
mech.ilyzaelle.possession.turnConditions: Spawns every 3 turns, from turn 3 or 4 depending on the number of characters.

mech.ilyzaelle.vers-les-tenebres.title: "Vers les ténèbres": pulls all characters (turns 3, 6, 9…)
mech.ilyzaelle.vers-les-tenebres.summary: From turn 3, with a 3-turn cooldown, Ilyzaelle pulls every character in the fight 10 cells towards her in line; an obstacle (block, ally) stops the pull.
mech.ilyzaelle.vers-les-tenebres.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.ilyzaelle.vers-les-tenebres.sequences.0.steps.1.action: On turns 3, 6, 9…, end your turn behind a block or a summon (or become stabilised).

mech.ilyzaelle.brulure.title: The dungeon's Brûlure state
mech.ilyzaelle.brulure.summary: Every time you move a monster or try to remove its MP, you gain the Brûlure state, which the next monster to play consumes to cast a special spell on you (critical removal, return to start-of-turn position with +150% damage taken, 1100 explosion around you, invisibility detection, pull and 4 MP steal depending on the monster).
mech.ilyzaelle.brulure.notes.0: Ilyzaelle has 250 critical resistance: the guide advises equipping as little critical as possible.

mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.title: "Résilience vampyrique" (-90% damage) bypassed with ghouls or erosion
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.summary: From the start of the fight, Anerice reduces all damage she takes by 90% (infinite). Each ghoul on the map (character or summon transformed by her Goulification spell) increases the damage she takes: from 3 ghouls you deal "normal" damage to her, ideally 4. Other method: erode her, since erosion is calculated without taking Résilience into account, until she is down to 1 max HP.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.notes.0: As a ghoul, you take 150% extra damage; to leave the state, you must take damage from yourself or an ally.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.unknownAspects.0: Guide predates Dofus 3 (published 16/11/2019, no update date).
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.unknownAspects.1: Exact value of the damage-taken increase per ghoul not stated.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.label: Two guide strategies
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.steps.1.action: First kill all the monsters, starting with the Kérigoule (ideally before her turn 2).
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: She shares damage between all monsters from her turn 2.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Strategy 1: let Anerice turn 3 to 4 entities (tanky characters or summons) into ghouls, then hit her.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Each ghoul increases the damage she takes.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.resilience-goul.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Strategy 2: erode her at range (e.g. Cra with Flèche cinglante) while staying more than 14 range from her, down to 1 max HP, then finish her off.

mech.anerice-la-shushess.marche-des-goul.title: "Marche des goules": monsters advance when you hit one
mech.anerice-la-shushess.marche-des-goul.summary: Once per turn per monster, dealing damage to a monster makes all the other monsters advance one cell towards the attacker; the effect resets at the start of the hit monster's turn. Hitting several "fresh" monsters with an area spell makes them advance that many cells.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.marche-des-goul.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.anerice-la-shushess.marche-des-goul.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Focus a single monster at a time.
mech.anerice-la-shushess.marche-des-goul.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Hitting it again before it plays no longer draws the others in.

mech.anerice-la-shushess.appetit-sanguin.title: "Appétit sanguinaire": +2 MP and +50% final damage (turn 2, then every 3 turns)
mech.anerice-la-shushess.appetit-sanguin.summary: From turn 2 (3-turn cooldown), Anerice gives 2 MP and 50% final damage for 1 turn to all monsters except herself; a character who is a ghoul is also buffed.

mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.title: Lunorbe invulnerability: hit from the blue glyph
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.summary: Torkélonia and her monsters are invulnerable thanks to the Lunorbe (invulnerable, cannot be moved) in the centre of the map. To lift a target's invulnerability, you must deal one damage line to it while standing on the rotating blue glyph: this first line removes the state without dealing damage, then you can hit the target as long as you stay on the glyph. When you leave the glyph or at the end of the turn, the target becomes invulnerable again: each player must repeat the process. Killing Torkélonia makes the Lunorbe disappear and makes the remaining monsters vulnerable.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.expectedStateChange: The target loses its invulnerability for that character as long as they stay on the glyph, until the end of their turn.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.vulnerabilityDuration: Until the character leaves the glyph or ends their turn.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.prerequisites.0: The character must be on the Lunorbe's blue glyph.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.notes.0: The character who kills Torkélonia is killed (one-shot), unless she dies during Nouvelle Lune or Pleine Lune; a summon can land the final blow to avoid the one-shot.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.notes.1: A monster passing over the blue glyph heals 10% of its max HP.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.label: Make a target vulnerable
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Blue glyph (in line or diagonal from the Lunorbe)
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit the target with a low-AP spell.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: This line removes invulnerability without dealing damage.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Then hit normally without leaving the glyph.
mech.torkelonia.lunorbe-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Leaving the glyph or ending your turn makes the target invulnerable again.

mech.torkelonia.cadran-lunaire.title: Lunar dial: glyph rotation and forcing
mech.torkelonia.cadran-lunaire.summary: The Lunorbe's blue glyph moves one position (clockwise) each turn, across 8 positions matching the lunar phases. A damage line on the Lunorbe forces it to the next position, but the monsters then stack the bonuses of several cycles (kept permanently if a monster dies at that moment). On each full rotation of the dial, the Lunorbe randomly removes 1 AP or 1 MP (permanent).
mech.torkelonia.cadran-lunaire.unknownAspects.0: Effect of a "misaligned" cycle (dial forced through a full rotation in less than one turn): the guide only mentions the glyph disappearing, with a question mark.

mech.torkelonia.cycle-lunaire.title: Lunar cycle: monster bonuses, permanent if a monster dies
mech.torkelonia.cycle-lunaire.summary: Each turn, the monsters gain a bonus based on the lunar phase (damage reflection, damage reduction, shields, MP, returned damage, AP, damage, final damage). Killing a monster during a phase gives that phase's bonus to all the other monsters permanently; the guide advises avoiding the Full Moon and the First Crescent in particular.

mech.misere.seuil-50.title: 50% HP threshold: Misère mounts her vulture (invulnerable 1 turn)
mech.misere.seuil-50.summary: At 50% of her vitality, Misère enters phase 2: she mounts her vulture and becomes invulnerable for a full turn (until the turn of the character who made her cross the threshold). She then gains 4 MP (10 in total) and the Unlockable state for the rest of the fight, along with new spells, including a long-range cooperation.
mech.misere.seuil-50.expectedStateChange: Misère invulnerable for 1 turn, then +4 MP and Unlockable until the end of the fight.
mech.misere.seuil-50.vulnerabilityDuration: Invulnerable for one turn, until the start of the turn of the character who crossed the threshold.
mech.misere.seuil-50.prerequisites.0: Misère's HP at 50% of her vitality.
mech.misere.seuil-50.unknownAspects.1: Conflicting cooldown for "Funérailles Célestes": 3 turns in the spell list, 2 turns in the 2.68 update note.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill all the monsters before starting on Misère, keeping her at a distance.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Prevents her from stealing power with Balance-Fléau.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.2.action: In phase 1, hide the team behind an obstacle and push Misère back every turn.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: She only has 4 MP without her mount.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Once in phase 2, kill her as fast as possible.
mech.misere.seuil-50.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: With 10 MP and her 8-range cooperation, she will reach you no matter what.

mech.misere.collecte.title: Stat theft from monsters in the Collecte state
mech.misere.collecte.summary: Monsters that steal characteristics from you enter the "Collecte" state. At the start of her turn, Misère steals those stats from each monster in Collecte that she has in line of sight (once per monster per turn) and removes the state from them; she keeps these bonuses as long as the monster in question is alive. She also gives 1 MP for 1 turn to monsters without Collecte or seen, and steals 5% resistances from them.
mech.misere.collecte.notes.0: In this dungeon, each attempt to remove AP, MP or range gives the monster 10 AP and MP Dodge (permanent according to the fight principle; 2 turns, stackable, according to the states section).

mech.misere.attraction-venale.title: "Attraction Vénale": pull at the start of her turn and on each hit taken
mech.misere.attraction-venale.summary: At the start of each of her turns and on each damage line she takes, Misère pulls all entities (allies and enemies alike) toward her: 1 cell above 75% HP, 2 cells from 75 to 50%, 3 cells from 49 to 25%, 4 cells below 25%.
mech.misere.attraction-venale.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.misere.attraction-venale.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place your characters behind obstacles (or carried by a Pandawa).
mech.misere.attraction-venale.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Avoid being pulled toward her when you hit her.

mech.misere.charognes.title: Charognes: heal monsters, shields for Misère
mech.misere.charognes.summary: Each entity that dies leaves a Charogne (320 HP). At the start of a monster's turn, Charognes within 4 range or less heal it for 1200 HP each (and it loses its 4 MP bonus); at the start of Misère's turn, she eliminates all Charognes, regardless of distance, and gains 880 shield points per Charogne.
mech.misere.charognes.unknownAspects.0: The tactical advice talks about killing the Charognes within 4 range of Misère, whereas the principle states she consumes them regardless of distance.

mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.title: 200% damage reflection, bypassed with the "Traître" state
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.summary: Servitude reflects 200% of the damage dealt to him (not poisons). To hit him without reflection, you need the "Traître" state: you get "Traître 1" by ending your turn on a white glyph placed by Servitude, then increase it (up to 5) by hitting your allies (1 per damage line). Each damage line on Servitude consumes one level. Immunity spells (Bastion, Barricade, Prohibition, Ataraxie) also counter the reflection.
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.notes.0: Servitude uses the "Traître" state against you via his "Trahison" spell: he pulls a Traître character and forces them to hit their nearest ally (all Traîtres in phase 2).
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.notes.1: Hitting an ally without already having "Traître 1" does not give the state.
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.label: Build up the Traître state
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.1.action: End your turn on a white glyph.
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Get "Traître 1" (the glyph gives no more than 1).
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit your allies with cheap, weak spells until you reach "Traître 5".
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Each line on an ally adds one level.
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit Servitude without exceeding your number of "Traître" levels.
mech.servitude.renvoi-traitre.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Each line consumes one level; beyond that, the reflection applies. Do not consume the last level.

mech.servitude.phases.title: Three phases: mount at 50%, rollback and 25% heal at 1 HP
mech.servitude.phases.summary: Phase 1 until 50% HP; at 50%, Servitude mounts his steed (phase 2), which strengthens his spells. On reaching 1 HP, he returns all entities to their starting positions and heals 25% of his HP (phase 3), which must then be defeated. The guide advises making him unhealable (and poisoning him) before bringing him to 1 HP.
mech.servitude.phases.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.servitude.phases.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before bringing him to 1 HP, apply the Unhealable state to him.
mech.servitude.phases.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He does not recover his 25% HP.
mech.servitude.phases.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Also apply a poison to him (e.g. Dofus Ébène).
mech.servitude.phases.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He then dies at the start of his turn.

mech.servitude.armecreantes.title: Armécréantes summoned every odd turn
mech.servitude.armecreantes.summary: Servitude summons an Armécréante 2 range from him every odd turn starting on turn 1 (6 alive maximum), going clockwise. Their number and stats do not depend on the number of characters (level 200 with 4, 212 with 8, with 20% less HP). They must be eliminated as soon as they are summoned, or at least hit every turn to remove their "Appel des renforts" state.
mech.servitude.armecreantes.notes.0: Armécréantes can send a character back to their start-of-turn position (rollback); Gravity, Rooted, Unmovable or a debuff prevents it.

mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.title: Remove "Kissiphrot Sipique" by healing in contact (Corruption dismounts for 3 turns)
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.summary: All monsters and Corruption carry "Kissiphrot Sipique": each damage line dealt to one of them applies a poison of about 1400 earth damage to you (stackable), which makes the fight impossible while the effect remains. You remove it by healing an ally or a summon in melee with the monster (monsters in contact are pushed back one cell); this is permanent for a monster. On Corruption, this "unlock" makes him dismount for only 3 turns: afterwards he remounts and reapplies the effect to himself and all his living allies.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.expectedStateChange: Corruption dismounts, loses "Kissiphrot Sipique" and changes spells; he no longer places his glyph.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.notes.0: If the Pistilangue (still under the effect) sacrifices an unlocked monster you are hitting, you still take the poison.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Remove the "Peau pourrissante" state from your damage dealers by healing them.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: It reduces their final damage by 90%.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.2.action: For each targeted monster, place an ally or a summon in contact with it and heal that ally or summon.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Permanently removes the effect from that monster.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill all the monsters before unlocking Corruption, keeping him at a distance without dealing damage to him.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Hitting him before the unlock poisons you.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Unlock Corruption (for example via a summon healed in contact with him), then kill him in under 3 turns.
mech.corruption.kissiphrot-sipique.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: After that, he remounts and reapplies the effect.

mech.corruption.maladies.title: Diseases, "Peau pourrissante" and the Corruption state
