mech.corruption.maladies.summary: All characters start with "Peau pourrissante": fire poison every turn, final damage reduced by 90% and, from turn 2, loss of 10% of current HP at the end of the turn; a heal (or life steal) removes it permanently. AP/MP/range removals, the glyph and Corruption's Bombe Bactériologique apply diseases: each different disease raises the Corruption state (reduced heals received, increased damage taken and erosion) up to the Germinal phase. It takes 3 heals on a character to remove one disease from them.
mech.corruption.maladies.notes.0: The guide advises keeping "Peau pourrissante" on characters who don't deal damage (tanks), since it prevents them from catching other diseases.

mech.corruption.bouillon-de-culture.title: "Bouillon de culture": purple glyph applying diseases (while mounted)
mech.corruption.bouillon-de-culture.summary: While on his mount, Corruption places a purple glyph of radius 3 around himself: walking in it deals about 300 damage (water + air) and a random disease. He no longer places this glyph once dismounted.

mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.title: 75/50/25% thresholds: invulnerable Lotus form for 5 turns and allied Roi Imagami
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.summary: Reine Amirukam has three HP thresholds (75%, 50% and 25%). At each threshold, she switches to "Lotus" form: rooted and invulnerable for 5 turns, during which she fully heals. The character closest to her then summons the Roi Imagami, controlled by that player, who fights on your side for those 5 turns; if he dies, the Reine returns to her normal form. After the third threshold, she has no more thresholds and simply has to be killed.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.expectedStateChange: The Reine becomes rooted and invulnerable for 5 turns; an allied Roi Imagami is summoned.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.vulnerabilityDuration: 5 turns per threshold (or until the Roi Imagami dies).
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.notes.0: In Lotus form, the Reine can be carried by a Pandawa; the guide also states that she can be given the unhealable state during this form.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place the character who plays first in initiative order as close as possible to the Reine when she reaches her threshold.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Roi is summoned by the closest character; the guide advises that this be the first in initiative.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Use the Roi Imagami to hit as many monsters as possible during the 5 turns (his damage spell needs no line of sight).
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.3.action: At the end of the 5 turns, the guide advises killing the Roi yourself with his "Extinction du Wukang" spell, then hitting the Reine before she plays again.
mech.reine-amirukam.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: She returns to 100% of her HP and you must reach the next threshold.

mech.reine-amirukam.glyphe-noir.title: Black glyph: eliminates paper monsters when the Lotus ends
mech.reine-amirukam.glyphe-noir.summary: On reaching a threshold, the Reine places a black glyph around herself (star of size 3, then 2, then square of size 1). Monsters from the paper zone standing in it when she returns to her normal form are eliminated. If a Pandawa has moved her out of her glyph, these monsters are not killed.

mech.reine-amirukam.brouillard-encre.title: "Brouillard d'Encre": glyphs on enemies on turn 1 then every 3 turns
mech.reine-amirukam.brouillard-encre.summary: On turn 1 and then every 3 turns, the Reine places glyphs under all enemy entities. On her next turn, these glyphs summon "Ruptures d'encre" which she kills immediately; characters and summons still on a glyph take 900 earth damage. The guide advises stepping out of the glyphs.
mech.reine-amirukam.brouillard-encre.turnConditions: Turn 1 then every 3 turns; effect on the Reine's next turn.

mech.reine-amirukam.lotus-monstres.title: Zone monsters: Lotus form at 10% HP and counterpart to kill
mech.reine-amirukam.lotus-monstres.summary: All monsters have a threshold at 10% of their HP: they switch to "Lotus" form (rooted, they skip their turn for 4 turns and heal 25% then 50%) and summon their Royaume de Papier counterpart. You must kill this counterpart before the monster's 4th turn to kill the monster permanently; otherwise the monster kills its counterpart itself and leaves the Lotus.
mech.reine-amirukam.lotus-monstres.unknownAspects.0: The text first describes monsters in Lotus as "Invulnerable", then states that since 3.6 "they" are no longer invulnerable: unclear whether the note refers to the monsters in Lotus or their summoned counterparts.

mech.reine-amirukam.vagues.title: Three waves of monsters
mech.reine-amirukam.vagues.summary: The fight takes place in one room with 3 waves; a new wave arrives earlier if the previous one is eliminated, and is invulnerable for 1 turn on arrival. All monsters have a 13,500 HP bonus.
mech.reine-amirukam.vagues.unknownAspects.0: Conflicting wave schedule: "every 4 turns", composition "in 4 turns" then "in 5 turns", and strategy "on turn 5 and turn 10".

mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.title: 75/50/25% thresholds: invulnerable Lotus form for 5 turns and allied Reine Amirukam
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.summary: Roi Imagami has three HP thresholds (75%, 50% and 25%). At each threshold, he switches to "Lotus" form: rooted and invulnerable for 5 turns, during which he fully heals. The character closest to him summons Reine Amirukam, controlled by that player, for those 5 turns; if she dies, the Roi returns to his normal form. After the last threshold, he simply has to be killed.
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.expectedStateChange: The Roi becomes rooted and invulnerable for 5 turns; an allied Reine Amirukam is summoned.
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.vulnerabilityDuration: 5 turns per threshold (or until Reine Amirukam dies).
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.notes.0: The guide names the Reine's damage spell sometimes "Inspiration du Wukin", sometimes "Expiration du Wukin".
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place the first character in initiative as close as possible to the Roi when he reaches his threshold.
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Reine is summoned by the closest character.
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Use the Reine to hit as many enemies as possible during the 5 turns.
mech.roi-imagami.seuils-lotus.sequences.0.steps.3.action: When the Lotus form ends, kill the Reine yourself with "Extinction du Wukin", then hit the Roi before he plays again.

mech.roi-imagami.glyphe-blanc.title: White glyph: eliminates ink monsters when the Lotus ends
mech.roi-imagami.glyphe-blanc.summary: On reaching a threshold, the Roi places a white glyph around himself (square of size 3, then 2, then 1). Monsters from the ink zone standing in it when he returns to his normal form are eliminated, unless he has been moved out of his glyph by a Pandawa.

mech.roi-imagami.papetuerie.title: "Papetuerie": damage to everyone except at the center of white glyphs
mech.roi-imagami.papetuerie.summary: From turn 2 and then every 3 turns, the Roi places size-1 cross-shaped white glyphs on all entities. On his next turn, he deals 700 neutral damage to all characters, except those standing on the center cell of a white glyph. He and his allies also gain shields when starting in a glyph.
mech.roi-imagami.papetuerie.sequences.0.label: Avoid Papetuerie
mech.roi-imagami.papetuerie.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before the Roi's next turn, stand on the center cell of a white glyph.
mech.roi-imagami.papetuerie.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Center cell of a white glyph

mech.roi-imagami.vagues.title: Three waves and monsters in Lotus form
mech.roi-imagami.vagues.summary: Fight in one room with 3 waves (the next one arrives earlier if the current wave is eliminated). All monsters have 13,500 bonus HP and, at 10% HP, switch to Lotus form, summoning their Royaume de Papier counterpart, which must be killed before their 4th turn.
mech.roi-imagami.vagues.unknownAspects.0: Inconsistent wave schedule on the page ("every 4 turns" but wave 3 "in 5 turns").

mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.title: Permanently invulnerable: only the Bras démoniaques can hurt him
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.summary: Kabahal is invulnerable and this state cannot be removed. Only the Bras démoniaques he summons can deal damage to him: he gets hit (1 time per turn) if he stands in a Bras's glyph, but above all a character can take control of all the Bras by ending their turn on one of the runes Kabahal places (from turn 2, then on even turns) and staying there until the boss's next turn; they can then use 2 spells per Bras.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.notes.0: The glyph of Kabahal's Bras is a size-3 circle; a character in this glyph when the Bras plays gets hit several times.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.notes.1: Control stays with the same character until another takes it, but on even turns the Bras's spells only have 3 range.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.label: Guide's method
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.1.action: On even turns, place a character on one of the runes placed by Kabahal and leave them there until the boss's next turn.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.1.position: On a Bras rune (or the special rune with a black sign)
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.2.action: On odd turns, use the Bras's spells (about 750 neutral, up to 5 range) against Kabahal, having placed him within range.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Bras hit in the neutral element.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit Kabahal with neutral spells even if they do 0, and avoid other elements and pushback.
mech.kabahal.invulnerabilite-bras.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Instabilité Chaotique: each line he takes removes 5% from him in that element and can give him neutral resistance.

mech.kabahal.chtyx.title: Five Bras summoned: Incarnation du Ch'Tyx wipes the team
mech.kabahal.chtyx.summary: The Bras only appear on 5 fixed cells. If Kabahal manages to summon all 5 Bras, on the next turn he teleports onto the special rune and summons the Incarnation du Ch'Tyx, which kills the whole team with "Pentadémonium". To prevent it: place a character (not a monster or a summon) on a rune that would complete the 5 positions, or kill a Bras before Kabahal plays again.
mech.kabahal.chtyx.notes.0: A monster or summon placed on a rune is killed and the Bras appears anyway.

mech.kabahal.invocations.title: Black runes: summoning of zone monsters (turns 6, 8…)
mech.kabahal.invocations.summary: From turn 5 and then every 2 turns, Kabahal places 2 symmetrical black runes that each summon a random zone monster (with 50% less HP) at the end of his next turn. These summons cannot be blocked; the number of runes increases at loot 5 to 8.
mech.kabahal.invocations.prerequisites.0: Runes from turn 5, summons from turn 6.

mech.kabahal.sacrifice.title: "Sacrifice Revigorant": monster killed on a Bras rune
mech.kabahal.sacrifice.summary: A monster standing on a Bras rune at the start of Kabahal's turn is killed by the Bras that appears; in return, Kabahal loses 10 turns of effects and gains 10 MP, 500 power and 550 shield for 2 turns. A rune placed on an existing Bras fully heals it and gives it 300 power ("Surcharge Démoniaque").

mech.eternel-conflit.diablotins.title: Invulnerable in melee and at range: kill the imps
mech.eternel-conflit.diablotins.summary: Éternel Conflit is invulnerable in melee and at range, in the Heavy state for the whole fight, and has a threshold at 4,000 HP. He summons two imps: killing the Bonraphin (invulnerable at range) removes his ranged invulnerability, killing the Brâklotin (invulnerable in melee) removes his melee invulnerability. A killed imp is re-summoned 2 turns later, and its death has a 25% chance of summoning the Cauchemar des Ravageurs for 1 turn.
mech.eternel-conflit.diablotins.notes.0: The 4,000 HP threshold cannot be crossed by this means alone: the "X" state is required.
mech.eternel-conflit.diablotins.unknownAspects.0: The page says in one place that an imp's death summons the Cauchemar (mechanics section) and elsewhere that there is a 25% chance: whether it is systematic is unclear.

mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.title: "X" state: vulnerable for 2 turns and 4,000 HP threshold removed
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.summary: The imps start with 10 states (Colère Bontarienne / Haine Brâkmarienne) and the boss with 0. Each time an imp uses its "Colonne", or the Bonraphin is hit at range or the Brâklotin in melee, the imp's state drops by 1 and the boss's rises by 1 (which strengthens his spells). When the boss has his 10 states of both types, at the start of his next turn he enters the "X" state: he kills the imps, becomes vulnerable for 2 turns with 9,000 shields and 400 dodge, permanently loses his 4,000 HP threshold and summons the Cauchemar des Ravageurs for 2 turns.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.expectedStateChange: Imps killed, boss vulnerable with 9,000 shields and 400 dodge; HP threshold removed.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.expectedResult: After 2 turns, he becomes invulnerable again, re-summons the imps and his states reset to 0.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.prerequisites.0: Éternel Conflit has reached 10 "Colère Bontarienne" states and 10 "Haine Brâkmarienne" states.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.notes.0: The more states the boss accumulates, the harder he hits: the guide advises avoiding the imps' attacks while monsters are still alive.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.unknownAspects.0: Bonus per Colère Bontarienne state given sometimes as +10, sometimes as +20 base damage.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.label: Guide's method
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the Bonraphin at range and the Brâklotin in melee to transfer their states to the boss (no limit per turn).
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Remove MP from the boss before the X state.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: In the X state he is immune to MP removal and removes the Pacifist state.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.steps.3.action: During the 2 turns, kill him; otherwise stall, then finish him by killing just one imp.
mech.eternel-conflit.etat-x.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The 4,000 HP threshold does not come back.

mech.eternel-conflit.modificateur.title: Cauchemar modifier: end your turn in line of sight of an enemy
mech.eternel-conflit.modificateur.summary: If a character ends their turn with no enemy in line of sight, the Cauchemar des Ravageurs (17,000 HP) appears 2 cells from them for one turn; the monster that summons it cannot drop below 1 HP while the Cauchemar is alive. When it disappears, all entities return to their starting position and the enemies are healed for 10% and gain 10% final damage. When an enemy is finished off, those who had it in line of sight become invisible for one turn. These rules no longer apply once only Éternel Conflit remains.

mech.eternel-conflit.massacre.title: "Massacre de l'Aurore Pourpre": leap with cooldown reduced per ally in contact
mech.eternel-conflit.massacre.summary: Éternel Conflit leaps up to 3 range without line of sight, debuffs himself of 4 turns, applies Heavy/Unmovable and hits water/fire with 20% erosion in a radius-2 circle. 4-turn cooldown, reduced by 1 per ally in contact with him at the start of his turn.
mech.eternel-conflit.massacre.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.eternel-conflit.massacre.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Prevent the boss from starting his turn in contact with his allies (imps, monsters).

mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.title: Invulnerable: push one fragile Krokille onto another
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.summary: Draguisla Bonita is permanently invulnerable. She summons 2 fragile Krokilles on her first turn, then one per turn (unmovable). To make her vulnerable, with at least 2 Krokilles alive: reduce a Krokille to 5 AP or less (it gains 2 MP per AP removal attempt); it loses its Unmovable state for 1 turn at the start of its next turn; you must then push it onto another Krokille, which kills both and makes Draguisla vulnerable (she gains 4 MP and 30% damage for 2 turns).
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.expectedStateChange: Both Krokilles die and Draguisla becomes vulnerable.
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.unknownAspects.0: Conflicting vulnerability duration: "2 full turns" then "one full turn"; the sentence also says "before she becomes vulnerable again" (probably "invulnerable").
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.sequences.0.label: Guide's method
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Keep 2 or 3 fragile Krokilles alive and eliminate the extras.
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Remove at least 3 AP from a Krokille to bring it down to 5 AP or less.
mech.draguisla-bonita.delock-krokilles.sequences.0.steps.3.action: On that Krokille's next turn (it becomes movable for 1 turn), push it onto another Krokille.

mech.draguisla-bonita.glyphe-krokilles.title: Blue glyph (poison per AP) and area AP removal from the Krokilles
mech.draguisla-bonita.glyphe-krokilles.summary: The Krokilles remove a lot of AP in a radius-2 circle, hence the advice not to stay grouped; Draguisla's blue glyph poisons (water) based on the AP used by those standing in it.
mech.draguisla-bonita.glyphe-krokilles.unknownAspects.0: Poison and AP removal values not given.

mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.title: Invulnerable: hit him in melee every turn
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.summary: The Glourséleste is invulnerable. Hitting him in melee disables his invulnerability, but only for the turn of the character who hits: each character must repeat a hit in contact on each of their turns, and this first hit deals no damage (the guide recommends a cheap spell or a multi-line weapon). This hit pushes entities in line within 4 range of him back 4 cells.
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.vulnerabilityDuration: The turn of the character who hit in contact.
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.notes.0: The guide states that any pushback damage kills you (one-shot).
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.unknownAspects.0: Undated page written in an old style: mechanic not confirmed for Dofus 3.
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.sequences.0.label: Guide's method
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before each hit, make sure you have 4 free cells behind you in line with the Glourséleste.
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Any pushback damage against an obstacle is lethal.
mech.glourseleste.invulnerabilite-cac.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit in contact with a small spell (no damage), then follow up with real damage in the same turn.

mech.glourseleste.resurrection.title: MP/range removal or displacement: companions resurrected
mech.glourseleste.resurrection.summary: Do not remove MP or range from the Glourséleste, and do not move him: otherwise he resurrects several companions already killed (no consequence if no monster has died yet). Watch out for the Glouragan, which pulls whatever is in line with it when hit and can thus move the boss. The Glourséleste hits harder as he loses HP (10% of his missing HP in melee).
mech.glourseleste.resurrection.unknownAspects.0: Number of resurrected companions not specified; the guide names the "Résuglours" state only in the achievements section.

mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerable on her islet while the monsters live; threshold at 50%
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.summary: Belladone starts alone on an islet, immobile and invulnerable, and only buffs her allies. Once all the monsters are eliminated, she teleports onto the closest character and only loses her invulnerability at the end of that turn. She then has a threshold at 50% of her HP: once reached, she returns to the islet, becomes invulnerable again, the characters return to their starting positions and the monsters are re-summoned. You must kill the monsters a second time, then take off her last 50%.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: Belladone leaves the islet, loses her Ensorcellement states, changes spells and becomes vulnerable at the end of her turn.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.notes.0: After the threshold, each re-summoned monster loses 10% resistances and gains 10% final damage at the start of each turn.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.notes.1: The empty islet keeps a permanent black glyph that kills any character who enters it.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: Belladone's exact HP outside loot 4 to 8 not detailed beyond the guide's example.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Sequence described by the guide
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Eliminate all the monsters (eroding them beforehand can help; they come back with the same max HP).
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Wait for the end of the turn in which Belladone joins the field, then hit her down to 50% of her HP.
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Eliminate the re-summoned monsters a second time (invulnerable for 1 full turn).
mech.belladone.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: When she returns to the field (invulnerable until the end of her turn), take off the remaining 50%.

mech.belladone.ensorcellement.title: "Ensorcellement" states: islet spells strengthened per monster killed
mech.belladone.ensorcellement.summary: Each monster eliminated raises Belladone's Ensorcellement state (up to III), which strengthens her support spells on the islet (Enchantement fatal, Charme maléfique, Ensorcellement explosif). The state disappears when she joins the field.
mech.belladone.ensorcellement.notes.0: At loot 5 or higher, the effect stays capped at level III.

mech.belladone.glyphe-condamnation.title: "Glyphe de condamnation": lethal star glyph
mech.belladone.glyphe-condamnation.summary: From the islet, Belladone places an infinite-size black star glyph around the targeted character (not on their cell); it lasts 1 turn and kills characters who start their turn in it. The spell also applies a neutral poison per AP used.
mech.belladone.glyphe-condamnation.notes.0: Starting your turn in the glyph = instant death.

mech.belladone.detection-protecteurs.title: "Détection des Protecteurs" zone: monster teleportation
mech.belladone.detection-protecteurs.summary: A monster that starts its turn with a character in line of sight at more than 4 range enters the "Férocité des Protecteurs" state: it can teleport into contact with that character, deal damage to them and put them in Gravity and "Détecté", while gaining 3 AP and 30% final damage. Staying out of line of sight or within 4 range avoids it.
mech.belladone.detection-protecteurs.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.belladone.detection-protecteurs.sequences.0.steps.1.action: End your turn out of the monsters' line of sight, or within 4 range of them.

mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.title: Invulnerability removed by the "Âmes Hurlantes" state (within 2 range)
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.summary: Cire Momore is invulnerable and unmovable. His invulnerability is only removed for the character who is playing: by moving within 2 range of him, that character enters the "Âmes Hurlantes" state and can hit him as long as they stay in the zone. They lose 1 MP on entering (regained on leaving), enter Gravity before the threshold or Unmovable after it, and cannot become Unlockable.
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.prerequisites.0: The character who is playing is within 2 range of Cire Momore.
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.notes.0: A character left in the zone outside their turn does not make Cire Momore vulnerable for the others.
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.sequences.0.label: Hit Cire Momore
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Enter the 2-range zone around Cire Momore during your turn and hit him.
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Leave the zone before the end of your turn.
mech.cire-momore.ames-hurlantes.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: At the start of his turn, he kills any character within 2 range (Âmespiration).

mech.cire-momore.amespiration.title: "Âmespiration": instant death within 2 range at the start of his turn
mech.cire-momore.amespiration.summary: At the start of his turn, Cire Momore instantly kills all entities in a radius-2 circle around him; each kill boosts his damage (10% per character, 3% per summon, permanent) and heals him for 2% of his max HP.
mech.cire-momore.amespiration.notes.0: Leaving a character or summon within 2 range at the end of the turn = one-shot and a boost for the boss.

mech.cire-momore.tour-25.title: Time limit: team one-shot on turn 25
mech.cire-momore.tour-25.summary: From the start of the fight, each character receives the effect "Kills the target (in 24 turns)": if Cire Momore is not defeated before the start of turn 25, the whole team is killed.
mech.cire-momore.tour-25.turnConditions: Defeat at the start of turn 25.

mech.cire-momore.seuil-80.title: 80% HP threshold: "Métal Hurlant" and strengthened spells
mech.cire-momore.seuil-80.summary: At 80% of his HP, Cire Momore immediately casts "Métal Hurlant" (then every 4 turns, 3-turn effect): heal per enemy out of his line of sight, shield, increased resistances and Briselâme range. Fatalité then removes 8 MP and Triste Cire hits in an area with range removal, Gravity and -50% heals received.
mech.cire-momore.seuil-80.notes.0: He has 1064 MP dodge (immune to MP removal) and 2 MP; his passives reduce his lock when hit in melee and pull an attacker located more than 2 range away by 2 cells.

mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.title: Guerre vulnerable only when she is alone
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.summary: In the Tempête, Guerre stays invulnerable as long as she is not alone on the field: she must be killed last. She summons a weapon that hits in an area and that she can use at each 20% HP step removed.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.prerequisites.0: Guerre is the only enemy entity left.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.notes.0: The page refers to the Trône de sang article for details of her spells.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: Detailed workings of the weapon not described on this page.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Put a tank character first in initiative: they summon the Feu Primordial, so keep them alive.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The first in initiative summons the Feu Primordial in the center; if this character dies, the fight is automatically lost.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Save Guerre for last: kill Corruption first, then Servitude, then Misère.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Guerre is invulnerable as long as she is not alone on the field; recommended order Corruption > Servitude > Misère > Guerre.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Meanwhile, lock Guerre with a tank character.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The guide advises locking her with a tank (for example a Feca) so she doesn't bother you too much.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Once alone, Guerre becomes vulnerable: choose to kill her weapons or ignore them and hit her at range.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: She becomes vulnerable by mounting her steed at the start of her turn; for every 20% HP removed, she summons a weapon that hits in an area.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If you kill the weapons: trigger the threshold right after Guerre's turn, then kill the weapon before she plays again.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: If a weapon is alive on her turn, Guerre boosts herself; if you kill the weapon after she has played with it, Guerre gains resistances and MP and heals herself.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If you ignore the weapons: hit Guerre at range, as far as possible from her and her weapons.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: This way you take as little damage as possible.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Stay more than 3 cells from Guerre to avoid the Brave state.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: 1 turn out of 3, she puts a character in the Brave state (2 turns); the others become Pacifist for 1 turn after a damage line. The spell has a maximum range of 3.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Hardi achievement: never let Guerre play with a weapon alive; hit up to the threshold, trigger the threshold after her turn, kill the weapon, and repeat at each threshold.
mech.guerre-tempete.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Block the Feu Primordial's line of sight with a summon to prevent it from triggering a threshold at the wrong time.

mech.guerre-tempete.feu-primordial.title: Allied Feu Primordial (fight rule)
mech.guerre-tempete.feu-primordial.summary: The first character in initiative summons the Feu Primordial in the center. It gives everyone big bonuses (500 power, 2 AP, 2 MP, resistances, +50% HP; more for the summoner), hits enemies in line of sight and is invulnerable. If its summoner dies, the fight is lost.
mech.guerre-tempete.feu-primordial.notes.0: Death of the Feu Primordial's summoner = immediate defeat.
mech.guerre-tempete.feu-primordial.notes.1: If an enemy hits the Feu while the summoner is in line of sight, the summoner loses their vitality bonus for the rest of the fight.
mech.guerre-tempete.feu-primordial.unknownAspects.0: Rule common to the whole fight, attached here to Guerre for lack of a dedicated entity.

mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.title: Misère: pull and mounting her steed at the 50% threshold
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.summary: Misère pulls all entities toward her at the start of each of her turns and when she takes damage (1 to 4 cells, stronger as her HP drops). At 50% HP she mounts her steed and becomes invulnerable for 1 turn; she must be eliminated before she plays again.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.vulnerabilityDuration: Invulnerable for 1 turn after mounting her steed.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.notes.0: The guide recommends a Feca playing after her to use Trêve during that turn.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.notes.1: Her Dahkma spell makes the target invulnerable and sends it back to its start-of-turn cell with -100 AP/MP; an ally can remove it with a damage spell on the target.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: She pulls all entities toward her at the start of her turn and when she takes damage (1 to 4 cells; the more HP she has, the less she pulls), including on the turn of the Feu Primordial, which hits her if it sees her.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep Misère at a distance as long as Corruption and Servitude are not dead.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: In the first phase she is not dangerous; avoid letting her hit you, especially with Dahkma.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If an ally is hit by Dahkma, cast a damage spell on them to remove the effect.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Dahkma makes the target invulnerable, sends it back to its start-of-turn cell and removes 100 AP and MP from it for 1 turn.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.4.action: When it's her turn to be focused: hit her at range, pushing her back every turn.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: This way she deals as little damage to you as possible.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Make her cross her threshold (50% HP) with a character who plays among the first in initiative.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: She mounts her steed and becomes invulnerable for 1 turn; she becomes vulnerable again on that same character's turn, which leaves a full turn to finish her.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.6.action: During her invulnerable turn, boost yourselves as much as possible (option: Feca "Trêve" or Enutrof "Corruption" to cancel her next turn).
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: She must be eliminated before she plays again.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Kill her in one go; otherwise, heal and protect yourselves.
mech.misere-tempete.seuil-monture.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: If you can't finish her in 1 turn, protect yourselves so she can't wipe you out.

mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.title: Servitude: hit only in the "Traître" state
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.summary: Servitude reflects 200% of the damage taken. To deal damage to him, you must be in the Traître state, obtained by ending your turn in the white glyph he places every two turns. He summons an Armécréante on the first turn and then every two turns (6 maximum).
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.prerequisites.0: The attacker is in the Traître state (end of turn in the white glyph).
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.notes.0: At his 1 HP threshold, he rolls back and heals 25%: the guide advises having made him Unhealable beforehand.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.notes.1: The Feu Primordial can take the Traître state if the glyph is under it, which is useless.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill Corruption first, then focus Servitude second.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Recommended order: Corruption > Servitude > Misère > Guerre.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Don't hit Servitude unprotected: get the "Traître" state by ending your turn in a white glyph.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Servitude reflects 200% of the damage taken; he places a white glyph every two turns (turns 2, 4, 6…), which remains until someone has ended their turn in it.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.3.action: End your turn on the glyphs with your highest-damage characters, as soon as possible.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: If the glyph is under the Feu Primordial, it takes the Traître state instead, which is useless.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Raise the Traître state (up to 5) by hitting your allies.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: +1 increment per damage line on an ally.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Hit Servitude: 1 damage line per state, but never consume the last state.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Otherwise you have to go back and get it from a glyph; keep 1 state and re-increment on your allies.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.6.action: With a Feca: protect the big hitters (Barricade, Bastion, Ataraxie) so they can hit without the Traître state.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The guide states that these spells let you hit Servitude without taking damage.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Place Servitude in the Feu Primordial's line of sight every turn.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The Feu Primordial adds 600 damage per turn to him.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Keep eliminating the Armécréantes as they come.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Servitude summons one on the first turn and then every two turns (6 alive maximum).
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Before bringing him to 1 HP, apply the Unhealable state to him (Pandawa's Prohibition, Masqueraider's Fougue), then finish him.
mech.servitude-tempete.traitre.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: At 1 HP, he sends everyone back to their starting positions and heals 25% of his HP.

mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.title: Corruption: "Kissiphrot Sipique" and "Peau Pourrissante" states
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.summary: Corruption puts the Kissiphrot Sipique state on his allies: each damage line dealt to a carrier poisons you (1300 earth at the end of the turn). You remove it by healing an entity in contact with the targeted enemy; if Corruption loses it, all his allies lose it and he dismounts. Characters start with "Peau Pourrissante" (-90% damage dealt, removed by a heal).
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.notes.0: Disease mechanic present; a disease is removed by healing the affected character 3 times.
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Heal each character who needs to deal damage once to remove "Peau Pourrissante".
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Heal an entity in contact with Corruption to remove Kissiphrot Sipique from him (and from all his allies).
mech.corruption-tempete.kissiphrot.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill him first (recommended order: Corruption > Servitude > Misère > Guerre) and put him in Gravity when he is on foot.

mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerable while his monsters live; vulnerable for 2 turns on the ground
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.summary: Gargandyas is invulnerable. In phase 1 he summons 3 monsters; when the last one dies, he falls to the ground and becomes vulnerable (and takes 100% more damage) for 2 full turns without playing. Reaching his threshold (50,000 HP in phase 1, 1,000 HP in phase 2) gets him up immediately and moves on to the next phase. Phase 2: 4 monsters, same principle. In phase 3 he becomes invulnerable again for the rest of the fight.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: Gargandyas falls to the ground, no longer plays and takes 100% extra damage.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.vulnerabilityDuration: 2 full turns (until the turn of the character who finished off the last monster).
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.prerequisites.0: All summoned monsters of the phase eliminated.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.notes.0: Being in the red glyph's zone when he falls = one-shot.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.notes.1: If the threshold is not reached, he wakes up on his own and casts Éboulement: -3 turns of effects, 1,000 earth and 1,000 neutral to everyone.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.notes.2: From phase 2, the monsters appear invulnerable until the end of their first turn.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Come with 4 characters, with MP removal and healing.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The fight allows 4 maximum and going with fewer is not recommended; MP removal handles the monsters at range, healing helps you last over time.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: As soon as a character receives the Bénidyas state, gather the whole team in the blue glyph around them before Gargandyas's next turn.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Rituel Primordial: all characters outside the glyph are one-shot (phases 1 to 3). Zone: circle 3 in phase 1, square 1 in phase 2, cross 1 in phase 3.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Stand on the sides of the map, avoiding the 3 lines on the side where the next Rafale Bestiale lands.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: On the sides, paw strikes and Gargameha don't hit. Rafale Bestiale (from turn 2, then every 2 turns, left then right) deals 500 air, pushes 7 cells toward the middle and removes 20% resistances for 3 turns.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Never end your turn in a red paw-strike glyph.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Impact Sauvagial: 2000 fire in the zone at the moment of the strike, 1500 if you cross the glyph, one-shot if you end your turn in it.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Gargandyas is invulnerable: eliminate his monsters (3 in phase 1, 4 in phase 2) while keeping them at a distance.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: When the last monster dies, he falls to the ground and loses his invulnerable state. From phase 2, the monsters that appear are invulnerable for 1 turn.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Don't be in the red glyph where he falls; finish off the last monster with your placer character.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Being in the zone when he falls = one-shot. The next phase's monsters appear near you.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.action: During the 2 turns on the ground, hit Gargandyas on the 6 cells around him down to his threshold (50,000 HP in phase 1, 1,000 HP in phase 2).
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: He takes 100% more damage. If he wakes up without the threshold reached, he removes 3 turns of effects and deals 1,000 earth + 1,000 neutral to everyone.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Phase 3: eliminate the 5 monsters while handling his 6-cell pushes/pulls, then hit the Corruption du graogarm before the end of its 3rd turn.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Gargandyas can no longer be hit. The Corruption has 100,000 HP and takes 4 times more damage; otherwise it deals neutral damage to everyone. To flee, do so before it disappears.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Phase 4: Gargandyas is an ally; quickly focus the Déchireuse or the Supervizoeuf, or keep the Vénérable Endormi at a distance and kill the monsters first.
mech.gargandyas.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: The fight ends when the boss and its 5 monsters are eliminated; place the monsters in the areas of Gargandyas's spells.

mech.gargandyas.phases-3-4.title: Phases 3 and 4: Corruption du Graogarm, then Gargandyas as an ally
mech.gargandyas.phases-3-4.summary: Phase 3: 5 monsters to kill, then a Corruption du Graogarm (100,000 HP, damage taken x4, threshold at 1 HP) appears and disappears after its third turn; if not destroyed, it hits everyone and poisons. Phase 4: a dimension boss (depending on the season) and 5 monsters appear; Gargandyas fights on your side. The fight ends when they are all eliminated.
mech.gargandyas.phases-3-4.notes.0: 4 characters maximum; 5 victories per weekend; seasonal offering increases with each attempt.

mech.gargandyas.rafale-bestiale.title: "Rafale Bestiale": claw alternating left/right every 2 turns
mech.gargandyas.rafale-bestiale.summary: From turn 2 and then every 2 turns, Gargandyas claws the far left then the far right of the field alternately: 500 air, 7-cell push toward the center (400 pushback damage) and -20% resistances for 3 turns. The rooted/unmovable/unshakable states do not prevent the push. The rhythm shifts when he is on the ground.
mech.gargandyas.rafale-bestiale.turnConditions: Turn 2 left, turn 4 right, turn 6 left… (shifted if he is on the ground).

mech.venerable-endormi.monture.title: Invulnerable while asleep; permanently vulnerable once his Mount is killed
mech.venerable-endormi.monture.summary: The Vénérable starts asleep: he doesn't play, heals 5% per turn and is invulnerable. He wakes up (vulnerable for 2 turns) if a monster enters the "Alerté" state within 3 range of him, then falls back asleep. To lift the invulnerability permanently, you must kill the Monture du Vénérable (summoned on turn 1, 10 MP, runs away, +2% final damage to monsters per turn, max 20%).
mech.venerable-endormi.monture.expectedStateChange: The Vénérable wakes up and stays vulnerable until the end of the fight.
mech.venerable-endormi.monture.prerequisites.0: The Monture du Vénérable is eliminated.
mech.venerable-endormi.monture.notes.0: He cannot be carried by a Pandawa, even when awake.
mech.venerable-endormi.monture.notes.1: He does not become Alerté by taking damage; only a monster becoming Alerté within 3 range (including on its death or that of a baby) wakes him up.

mech.venerable-endormi.seuil-50.title: 50% threshold: "Gare au Gorille"
mech.venerable-endormi.seuil-50.summary: At 50% of his HP (16,000), the Vénérable triggers "Gare au Gorille" until the end of the fight: +20% final damage, +4 range, +100 pushback damage, +60 AP and MP removal.

mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.title: Zone: "Apathique" / "Alerté" states of the Zarbivores
mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.summary: The monsters start Apathique (-80% MP, no spells, heal every turn). Since 3.7 and the 13/10/2026 maintenance, they become Alerté at the start of global turn 3 even without damage, for 2 turns, then go back to Apathique for 2 turns, and so on. Hitting a monster also alerts the monsters within 3 range.
mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.notes.0: Dimension dungeon: 5 waves (turns 1, 6, 11, 16, 21), monsters invulnerable until the end of their first turn.
mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.sequences.0.label: Guide's advice
mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Move the monsters away from the Vénérable without hitting them (damage-free displacement).
mech.venerable-endormi.apathique-alerte.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Never hit or kill a monster (or its baby) within 3 range of the Vénérable.

mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerability removed via the Autel de la Chasse and the Réaction Saisonnière
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.summary: The Déchireuse is invulnerable. The Autel de la Chasse (invulnerable) copies, at the end of its turn, the monsters' spells and Réactions Saisonnières onto the entity closest to it. Depending on the season, you must trigger (5 damage lines) a specific monster's reaction: Naissances = Voracle (invisibility copied onto the Déchireuse, then hit her), Chasse = Domptueuse (swap places with the Déchireuse placed 4 range from the Autel's target), Repos = Ébourifauve (reflection copied onto a character she teleports onto). She then becomes vulnerable for the rest of the fight.
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: The Déchireuse loses her invulnerability for the rest of the fight.
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.notes.0: The waves always arrive on turns 1, 6, 11, 16 and 21 in this dungeon.
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Unlock by season
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the season's monster 5 times to trigger its Réaction Saisonnière.
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: In the same turn, before the Autel's turn, place the required entity as close as possible to the Autel (Déchireuse, Domptueuse/character, or character in line of sight of the Déchireuse depending on the season).
mech.dechireuse.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Let the Autel replay the effect; complete the unlock (hit her in Naissances).

mech.dechireuse.espece-menacee.title: Teleportation and the "Espèce menacée" state (one-shot on the second mark)
mech.dechireuse.espece-menacee.summary: At the start of her turn, the Déchireuse teleports onto the closest character in line of sight (not summons), deals 500 fire to them and applies "Espèce menacée" for the whole fight. If the target already has this state, they are killed, and the Déchireuse can teleport again. Gravity does not prevent it.
mech.dechireuse.espece-menacee.notes.0: A character already marked and in line of sight at the start of her turn risks being one-shot.

mech.dechireuse.barbarisme.title: 1 HP threshold: "Barbarisme" state (phase 2) and Unerodable
mech.dechireuse.barbarisme.summary: At 1 HP, the Déchireuse enters the "Barbarisme" state, recovers all her HP and changes spells. She is Unerodable and cannot be made Unhealable to prevent this heal.
mech.dechireuse.barbarisme.unknownAspects.0: The page notes that heal reductions have worked since a 12 August maintenance, probably due to a bug: current behavior uncertain.

mech.dechireuse.matriarche.title: "Matriarche" effect: MP per aligned monster
mech.dechireuse.matriarche.summary: At the start of each turn, the Déchireuse gains 1 MP (permanent) per allied monster in line with her.

mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.title: Vulnerable for 1 turn after damage from a summon
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.summary: According to the guide (flagged as needing review), the Kolosso becomes vulnerable for 1 turn as soon as a summon deals damage to him.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.prerequisites.0: An allied summon deals damage to the Kolosso.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.notes.0: The page displays a banner stating that it needs review.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.unknownAspects.0: Invulnerability mechanic not confirmed by a recent version of the guide.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Don't count on your heals during this fight.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: From the start, all your allies have a -10,000 heals state that cannot be debuffed (only summons such as the Lapino can heal).
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.2.action: To heal yourself, hit the monsters during Professeur Xa's spell while staying within 4 range of the monster being hit.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: 1 turn out of 2, the Xa gives his allies a spell: each hit a monster takes gives it 100 damage, but heals your allies within 4 range of the hit monster for 100 HP.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Leave no one in melee with the Kolosso (no ally, summon or monster).
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Razepoutine is only cast if an entity is in contact with him: very high earth damage in a triangle, increasingly strong when he is low on HP. He can pull his enemies into contact to cast it.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Make the Kolosso vulnerable by dealing damage to him with a summon.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: He then becomes vulnerable for 1 turn.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.5.action: During that turn, the whole team hits the Kolosso.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Warning: under "Baikal", he gains 10% final damage for each damage taken in melee.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Repeat: hit him again with a summon every turn to make him vulnerable again.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Be aware that killing Professeur Xa strengthens the Kolosso.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: He gains 1 MP, 200 power and the Xalactite spell (350 water life steal, -30% dodge, up to 8 range). Alone on the field, he can apply the unhealable state in a line up to 3 range.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "Alliés passés au futur" achievement: have no ally or summon within 5 range of a monster hit during Kirbili, and focus Professeur Xa early.
mech.kolosso.invulnerabilite-invocation.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Kirbili is cast on turn 1 then every 2 turns; life steal does not count as healing.

mech.kolosso.soins-interdits.title: Healing impossible (-10,000 heals); only Professeur Xa's spell heals
mech.kolosso.soins-interdits.summary: From the start of the fight, all allies receive a non-debuffable -10,000 heals state: you cannot heal yourself (except summons such as Lapino). Every other turn, Professeur Xa gives his allies an effect that heals the player's allies within 4 range of a hit monster for 100 HP.
mech.kolosso.soins-interdits.notes.0: The achievements section mentions a size-5 healing area (Kirbili spell), versus 4 range in the general description.
mech.kolosso.soins-interdits.unknownAspects.0: Exact values of Professeur Xa's healing area (4 or 5 range depending on the passage).

mech.kolosso.razepoutine.title: "Razepoutine": triangle strike if an entity is in contact with him
mech.kolosso.razepoutine.summary: The Kolosso, in the Heavy state, only attacks with Razepoutine, cast only if an entity (ally or enemy, summons included) is in contact with him: high earth damage in a triangle in his direction, stronger as his HP drops. He can pull to take advantage of it.
mech.kolosso.razepoutine.notes.0: When Professeur Xa dies, the Kolosso gains 1 MP, 200 power and the Xalactite spell (water life steal at 8 range).

mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.title: Vulnerable for 1 turn by killing the Zombie under "Gelée blanche" in contact with him
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.summary: Grolloum is invulnerable for the whole fight. Every 2 turns he resurrects the last dead monster in the Zombie state, then casts "Gelée blanche" on it, which gives the "Instant" effect. Finishing off this Zombie while it is in contact with Grolloum makes him vulnerable until the start of the next turn of the character who finished it off.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.vulnerabilityDuration: Until the start of the next turn of the character who made him vulnerable.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.prerequisites.0: A monster resurrected as a Zombie carries the "Instant" effect (Gelée blanche) and is in contact with Grolloum.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.notes.0: Vulnerable during his turn, he gains "Frimas", which hits based on his missing HP; once invulnerable again, "Banquise" heals him for 1500 HP per character hit.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Eliminate the monsters, finishing with the one you want resurrected (the guide recommends the Gobus).
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place the Zombie in contact with Grolloum and reduce its HP as much as possible.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Wait for Grolloum to cast "Gelée blanche" on the Zombie.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Finish off the Zombie with as few AP as possible, then hit Grolloum.
mech.grolloum.zombi-instant.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Ideally by the character who plays right after Grolloum.

mech.grolloum.retrait-pm.title: +8000 resistances for 1 turn if he suffers an MP removal attempt
mech.grolloum.retrait-pm.summary: Any MP removal attempt on Grolloum gives him 8000 resistances in every element for 1 turn, which prevents hitting him even when vulnerable. The guide suggests taking the opportunity to erode him without removing HP.
mech.grolloum.retrait-pm.notes.0: Removing MP on the turn before the unlock makes the vulnerability window useless.

mech.grolloum.gobus.title: Gobus: explodes and one-shots in line at the end of its 2nd turn
mech.grolloum.gobus.summary: The Gobus (summoned by the Perkü) has 0 MP; at the end of its second turn, it one-shots all characters in line with it and dies. It does not explode as long as no enemy is in line at the start of its turn. Never stay in line with it.

mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.title: Vulnerable while the Silhouette is in the Globilum's glyph and Ombre is outside
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.summary: Ombre starts invulnerable. He becomes vulnerable as long as two conditions are met: the Silhouette is in the Globilum's white glyph (radius-3 circle), and Ombre himself is not in it. As soon as either condition stops being met, he loses his vulnerability.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.prerequisites.0: Silhouette in the Globilum's white glyph.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.prerequisites.1: Ombre outside the Globilum's white glyph.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.notes.0: "Encrage" effect: Ombre and the Silhouette become unmovable for 1 turn after being moved, so only one displacement each per turn.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.notes.1: The Globilum gains 1 MP per turn and moves: take this into account when placing the Silhouette.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Eliminate the monsters first (Sombléro, then Caznoar, then Noctulule).
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep Ombre away from the Globilum by removing his MP.
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Bring the Silhouette into the glyph (it flees after hitting; you can limit its MP).
mech.ombre.globilum-silhouette.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Hit Ombre; reposition the Silhouette if it leaves the glyph.

mech.ombre.eclairage.title: "Éclairage": damage outside the Globilum's radius-6 circle
mech.ombre.eclairage.summary: At the start of each turn, Ombre casts "Éclairage" via the Globilum (invulnerable and unmovable): 350 neutral damage to enemies located in an inverted radius-6 circle around the Globilum, and +50 damage to monsters in that same zone.
mech.ombre.eclairage.notes.0: Enemies in the Globilum's white glyph gain 20% final damage.

mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.title: -20% resistances per summon alive at the end of his turn
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.summary: Comte Razof has more than 100% resistances everywhere (100% neutral to 135% water). For each non-static summon alive at the end of his turn, he loses 20% resistances for 1 turn; the Minikrone counts. So you must summon and protect your summons out of his line of sight.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.prerequisites.0: Allied non-static summons alive at the end of Comte Razof's turn.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.notes.0: The penalty is calculated at the end of his turn: a summon killed in the meantime does not give him back his resistances immediately.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before the dungeon: learn the Chafer and Arakne summoning spells (or bring a summoner class).
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Non-static summons are needed to remove the Comte's resistances (100 to 135% depending on the element).
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.action: During placement, keep the character who will go into contact (locker) away from the Comte: the Minikrone appears in contact with the character closest to Razof.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Minikrone follows its summoner; it's better for it to be summoned by a character who won't go into melee.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Never let the Comte get into contact with the Minikrone.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: It is invulnerable, but Trophée de Chasse (melee, from turn 2) one-shots it: your characters then lose 20% resistances and 2 AP for the whole fight.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Block the Comte with a tank character with about 150 lock, placed between him and your other characters.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.position: Locker in contact with the Comte, allies out of his line of sight
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Pelliste (up to 15 range) removes 6 MP and applies Gravity and Weakened. Reposition the locker if they are pulled by the Viandargh or pushed by the Crâmbo.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Kill the Viandargh first, then the other monsters (the Nemroz can be left for last).
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Viandargh is one of the most dangerous (power penalty, pull). Avoid the Crâmbo's line of sight while it is at 100% HP (Premier Sang).
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Summon as many summons as possible, spread out, far from the Comte and out of his line of sight.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Each non-static summon alive at the end of the Comte's turn removes 20% of his resistances for 1 turn (Minikrone included). Archi-Pelle hits in a radius-2 circle up to 6 range.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.7.action: After his turn ends, hit the Comte while he has lost his resistances.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The penalty is calculated at the end of his turn and lasts until his next turn.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Keep repositioning and protecting the summons every turn until he dies.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: If summons die, the next penalty will be smaller (e.g. 3 summons = -60%).
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.9.action: "Premier" achievement: summon and boost from turn 1 to kill the Comte on turn 2 or 3.
mech.comte-razof.invocations-resistances.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: The Comte must be finished off first; the monsters are dangerous if the fight drags on.

mech.comte-razof.minikrone.title: Minikrone: invulnerable, one-shot only by "Trophée de Chasse"
mech.comte-razof.minikrone.summary: An invulnerable Minikrone is summoned on the players' side in contact with the character closest to Razof. Only Razof can kill it, in melee, from his turn 2. If it dies, all characters lose 20% resistances and 2 AP for the rest of the fight. It heals and protects an ally in contact with it, and applies penalties if it starts in contact with an enemy or ends on its black glyph.
mech.comte-razof.minikrone.notes.0: Letting Razof reach melee with the Minikrone: it is killed and the team is penalized for the whole fight.
mech.comte-razof.minikrone.notes.1: Staying on your start-of-turn cell can let the Minikrone end on its black glyph (-2 MP and 50% erosion to everyone).

mech.comte-razof.etat-piege.title: "Piégé" state via the Nemroz's invisible trap
mech.comte-razof.etat-piege.summary: In this area, the Piégé state empowers many spells (including Archi-Pelle and Pelliste de Razof). It can only be obtained by triggering the Nemroz's invisible "Éblouissant" trap, which also applies -6 AP and -9 range in a radius of 2.

mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.pas-d-invulne.title: No invulnerability; +20% resistances on each push
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.pas-d-invulne.summary: The guide describes no invulnerability. The "Clochecuivre" effect makes her Lourd and gives her 20% resistances for 2 turns (stackable, cannot be debuffed) every time she is pushed: avoid pushing her when you focus her.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.pas-d-invulne.unknownAspects.0: The absence of invulnerability is inferred: the page does not state it explicitly.

mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.title: "Clochecuivre" state: position swap and -100 MP
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.summary: The first character to take damage during the turn (from any source) gets the Clochecuivre state; at the start of her turn, Barbéryl swaps places with them and removes 100 MP from them for 1 turn. Remove it by dealing melee damage to Barbéryl (any ally or summon), or counter it with Pesanteur, Enraciné, Indéplaçable or by carrying the character.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.notes.0: A summon is only eligible if it was already on the battlefield during Barbéryl's previous turn.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Choose your strategy: kill Barbéryl first (the easiest) or last using MP reduction.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The biggest danger is her melee one-shot spell (Nindécence), unlocked at Nimpatience III; if she is killed quickly, she never gets there.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Turn 1: buff your characters (and possibly hit her from range) so you can kill her on turn 2, while staying back.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Later on (turn 3 or 4), she will very likely be able to one-shot a character. She is in the Lourd state: she cannot be carried.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Stay out of range of her spells and of the monsters so you don't get hit.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The first character hit during the turn gets the "Clochecuivre" state; out of range of Nimparabilité (8 range), she does not gain Nimpatience (+20% final damage per state). Watch out for the Marthos, which hits along a whole line.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.4.action: As soon as a character has the "Clochecuivre" state, hit Barbéryl in melee (character or summon) before her turn.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Otherwise, at the start of her turn, she swaps places with that character and removes 100 MP from them for 1 turn. Any ally or summon can deal this melee damage.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Otherwise, put that character or Barbéryl in Pesanteur or Enraciné (or carry the character with a Pandawa).
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: A state that prevents position swaps cancels the swap and the 100 MP penalty. Pesanteur also blocks Ninfernal's leap.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not push her while you focus her.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Each push gives her +20% resistances for 2 turns (stackable, cannot be debuffed).
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Prevent the Sanglirok from casting "Ninspiration" on her (move it more than 5 range away, block its line of sight or debuff).
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: This spell shares damage between the Sanglirok and its target for 2 turns.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.8.action: If she reaches Nimpatience III or V, place summons in her path.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Her AI tends to one-shot the first enemy entity in her path, often summons. At Nimpatience V, the one-shot can be cast once per turn.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Once Barbéryl is dead, finish off the remaining monsters.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.etat-clochecu.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: The fight is then easy. "Dernier" achievement: kill the monsters first (Marthos first) using MP reduction, then Barbéryl from range without pushing her.

mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.nimpatience-o.title: Nimpatience: +20% final damage per state; melee one-shot from Nimpatience III
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.nimpatience-o.summary: Each damage line she deals to an enemy increments her Nimpatience state (max 2 times per turn, 5 in total, never decremented). Each state gives her 20% final damage; at Nimpatience III she unlocks "Nindécence" (melee one-shot), usable once, then once per turn at Nimpatience V.
mech.barberyl-clochecuivre.nimpatience-o.notes.0: The guide advises eliminating her on turn 2, before she reaches Nimpatience III, and staying out of range of "Nimparabilité" (8 range).

mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.title: Invulnerability removed when the Sporakne ends its turn in a glyph
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.summary: The Korriandre is invulnerable and summons a Sporakne on turn 1. If the Sporakne ends its turn in one of the glyphs placed by the characters, he loses his invulnerability for the rest of the fight (and gains 1 MP, 200 power and the Riraule teleport spell).
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.prerequisites.0: The Sporakne ends its turn in a glyph placed by a character.
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.notes.0: If the Sporakne is killed by mistake, the Korriandre summons it again after 3 turns.
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.sequences.0.label: Guide tips
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the Sporakne to remove up to 3 MP from it (it loses 1 MP per hit taken, stacks 3 times).
mech.korriandre.sporakne-glyphe.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Push/pull it or bring it to 0 MP inside a glyph so that it ends its turn there.

mech.korriandre.glyphes-mortels.title: Start-of-turn glyphs that one-shot
mech.korriandre.glyphes-mortels.summary: Throughout the fight, each character places a glyph on their cell at the start of their turn; these glyphs kill characters and summons that start or end their turn on them. They last the whole fight, unless their caster dies.
mech.korriandre.glyphes-mortels.notes.0: Ending your turn on a glyph (yours or an ally's) = instant death.

mech.korriandre.hairpay.title: "Hairpay": 450 air damage every time damage is taken
mech.korriandre.hairpay.summary: The Korriandre only hits in a line. His Hairpay spell applies an effect that deals 450 air life steal damage to the target every time it takes damage. His damage spells have modifiable range: range reduction greatly lowers his threat.

mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.title: Hits only in melee, very hard
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.summary: The guide mentions no invulnerability. The Bworker only hits at close range (Sanction Bwork: 2400 neutral; Correction Bwork based on his missing HP) and buffs himself with 3 MP every x turns. Keeping him at range (MP reduction, pushes) or blocking him in a corner between two monsters makes the fight simple.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.notes.0: Do not block him with the Cybwork (which takes his damage) or with the Mama (which heals him).
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.unknownAspects.0: Guide predates Dofus 3 (2018); exact frequency of "Poursuite" not given ("every x turns").
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.unknownAspects.1: No mention of invulnerability: absence inferred.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Never let the Bworker reach melee range of any of your characters.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He hits only in melee and very hard: Sanction Bwork 2400 neutral, Correction Bwork 30% of his missing HP, Fauchoir 350 and a 2-cell push.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Option A: bring an MP-reduction character (e.g. an Enutrof) who removes his MP every turn.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: If he never reaches melee range of you, the fight is very simple. Warning: Poursuite gives him 3 MP every x turns.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Option A: meanwhile, kill the other monsters with the rest of the team, and push the Bworker back if he gets too close.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: This is the guide's range and MP-reduction strategy.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Option B: let the Bworker approach without him reaching melee range of you, then place him in a corner (a Pandawa is very useful).
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.4.position: Bworker in a corner of the map
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The guide's blocking strategy, which requires placement spells.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Option B: block him with two enemies, but not the Cybwork or the Mama.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Cybwork would take the boss's damage (Don de Soi) and the Mama would heal him.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Option B: put an ally with a lot of lock in melee with those two enemies; otherwise reposition them as soon as they move.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: So that the monsters blocking the boss don't move.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Kill or avoid the Bworks' Flammèches as a priority.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: They pull 4 cells and explode in melee for about 500, or even 1000 on a critical hit, on several characters from the very first turn.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "Baston équitable" achievement: kill the Bworker first, without AP/MP/range reduction or displacement; otherwise trap him with summons or a tank.
mech.bworker.corps-a-corps.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Enemies must not suffer any reduction or any displacement attempt.

mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.title: No invulnerability described; "Spore Hanchambre" fully heals him
mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.summary: The guide describes no invulnerability. From turn 2 (every 3 turns), Spore Hanchambre gives him a random one-turn buff that fully heals him if he takes either damage, an AP reduction attempt, or an MP reduction attempt. The guide advises debuffing him at the start of turn 2 and then killing him.
mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.unknownAspects.0: No mention of invulnerability: absence inferred.
mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Debuff the Ougah at the start of turn 2 (character with initiative).
mech.ougah.spore-hanchambre.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit him as hard as possible to eliminate him first, then finish the monsters.

mech.ougah.invocations-poisons.title: Summons every turn from turn 2 and poisons
mech.ougah.invocations-poisons.summary: From turn 2, the Ougah summons a random monster from the area every turn (6 summons maximum). His poisons (Sirop Spore: 80 damage per AP used for 4 turns) and those of the monsters quickly become dangerous; Bizarrerie strongly buffs the monsters around the target.

mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state; never remove his MP
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: Père Fwetar has no invulnerable state and only 2 MP, but he kills in melee (Infantophagie) and pulls 3 cells in a line. His passive "Vilain Garnement" gives him 1 MP for the whole fight on every MP reduction attempt (stacks infinitely): he can be pushed back, but not slowed down.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.notes.0: Every MP reduction attempt gives him 1 permanent MP.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.notes.1: Being pulled into contact with him exposes you to the melee one-shot (Infantophagie).
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Never try to remove MP from Père Fwetar (he can be pushed back).
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Vilain Garnement: every MP reduction attempt gives him 1 MP for the whole fight (stacks infinitely). He has no invulnerable state and only 2 MP.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Do not stay in line with him and never end your turn in contact with him; use obstacles.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Aspir'nenfan pulls 3 cells in a line, and Infantophagie one-shots in melee (he heals himself for 2100 HP).
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Stay 7 cells or less from him, without being adjacent, when possible.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Fwetage (700 in a random element, every turn, no line of sight needed) can only be cast from 8 range.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Kill the Wabbit plush first, then the Cadob' at loot 5+, then the Tofu plush, and the Bouftou plush last.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Wabbit heals a lot; the Cadob' can summon a Cadob'Omb that one-shots in a circle of radius 2.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: On turns 1, 4, 7, 10…: if the Poutch Ingball is not transformed, kill it within 3 turns.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: If it receives 2 AP twice, it has 4 AP and casts "Tuerie", which one-shots the whole team. When summoning, Père Fwetar also gains 1 MP for one turn.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If it is a puppet, adapt: kill the Dragon Cochon quickly (or debuff "Étourderie quasi-mortelle"), lock/block the line of sight of the Bouftou Royal, keep Mulou, Minotoror and Dark Vlad at range.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Do not kill the Mulou's Milimeulou: when it dies, the monsters gain 2 MP and 200 power.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Once the monsters are dead, hit Père Fwetar, preferably with earth.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Kill him in a single prepared turn, or leave him around 35-40% HP and finish him in one go the next turn.
mech.pere-fwetar.pas-d-invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Embûche de Nowel (every 10 turns, around 30% HP) fully heals him and gives 100 power to all monsters for 10 turns.

mech.pere-fwetar.fwetage.title: "Fwetage": heavy damage at infinite range, but not under 8 range
mech.pere-fwetar.fwetage.summary: Every turn, Père Fwetar hits hard (700 in a random element) at infinite range without line of sight, but this spell cannot be cast at less than 8 range. Staying 7 cells or less from him prevents it, at the cost of a higher risk of being pulled and one-shot in melee.

mech.pere-fwetar.poutch-marionnettes.title: Poutch Ingball and puppets (turns 1, 4, 7…); risk of a team one-shot
mech.pere-fwetar.poutch-marionnettes.summary: Every 3 turns (turns 1, 4, 7, 10…), he summons a Poutch Ingball and then transforms it: 2 chances in 3 into a random puppet (Bouftou Royal, Dark Vlad, Dragon Cochon, Minotoror or Mulou Meulé), 1 chance in 3 by giving it 2 AP. If the Poutch receives 2 AP twice, it reaches 4 AP and can cast "Tuerie", which kills the whole team: it must be eliminated within 3 turns.
mech.pere-fwetar.poutch-marionnettes.notes.0: Poutch at 4 AP = "Tuerie" spell, which one-shots all characters.
mech.pere-fwetar.poutch-marionnettes.notes.1: The Dragon Cochon puppet is the most dangerous (poison per AP used, "Étourderie quasi-mortelle"): debuff it or kill it quickly.
mech.pere-fwetar.poutch-marionnettes.notes.2: Summoning also gives him 1 MP for one turn.

mech.pere-fwetar.embuche-de-nowel.title: "Embûche de Nowel": full heal around 30% HP (every 10 turns)
