mech.pere-fwetar.embuche-de-nowel.summary: At around 30% of his HP, he fully heals himself and gives 100 power to himself and all monsters for 10 turns (10-turn cooldown). The guide advises leaving him around 35-40% and then finishing him in a single turn.
mech.pere-fwetar.embuche-de-nowel.notes.0: Do not bring him below 35% if you cannot finish him within the turn.

mech.pere-fwetar.cadob-butin5.title: Loot 5+: Cadob' and its Cadob'Omb
mech.pere-fwetar.cadob-butin5.summary: At loot 5 or higher, the Cadob' monster is present; each turn it has a 1 in 4 chance to summon a Cadob'Omb that kills all characters in a circle of radius 2 around it. The guide recommends eliminating it first.
mech.pere-fwetar.cadob-butin5.notes.0: Character at 2 range or less from the Cadob'Omb = one-shot.

mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerability removed by the Fulguration + Floutage states (Yomi and Yokaï)
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.summary: The Tengu starts invulnerable (and Lourd for the whole fight). In the same turn, you must: place the Yomi Givrefoux in line with the Tengu and hit the Yomi with a weapon (Fulguration state), and push or pull the Yokaï Givrefoux onto the Tengu's diagonal (Floutage state). Distance does not matter. At the start of his next turn, the Tengu casts "Toison givrée" and becomes vulnerable for 4 turns.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.expectedStateChange: With Fulguration and Floutage at the start of his turn, the Tengu casts "Toison givrée" and loses his invulnerability.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.prerequisites.0: A Yomi and a Yokaï Givrefoux alive on the battlefield.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.notes.0: Keep the Yomi and Yokaï alive while the Tengu is invulnerable; he summons new ones on turn 2 and then every 3 turns (2 summons max).
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.notes.1: Pushing the Yokaï makes characters on its diagonal Affaibli (no weapon); hitting the Yomi with a weapon applies 20% erosion to characters in line with it.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Removing the invulnerability
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place the Yomi in line with the Tengu and hit it with a weapon.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Yomi and its allies in line gain Fulguration (2 turns).
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Push or pull the Yokaï onto the Tengu's diagonal, in the same turn.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Yokaï and its allies on the diagonal gain Floutage (2 turns).
mech.tengu-givrefoux.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit the Tengu during his 4 turns of vulnerability; otherwise start again.

mech.tengu-givrefoux.etat-unique.title: Only one of the two states = dangerous special spell
mech.tengu-givrefoux.etat-unique.summary: If the Tengu has only one of the two states: with Fulguration alone he can cast "Mornifle" (melee one-shot); with Floutage alone, "Torgnole givrée" (30% erosion for 1 turn on all characters and summons). Hence the need to apply both states in the same turn.
mech.tengu-givrefoux.etat-unique.notes.0: Fulguration alone + character in contact = one-shot (Mornifle).

mech.tengu-givrefoux.attirance.title: "Câlin frigorifique": pulls 3 cells in a line
mech.tengu-givrefoux.attirance.summary: The Tengu only hits in melee but pulls 3 cells in a line, from 2 to 8 range, without line of sight. Avoid being in line with him, or hide behind an obstacle or a static summon.

mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.pas-d-invuln.title: Fuji has no invulnerable state
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.pas-d-invuln.summary: In the Tengu + Fuji variant, Fuji has no invulnerable state; the guide instead advises killing her first, unless the Tengu's invulnerability can be removed as early as turn 2. She only hits diagonally: staying in line with her avoids her damage.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.pas-d-invuln.notes.0: Much smaller map than the one with the Tengu alone.

mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.title: "Instinct maternel" passive: bonus for every monster killed
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.summary: For every monster eliminated, all monsters gain 1 MP for 1 turn, and Fuji and the Tengu gain 1,000 damage for 1 turn (stackable, cannot be debuffed). Kill the monsters out of reach of Fuji and the Tengu. The Tengu's summons do not trigger this bonus when they die.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Bring a class that can push back and/or remove MP.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The map with the Tengu and Fuji is much smaller: it is harder to avoid damage.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stay in line with Fuji, never on her diagonal.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Her damage spell (Foufoux) only hits diagonally: when you are in line with her, she can never hit you.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Never end your turn in contact with Fuji, and do not leave a summon near her.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Progéniture one-shots the target in melee and replaces it with a random monster from the area.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Focus Fuji first (unless you remove the Tengu's invulnerability as early as turn 2).
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Before killing a monster, make sure neither Fuji nor the Tengu will be able to hit you.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Instinct maternel: for every monster killed, all monsters gain 1 MP for 1 turn, and Fuji and the Tengu +1,000 damage for 1 turn (stackable, cannot be debuffed).
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Hide behind obstacles to avoid the Tengu's pull.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The Tengu pulls 3 cells in a line and only hits in melee.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.7.action: For the Tengu: in the same turn, hit the Yomi with a weapon while it is in line with the Tengu, and push or pull the Yokaï onto his diagonal.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.instinct-mat.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: With Fulguration and Floutage, the Tengu loses his invulnerability for 4 turns at the start of his next turn.

mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.progeniture.title: "Progéniture": melee one-shot and replacement by a monster
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.progeniture.summary: Fuji kills the target in melee and replaces it with a random monster from the area (limited to 1 per turn). Leave neither characters nor summons in contact with her.
mech.fuji-givrefoux-taniere.progeniture.notes.0: Being in contact with Fuji = one-shot.

mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.title: Invulnerable to ranged attacks: can only be hit in melee
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.summary: Père Ver is invulnerable to ranged damage for the whole fight (passive "Digestion Lente"): only melee damage hurts him. He has no MP, is Indéplaçable and teleports at the start of the fight to a fixed cell in the top right of the map. Every monster killed removes 10% resistances from him (infinite duration) but heals him for 20% of his max HP.
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.notes.0: He hits all characters in contact with him for 450 earth at the start of each of his turns: break away from him if your HP is low.
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.notes.1: 50% air resistance according to the achievements section.
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Eliminate all the monsters first (each one removes 10% resistances from the boss).
mech.pere-ver.invulnerable-distance.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Get into contact with Père Ver and hit him until he dies.

mech.pere-ver.passifs.title: Passives while he lives (erosion, pull, healing glyph) and poison after his death
mech.pere-ver.passifs.summary: While he is alive: 10% infinite erosion on characters, water damage on every forced displacement, 4-cell pull of characters in his line of sight and reveal of invisible ones, and each character places a brown glyph at the start of their turn that heals him for 15% of his max HP if he ends his turn on it. Once Père Ver is dead, these effects are replaced by an end-of-turn water poison.
mech.pere-ver.passifs.unknownAspects.0: Timing of the pull contradicts itself on the page: "at the start of each of his turns" (spells) vs "At the end of each of his turns" (mechanics).

mech.pere-ver.deces-traumatisant.title: "Décès Traumatisant": a killed monster hits its line of sight
mech.pere-ver.deces-traumatisant.summary: The monsters cannot be locked. When one of them dies, it deals 500 fire damage to all characters in its line of sight: block lines of sight (obstacles, summons) before finishing it off.

mech.pere-ver.paternalisme.title: "Paternalisme": damage sharing with a monster (from turn 2)
mech.pere-ver.paternalisme.summary: From turn 2, every turn he shares his damage with a monster (cannot be debuffed) and heals it for 10% on the following turn. Since Père Ver is invulnerable to ranged damage, hitting that monster only deals half the damage to it: switch targets unless the monster is almost dead. On turn 1, you can focus freely (the guide recommends the Trémorse).
mech.pere-ver.paternalisme.notes.0: "Coup d'Oeil" (turns 1, 3, 5…) applies a poison per MP used: limit your movement on that turn.

mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.title: Invulnerable until 4 Zoeuf explosions ("Zoeuf'd" state)
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.summary: The Supervizœuf is invulnerable. When a Zoeuf summoned by a monster is eliminated, it explodes in an area that depends on its summoner (Kamikabz: square 1; Quadrabz: ring 2; Toubibz: circle 2; Balebz: swap with the nearest entity). Each explosion that hits the boss gives him a "Zoeuf'd" state; at the 4th, he becomes vulnerable for the rest of the fight and enters phase 2.
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.prerequisites.0: Living Kabombz to summon Zoeufs (they only summon if they can use their damage spell).
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.notes.0: Balebz's Zoeuf: the Supervizœuf must be the nearest entity at the moment it is finished off.
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.notes.1: Each Kabombz only has one Zoeuf at a time.
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.sequences.0.label: Removing the invulnerability
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Keep some Kabombz alive (ideally the Kamikabz, which can summon again every turn) and place summons near them so they summon.
mech.supervizoeuf.zoeufd.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place each Zoeuf near the Supervizœuf, then eliminate it so the explosion hits him.

mech.supervizoeuf.phase-2.title: Phase 2: explosive clone and teleport onto the nearest character
mech.supervizoeuf.phase-2.summary: In phase 2, he gains 20% critical and 10% final damage, can no longer be put in Pesanteur, summons a clone (half his HP, 4 MP, 1,000 lock) that explodes after 2 turns (500 fire at 3 range), and teleports at the start of each turn onto the nearest character (clockwise priority). Killing the clone prevents the explosion and makes the boss take 20% more damage for 1 turn.
mech.supervizoeuf.phase-2.notes.0: The guide advises focusing him as soon as he is vulnerable.

mech.supervizoeuf.mort-explosion.title: Explosion on death, then 5 waves of monsters
mech.supervizoeuf.mort-explosion.summary: On death, he deals 250 damage in each element (1,000 in total) in a size-3 circle: move away before finishing him off. The fight then continues with 5 waves of monsters; in this dungeon every entity killed explodes in an area (except the Toubibz and its Zoeuf, which heal).
mech.supervizoeuf.mort-explosion.notes.0: Staying in the size-3 circle when the killing blow lands = 1,000 damage.
mech.supervizoeuf.mort-explosion.unknownAspects.0: Exact composition and trigger of the 5 waves not detailed in the boss section.

mech.supervizoeuf.saisons.title: Osavora season modifiers
mech.supervizoeuf.saisons.summary: Osavora has no classic dimension modifier but season modifiers (birth, hunt, rest), which also change the explosion areas and the hatching speed of the Zoeufs.

mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.title: Kill the 2 Kitsounebi in the same turn
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.summary: Koumiho is invulnerable from the start and summons 2 Kitsounebi flames that become invisible. Both must be killed in the same turn, before Koumiho plays again; he then becomes vulnerable for the whole fight and gains 20% melee damage. Walking into a Kitsounebi's blue glyph makes Koumiho swap places with it, which reveals its position; the Lanterne des Spiritueurs makes them visible and deals water damage to them.
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.prerequisites.0: Both Kitsounebi killed in the same turn.
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.notes.0: Killing only one Kitsounebi: it is summoned again and Koumiho deals heavy air damage (about 2,500) to the character who killed it.
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.unknownAspects.0: Exact timing of the invisibility is inconsistent on the page: "from turn 2" vs "at the end of their second turn".
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.sequences.0.label: Removing the invulnerability
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.sequences.0.steps.1.action: First eliminate the monsters accompanying Koumiho.
mech.koumiho.kitsounebi.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill both Kitsounebi in the same turn, before Koumiho's turn.

mech.koumiho.retraite.title: "Retraite" below 50% HP: invisible escape, then heal and shield
mech.koumiho.retraite.summary: If he starts his turn at 50% of his HP or less, Koumiho becomes invisible and Pacifiste with 3 extra MP; on the following turn he heals for 15% of his max HP, gains 30% of his HP as shield and 250 power (3-turn cooldown). To counter it: stop around 55-60% and then finish him in one turn, make him unhealable, or surround him so he cannot escape.
mech.koumiho.retraite.notes.0: Even when unhealable, he gains about 2,600 shield that cannot be debuffed.

mech.koumiho.lanterne.title: Special spell "Lanterne des Spiritueurs" (recommended)
mech.koumiho.lanterne.summary: The special spell "Lanterne des Spiritueurs" (obtained from Danaba Retzu at [36,-40] for 4 Étoffes de Samouraï fantôme) is not mandatory but strongly recommended: cast on yourself or summoned (radius-3 glyph), it removes certain states from the dungeon's monsters and, on the Kitsounebi, deals 20% of their current HP as water damage and makes them visible.
mech.koumiho.lanterne.notes.0: A summoned lantern blocks the spell for everyone as long as it is on the battlefield; if it is killed, there is a full 1-turn wait.

mech.kanigroula.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state
mech.kanigroula.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: Kanigroula has no invulnerable state. The difficulty comes from the high damage and the permanent effects applied at the start of the fight, which penalize focusing the boss as much as focusing the monsters.

mech.kanigroula.effets-permanents.title: Permanent effects: Sauvagerie and Mort Méphitique
mech.kanigroula.effets-permanents.summary: If Kanigroula dies, the monsters still alive gain 2 MP, 200 power and 10% resistances until the end. Conversely, every monster killed makes the characters lose 10% resistance and 50 power (stackable). She also reveals invisible enemies at the start of every turn.
mech.kanigroula.effets-permanents.notes.0: Odorat Bestial: invisible enemy entities are revealed at the start of every turn.

mech.kanigroula.pheromones.title: Phéromones Sauvages: bonus to enemies near the characters
mech.kanigroula.pheromones.summary: At the start and end of each character's turn, enemies 2 cells or less from them gain 10% critical and 100 power for one turn, stackable.
mech.kanigroula.pheromones.notes.0: Staying in contact with the monsters makes them stronger.

mech.kanigroula.strategie.title: Recommended strategy: monsters first, Kanigroula afterwards
mech.kanigroula.strategie.summary: The guide advises killing the monsters first (Kaniblou, then Orfélin from range, then Kanihilan) while letting Kanigroula run, then finishing her preferably from range because of "Rugissement matriarcal", which hits around her based on her HP.
mech.kanigroula.strategie.notes.0: "Chachyène dominante" kills the targeted summon from turn 3.
mech.kanigroula.strategie.sequences.0.label: Order recommended by the guide
mech.kanigroula.strategie.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the Kaniblou (healer, dangerous at range).
mech.kanigroula.strategie.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the Orfélin by hitting it from range (its "Boubou" spell reduces melee damage).
mech.kanigroula.strategie.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Finish off the Kanihilan (its spell reflect does not work on melee hits).

mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.title: Vulnerable for 3 turns when an ally is pushed into him
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.summary: The Obsidiantre is invulnerable from the start of the fight. He becomes vulnerable for 3 turns when an allied character is pushed into him and takes pushback damage. Pushing a summon, or pushing the boss into an ally, does not work. This also buffs him with 50 damage for 4 turns.
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.prerequisites.0: An allied character is pushed into the Obsidiantre and takes pushback damage.
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.notes.0: Pushing a monster into him heals him for 2000 HP and buffs him (Objurgation spell).
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.notes.1: Pushing a summon or pushing the Obsidiantre into an ally does not remove the invulnerability.
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.sequences.0.label: Removing the invulnerability
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place an ally in line with the Obsidiantre and push them into him (a Pandawa can help).
mech.obsidiantre.invulnerabilite-poussee.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit the boss during the 3 turns of vulnerability.

mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.title: Pougnette: explodes on its 5th turn, lethal beyond 7 range
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.summary: Every 3 turns, the Obsidiantre summons a Pougnette (Lourd state, reflects 150 damage when hit). At the end of its 5th turn, it explodes and kills enemies located more than 7 range away from it. Either kill it, or be between 1 and 7 range from it at that moment.
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.notes.0: Being more than 7 range from the Pougnette when it explodes = death.
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.notes.1: Guide tip: put it in the Pacifiste state on the turn of the explosion (e.g. Corruption).
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.sequences.0.label: Options described by the guide
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Either kill the Pougnette (it reflects damage).
mech.obsidiantre.pougnette.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Or stand between 1 and 7 range from it when its 5th turn comes (it can be pushed).

mech.obsidiantre.objurgation.title: "Objurgation": heal when a monster is pushed into contact with him
mech.obsidiantre.objurgation.summary: Pushing a monster onto a cell adjacent to the Obsidiantre heals him for 2000 HP and gives him 50 damage for 4 turns. "Scie licate" hits harder as he loses HP.

mech.minotot.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state described; Water and Air weaknesses
mech.minotot.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: The page describes no invulnerable state for the Minotot. It states that he is weak to Water and Air and advises killing him first, before turn 4.
mech.minotot.pas-d-invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: The page does not explicitly say there is no invulnerability; it simply describes none.

mech.minotot.destinos.title: "Destinos": transformation into a Tofu on turns 1, 4, 7…
mech.minotot.destinos.summary: Destinos debuffs the enemies hit, transforms them into Tofus, removes 100 AP from them for 3 turns, poisons them (400 fire per turn for 3 turns) and pushes them back. It is cast on turn 1 and then every 3 turns (size-5 cross area). These effects can be debuffed.
mech.minotot.destinos.sequences.0.label: Guide tip
mech.minotot.destinos.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Move away from the Minotot before the turns when Destinos comes back.

mech.minotot.kitos.title: "Kitos" at 15 AP: big group heal
mech.minotot.kitos.summary: The Minotot gains 1 AP per turn ("Motivatos", 6 turns). At 15 AP, he can cast Kitos, which heals him and his allies for 2000 HP at the start of each turn for 3 turns. The guide advises debuffing him at around 13-14 AP.

mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.title: Invulnerability removed for 2 turns by the "Lanterne des Spiritueurs"
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.summary: The Shogun is permanently invulnerable. You need the special spell "Lanterne des Spiritueurs" (obtained from Danaba Retzu at [36,-40] for 4 Étoffes de Samouraï fantôme): summoning the lantern 3 cells or less from him, or casting the spell on yourself with the boss within a radius of 3, removes his invulnerability for 2 turns.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.prerequisites.0: At least one character has the special spell "Lanterne des Spiritueurs".
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.notes.0: The guide thinks you then have to wait about 2 turns before you can make him vulnerable again ("It would seem").
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.unknownAspects.0: Exact delay before the invulnerability can be removed again not confirmed by the page.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first (Tambouraï first, keep the Kabushido at range).
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Block the Shogun (summon, character or wall behind him) so that he is not pushed out of the glyph.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.lanterne.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Summon the lantern 3 range or less from him and kill him during the 2 turns of vulnerability.

mech.shogun-tofugawa.brume-spectrale.title: "Brume Spectrale": enemies invisible outside the lantern's glyph
mech.shogun-tofugawa.brume-spectrale.summary: When his invulnerability is removed, the Shogun covers the whole map with a glyph: the monsters and the boss on it become invisible for 2 turns, except those that stayed inside the lantern's glyph. The lantern pushes enemies back 4 cells (2 diagonally), unless they are blocked. The Shogun also summons 2 Assaïshin that hit in melee.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.brume-spectrale.notes.0: Casting the lantern on yourself makes all enemies invisible, including the Shogun: not recommended by the guide.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.brume-spectrale.notes.1: Brume Spectrale disappears when the Shogun dies.

mech.shogun-tofugawa.malediction.title: "Malédiction du Dark Vlad": monsters cannot be locked
mech.shogun-tofugawa.malediction.summary: All the dungeon's monsters permanently cannot be locked. The lantern (summoned or cast on yourself) pushes back monsters within a radius of 3, removes 36 MP dodge and their lock-immune state for 1 turn; they cannot enter the lantern's glyph.
mech.shogun-tofugawa.malediction.notes.0: If the lantern dies from a monster's damage or from ranged damage, you must wait 1 full turn before casting the spell again.

mech.shogun-tofugawa.aspiration.title: "Aspiration du Yokomaïnu": 6-cell pull
mech.shogun-tofugawa.aspiration.summary: The Shogun only has 4 MP but pulls in a line up to 7 range, which can bring a character into contact with a Kabushido, very dangerous in melee.

mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.title: Vulnerable for 5 turns when a Hamrack explodes in contact with him
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.summary: Ben le Ripate is invulnerable and Lourd. He summons a Hamrack (Lourd, invulnerable, Enraciné, 2 MP) that disappears after 3 turns. If the Hamrack reaches contact with Ben, it explodes with "Gouverne ail" and makes him vulnerable for 5 turns, hitting allies standing in the area.
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.prerequisites.0: The Hamrack reaches melee range of Ben le Ripate.
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.notes.0: The explosion deals about 350 water damage to allies in the area around Ben.
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.notes.1: When Ben becomes vulnerable, all Hamracks present explode.
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Bring Ben closer to the Hamrack by pushing Ben (the Hamrack cannot be moved).
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Block Ben with characters or summons so he stays near the Hamrack.
mech.ben-le-ripate.hamrack.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Try to remove MP from the Hamrack: it then gains 3 MP for 1 turn and reaches Ben more easily.

mech.ben-le-ripate.mate-l-eau.title: "Mâte l'eau": pull and increasing damage
mech.ben-le-ripate.mate-l-eau.summary: Ben hits in a 4-range cross around him and pulls targets 3 cells; the damage increases as his HP goes down. The guide advises staying far from him when he becomes vulnerable.

mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.title: 200% resistances, reduced by turtles in contact with him
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.summary: According to the page (flagged for revision), the Sphincter Cell has 200% resistances in every element. His summoned turtles, placed in contact with him with a character in contact with the turtle, apply -200% resistances in their element to him for 2 turns (red fire, green earth, blue water, yellow air/agility).
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.prerequisites.0: A turtle in contact with the Sphincter Cell, with a character in contact with the turtle.
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.notes.0: The turtle's vulnerability also affects the character in contact with it (-200% in the element).
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.unknownAspects.0: Current mechanic to be confirmed (page flagged for revision, no date).
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.unknownAspects.1: The page mentions "agility weaknesses" for the yellow turtle: Air element assumed.
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.sequences.0.label: Method described by the page
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first, especially the Rat Noir and the Rat Blanc.
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the turtles whose element you don't use.
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Immobilize the Cell (Pesanteur, 0 MP, blocking) and place the chosen turtle in contact with him, at 0 MP.
mech.sphincter-cell.tortues.sequences.0.steps.4.action: On the turtle's turn, hit him in the weakened element for 2 turns; repeat if needed.

mech.sphincter-cell.rats.title: Sidekicks: Rat Noir and Rat Blanc
mech.sphincter-cell.rats.summary: The Cell is accompanied by the Rat Noir (poisons that can kill a character who is healed or hit) and the Rat Blanc (gains 50% resistance in the element that hits it). The page advises killing them first.

mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.title: Invulnerability removed by 6 attacks in the imposed Rage element
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.summary: Hell Mina is Lourd and invulnerable. At the start of each of her turns, she gives each character a Rage state (Earth, Fire, Water or Air). Each character who uses a spell of that element (even on an empty cell) increments her Rage state by 1, once per character. At the 6th increment, she loses Lourd and Invulnerable for the rest of the fight.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.expectedStateChange: Hell Mina permanently loses Lourd and Invulnerable; she gains 3 MP, 40% final damage and 50% critical.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.prerequisites.0: Six uses of the correct Rage element in total (one per character and per assignment).
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.notes.0: Not using the assigned element: 500 damage in that element and the state disappears without incrementing.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.notes.1: At state V, nothing is displayed anymore; one last attack of the correct element is enough.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.sequences.0.label: Guide's overall strategy
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Every turn, use at least one spell in the assigned element.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the monsters first, and keep the last increment(s) for the end.
mech.hell-mina.etats-rage.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Once she is vulnerable, kill her quickly: she gets stronger.

mech.hell-mina.malterego.title: "Appel du Malterego" area mechanic
mech.hell-mina.malterego.summary: At the start of its first turn, each monster becomes invisible and summons a copy (Malterego) with different spells. Killing the Malterego makes its summoner visible and weakens it (-3 MP, -40% resistances, damage reduced by 50%). Killing a monster before its first turn prevents it from summoning.
mech.hell-mina.malterego.notes.0: Maltrio's Malterego gives 3 AP but deals 80 neutral damage per AP used (end-of-turn poison).
mech.hell-mina.malterego.notes.1: Each monster summons only one Malterego per fight.

mech.hell-mina.poussee.title: Pushback damage and Fire resistance
mech.hell-mina.poussee.summary: A good part of Hell Mina's damage is pushback damage (Bond maléfique, Extermination Iopesque, "Préjudice" buff): avoid ending your turn near a wall. She has 31% Fire resistance; Water and Air are her weaknesses.

mech.chene-mou.description.title: Line pull and ranged hits
mech.chene-mou.description.summary: According to the page (flagged for revision), the Chêne Mou pulls characters lined up with him, hits them hard with Water and then pushes them back; with no target in line, he hits at range with Earth and AP reduction. The guide advises removing his range and MP, killing the two branches first and then the monsters, and favoring Air and Water.
mech.chene-mou.description.notes.0: Page flagged as needing revision; description predates many updates.
mech.chene-mou.description.unknownAspects.0: No invulnerable state is described for the classic dungeon.
mech.chene-mou.description.unknownAspects.1: Current spells and numbers not confirmed.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place the characters with the least HP at the back of the map.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Fragile characters at the back of the map
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Chêne Mou pulls characters in line with him, hits them very hard with water and then pushes them back; with nobody in line, he hits at range (about 500 earth with AP reduction).
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Buff up, then debuff the Chêne Mou if he gives himself range, and remove range from him (e.g. with an Enutrof).
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He can buff his range, critical hits and damage enormously.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: To prevent him from pulling you into melee with him.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: They can be very troublesome for the rest of the fight.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Kill the rest of the monsters while keeping the Chêne Mou out of range of the team.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.6.action: When he is alone, hit the Chêne Mou, favoring air and water spells.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Guide tip; the expedition section specifies that he has lower resistances in these two elements.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Guild expedition: kill the monsters, then the Chêne Mou, and only then the branches.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The branches are invulnerable as long as the Chêne Mou is alive; the Branche Invocatrice summons a monster every two turns.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "Enchaînemou" achievement: end each turn in line with an enemy, avoiding ending too often in line with the Chêne Mou.
mech.chene-mou.description.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Killing him first can help, since once he is alone you will have no choice but to end in line with him.

mech.chene-mou.expedition-branches.title: Guild expedition: branches invulnerable as long as the Chêne Mou lives
mech.chene-mou.expedition-branches.summary: In the guild expedition, the Chêne Mou has a lot of resistances and the branches accompanying him (including summoned ones) are invulnerable. Their invulnerability only disappears when the Chêne Mou dies: kill the other monsters, then the Chêne Mou, then the branches.
mech.chene-mou.expedition-branches.notes.0: The Branche Invocatrice summons a monster every two turns.
mech.chene-mou.expedition-branches.notes.1: The Branche Soignante makes the nearest enemy heal every time the affected character moves (per movement, not per MP).
mech.chene-mou.expedition-branches.unknownAspects.0: Rule specific to the guild expedition; page flagged for revision.

mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.title: Vulnerable for 6 turns when an ally is healed in contact with him
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.summary: The Mansot Royal is invulnerable from the start. He becomes vulnerable for 6 turns when a character is healed while in melee with the boss, which triggers "Mansodah" (healing a summon does not work). If that character dies, the boss becomes invulnerable again.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.prerequisites.0: A character (not a summon) is healed while in contact with the Mansot Royal.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.notes.0: Mansodah hits allies in contact with the healed character for about 200 water (about 900 for the healer if they heal a character in contact with themselves).
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.notes.1: Death of the character healed in contact = invulnerability returns.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring a character who can heal.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: It is a heal that removes the Mansot Royal's invulnerability (a cawotte's glyph also works, but it is more complicated).
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Start of the fight: the Mansot Royal is invulnerable. Choose to kill him first, especially in a small team.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Mansomon: each allied monster that dies gives him +1000 vitality, +10% final damage and +1 MP, with no time limit and cannot be debuffed.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Send ONE character (not a summon) into melee with the Mansot Royal, with no ally adjacent to that character.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.3.position: In contact with the boss, cells around the character free of allies
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The heal triggers Mansodah, which hits allies in contact with the healed character for about 200 water.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.4.action: The healer heals that character from range, without being adjacent to them.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: If the healer heals someone in contact with them, Mansodah hits them much harder (about 900).
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.5.action: The Mansot Royal is vulnerable for 6 turns from that heal: the whole team focuses its damage on him.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The 6 turns start at the moment of the heal. Warning: while vulnerable, he can cast Mansolénoïde in melee, and Mansoxygène gives him a shield of 200% of his level for 2 turns (cannot be debuffed).
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Protect the character who was healed in contact: they must not die.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: If they die, the Mansot Royal becomes invulnerable again.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Option: push or pull the Mansot Royal before hitting him, to heal yourself, provided you have no ally next to you.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Mansomnanbule (1 turn): you heal for 100% of the damage you deal to him, but this heal also triggers Mansodah on allies in contact.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.8.action: If he is not dead at the end of the 6 turns, start again from step 3.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.9.action: "Privilège royal" achievement: only the designated fighter (heart icon above them) can be healed, so they are the one who must go into contact with the Mansot Royal.
mech.mansot-royal.soin-en-melee.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: The Mansot Royal designates this fighter at the start of each turn.

mech.mansot-royal.mansomon.title: "Mansomon": buff for each dead ally
mech.mansot-royal.mansomon.summary: For each of his dead allies (excluding summons), the Mansot Royal gains 1000 vitality, 10% final damage and 1 MP, permanently and cannot be debuffed. Some players therefore prefer to kill him first, especially in a small team.

mech.mansot-royal.mansomnanbule.title: "Mansomnanbule": heal from damage after a push/pull
mech.mansot-royal.mansomnanbule.summary: Pushing or pulling the Mansot Royal gives him the Mansomnanbule effect for 1 turn: you then heal for 100% of the damage you deal to him. Be careful not to be next to an ally, since the heal triggers Mansodah.

mech.tynril.resistances.title: Four Tynrils with 200% resistances except in one element
mech.tynril.resistances.summary: The four Tynrils have 200% resistances in all elements but one: Perfide (Fire/intelligence), Déconcerté (Water/chance), Consterné (Air/agility), Ahuri (Earth/strength). Hit each one in its weak element.
mech.tynril.resistances.unknownAspects.0: Undated page, written in an old style; to be rechecked.

mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.title: -2000% weakness and lethal melee hits
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.summary: Each Tynril applies -2000% resistances in its element to the nearest character; since it hits in melee in that element, a weakened character it hits is killed outright. Two Tynrils in contact can merge back together, and each one swaps places with another on its turn.
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.notes.0: Being hit in melee by the Tynril whose weakness you carry = instant death.
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.notes.1: The guide considers healing useless in this room.
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.sequences.0.label: Page tips
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place important characters as far as possible from the Tynrils.
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Bring the Tynrils to 0 MP (they only have 2 MP and little dodge) or push them back.
mech.tynril.faiblesse-2000.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit each one in its weak element.

mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.title: Shared damage; Hanshi reduces melee damage by 50%
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.summary: Hanshi and Shihan share the damage they take. Hanshi reduces melee damage by 50%, Shihan ranged damage: it is better to hit Hanshi from range and Shihan in melee. No invulnerable state is described.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.notes.0: The guide advises killing the monsters before attacking the two bosses.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first before attacking the two guardians.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit Hanshi mostly from range, and Shihan mostly in melee.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Hanshi and Shihan share the damage they take; Hanshi reduces melee damage by 50%, Shihan ranged damage by 50%.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not stay in line with Hanshi at 7 range or less.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Da Bàng (200 earth) pulls the target into melee with him, only in a line up to 7 range.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Have 60 to 70 dodge (or the Pandawa's Stabilisation, the Sram's Brume/Invisibilité) to get out of his contact.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Jufang applies Pesanteur and Indéplaçable to the target and to himself; he loses 100 MP but gains 50 lock for 1 turn (3-turn cooldown).
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Beware of his HP thresholds: stay far away when he approaches 2,900 and then 1,450 HP.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: At 2,900 HP he gains 4 MP for 2 turns; at 1,450 HP, 4 MP and 20% melee damage for 2 turns.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.6.action: "Dernier" achievement (Hanshi finished last): rush Shihan in melee.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: That way Hanshi will lose less HP than Shihan, and you can kill Shihan without killing Hanshi.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.7.action: "Vents contraires" achievement: deal only ranged damage to Hanshi.
mech.hanshi.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Hanshi masters the breath of the Wukang: he must only take ranged damage.

mech.hanshi.seuils.title: Hanshi's HP thresholds
mech.hanshi.seuils.summary: Hanshi gains 4 MP for 2 turns at 2,900 HP, then 4 MP and 20% melee damage for 2 turns at 1,450 HP.

mech.hanshi.jufang.title: "Jufang": melee lockdown
mech.hanshi.jufang.summary: Jufang hits in melee and applies Pesanteur and Indéplaçable to the target and to Hanshi for 1 turn; Hanshi loses his MP but gains 50 lock. "Da Bàng" pulls the target to him in a line up to 7 range.

mech.shihan.partage-dommages.title: Shared damage; Shihan reduces ranged damage by 50%
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.summary: Shihan shares the damage he takes with Hanshi and reduces ranged damage by 50%: so he must be hit in melee.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first before attacking the two guardians.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit Shihan mostly in melee, and Hanshi mostly from range.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Shihan and Hanshi share the damage they take; Shihan reduces ranged damage by 50%, Hanshi melee damage by 50%.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Beware of his Qìkǒng trap and his Grande Lame du Vent (in a line).
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Qìkǒng (150 fire) teleports the nearest enemy into melee with him; Grande Lame du Vent (270 air, line of 5, up to 7 range) pushes back 3 cells and places a glyph that removes 2 MP.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Anticipate his HP thresholds at 4,350 and 1,450 HP.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: At each threshold, Shihan gains 2 MP for 2 turns.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.5.action: "Dernier" achievement (Hanshi finished last): rush Shihan in melee to kill him before Hanshi.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Hanshi will lose less HP than Shihan thanks to his melee reduction.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.6.action: "Vents contraires" achievement: deal only melee damage to Shihan.
mech.shihan.partage-dommages.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Shihan masters the breath of the Wukin: he must only take melee damage.

mech.shihan.seuils.title: Shihan's HP thresholds
mech.shihan.seuils.summary: Shihan gains 2 MP for 2 turns at 4,350 HP and again at 1,450 HP. He supports his allies (Brise apaisante: heal and shield) and places a trap that teleports the nearest enemy into contact with him.

mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.title: Invulnerable for 2 turns if hit with a close combat weapon
mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.summary: The guide (page flagged for revision) only states that dealing damage to the Haute Truche with a close combat weapon makes her invulnerable for 2 turns; so avoid using weapons on her.
mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.vulnerabilityDuration: 2 turns of invulnerability after close combat weapon damage.
mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.notes.0: Hitting the Haute Truche with a close combat weapon = 2 turns without being able to damage her.
mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.unknownAspects.0: The page states that it needs revision: the boss's spells and other mechanics are not described.
mech.haute-truche.invulnerabilite-cac.unknownAspects.1: Information taken from the achievements section; not confirmed elsewhere on the page.

mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.title: Invulnerable: killed by eliminating 4 Pépites du Croqueleur
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.summary: From the start of the fight, the Croqueleur casts Croquelure: he becomes invulnerable (infinite) and gets 4 chocolate states. He cannot be killed directly: you must make him summon 4 Pépites one after another and eliminate them; each Pépite killed removes 25% of his HP and one of his states, and he dies when the last one is finished off.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.notes.0: You must hit him with the expected element before pushing him, otherwise no Pépite appears.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.notes.1: Each push that makes a Pépite appear gives him 1 AP and 1 MP (max 4 in total).
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.notes.2: The guide advises that the character playing right after the Croqueleur be the one who makes the Pépites appear.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.label: Sequence described by the guide
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Eliminate all the monsters first and keep the Croqueleur for last.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit the Croqueleur with fire (Fondu state), then push him: 1st Pépite, to be killed within 1 turn.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit with air (Soufflé state), then push: 2nd Pépite, 2 turns to kill it.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Hit with water (Lavé state), then push: 3rd Pépite, 2 turns to kill it.
mech.croqueleur.invulnerabilite-pepites.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Hit with earth or neutral (Brisé state), then push: 4th Pépite; its death kills the Croqueleur.

mech.croqueleur.delai-pepites.title: Pépites must be killed within 1 turn (the 1st) or 2 turns, otherwise they disappear
mech.croqueleur.delai-pepites.summary: A Pépite du Croqueleur must be eliminated within 2 turns at most, counted from the turn of the character who made it appear (only 1 turn for the first one), otherwise it disappears and you must start again.
mech.croqueleur.delai-pepites.notes.0: Pépite not killed in time = it disappears, the step must be redone.

mech.croqueleur.resistances-pepites.title: Pépites resistant to ranged damage: favor melee
mech.croqueleur.resistances-pepites.summary: The Pépites du Croqueleur have decreasing ranged protections: the 1st is invulnerable to ranged damage (25% of the boss's max HP), the 2nd has 70% ranged resistance (35%), the 3rd 40% (45%), the 4th 10% (55%). They have a 10% weakness in the element the Croqueleur was hit with.
mech.croqueleur.resistances-pepites.notes.0: In the air phase, his Attraction gourmande spell can inflict -50% melee damage.

mech.croqueleur.morcelage.title: "Morcelage": the monsters' crunchy Pépites
mech.croqueleur.morcelage.summary: All the dungeon's monsters can randomly summon crunchy Pépites (200 HP, immobile) when hit. A Pépite that dies gives characters in contact 50 power and 210 shield points for 2 turns; but a monster that eats one (Croquanibalisme, in contact) gains 1 AP, heals itself and gets a bonus specific to its race.
mech.croqueleur.morcelage.unknownAspects.0: The guide states that the appearance of the pépites seems random (probability not specified).

mech.el-piko.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state; reflects 50 damage per line
mech.el-piko.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: The guide describes no invulnerability for El Piko: once he is alone, just focus him. However, he reflects 50 damage for each damage line taken, for the whole fight.
mech.el-piko.pas-d-invulnerabilite.notes.0: The guide advises killing the Lévito(s) first, as they remove AP/MP and apply states.

mech.el-piko.guerillero.title: "Guerillero" effect: damage to adjacent allies at end of turn
mech.el-piko.guerillero.summary: From the start of the fight, all characters receive the Guerillero effect (infinite): when a character ends their turn, entities on adjacent cells take about 110 damage (element depending on El Piko's Tactique state). So never end your turn adjacent to an ally.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.notes.0: Ending your turn in contact with an ally deals damage to them.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Never end your turn in contact with an ally, for the whole fight.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Guerillero: when a character ends their turn, all characters on an adjacent cell take 110 damage (element depending on the Tactique state).
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: They can remove several AP and MP and apply various states that complicate the fight.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Then kill the other monsters, playing mostly at range.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Several spells of the monsters and of El Piko can only be cast in melee (e.g. Pikak, 300 damage).
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Don't worry about the Tactique A/B/C/D states.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: They are drawn at random at the start of each of El Piko's turns and only change the fight very slightly.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Once the monsters are dead, focus El Piko alone.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He has no invulnerable state but reflects 50 damage for each damage line taken, for the whole fight.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.6.action: "Blitzkrieg" achievement: prepare a turn of buffed damage to kill him in one turn, and avoid doing it during Tactique A if you lack damage output.
mech.el-piko.guerillero.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: An attacked enemy must be finished off before its turn; Tactique A gives 10% resistances to all enemies for 1 turn.

mech.el-piko.etats-tactique.title: Random "Tactique" A/B/C/D states on each of El Piko's turns
mech.el-piko.etats-tactique.summary: At the start of each of El Piko's turns, he and his allies randomly receive a Tactique state (25% each) that changes the element and effects of their spells (switch to life steal) and grants a bonus for the turn: A = 10% resistances, B = 25 lock and dodge, C = 25 AP/MP dodge, D = 100 power. The guide considers that this changes the fight very little.
mech.el-piko.etats-tactique.notes.0: In Tactique A, enemies gain 10% resistances: the guide advises taking it into account for a burst turn.

mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.title: Invulnerable in a geoglyph: get him out of the glyph
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.summary: The Tanukis, boss included, place a brown geoglyph on and around themselves at the start of the fight and at the end of each turn; a Tanuki in a geoglyph (its own or another one's) is invulnerable. Get it out of the glyph: inside the glyph, a melee attack pushes it back 2 cells and a ranged attack pulls it 2 cells.
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.prerequisites.0: The targeted Tanuki is not on any geoglyph.
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.notes.0: The Tanukouï San's geoglyph grows with his phase: 7x7 square (I), checkerboard of radius 6 (II), infinite star (III).
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.notes.1: The guide advises keeping the monsters away from each other so the geoglyphs don't stack.
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.sequences.0.label: Making a Tanuki vulnerable
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the Tanuki in melee (pushed back 2) or from range (pulled 2) to get it out of the glyph.
mech.tanukoui-san.geoglyphe.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit it once it is outside every geoglyph.

mech.tanukoui-san.phases-soin.title: 3 threshold phases and X.5 steps that heal him
mech.tanukoui-san.phases-soin.summary: The Tanukouï San has 3 phases with HP thresholds (Roman numeral above his head). At each intermediate X.5 step, if he has not moved to the next phase before the start of his turn, he heals for about 20% of his max HP. So plan enough damage (about 400 to 500 extra) to pass the step before he plays.
mech.tanukoui-san.phases-soin.notes.0: Staying in phase X.5 at the start of his turn = heal of about 1300 HP (loot 4).
mech.tanukoui-san.phases-soin.unknownAspects.0: Threshold values given only for loot 4, and approximately.

mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.title: Invulnerable to ranged attacks on her islet: reach it via a Bombombre à Eau
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.summary: From the start, Nagate is teleported onto an islet on the other side of the map and stays invulnerable to ranged damage for the whole fight: you must reach her and hit her in melee. To do this, wait for a monster to summon a Bombombre à Eau (rare), place it on one of the 3 edge cells in front of the islet, then hit it in melee without killing it: the character is teleported onto the islet.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.prerequisites.0: A Bombombre à Eau is present on the battlefield.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.notes.0: If Nagate is not killed and the character is not in contact with her at the start of her turn, she sends them back to the main map.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.notes.1: On the islet, when not in contact with her, she can send the character off the islet (Hors de ma vue).
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.sequences.0.label: Reaching Nagate
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Do not kill the Bombombre à Eau; place it on one of the 3 map-edge cells in front of the islet.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stand in contact with the Bombombre and deal damage to it without killing it.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The character is then teleported onto the islet.
mech.nagate.ilot-bombombre-eau.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill Nagate in melee, ideally in the same turn.

mech.nagate.reverence.title: "Révérence" spell: control a Kwapa to force a Bombombre à Eau
mech.nagate.reverence.summary: The Révérence spell, obtained before the dungeon from Rei Beransu (Osakwa Tavern, [20,-20]), heals a Kwapa and has a very small chance of taking control of it (it must not be at full health). A controlled Kwapa summons a Bombombre à Eau for sure and can kill itself with Kwarakiri.
mech.nagate.reverence.unknownAspects.0: Exact probability of taking control and of a Bombombre à Eau appearing naturally not quantified.

mech.nagate.bombombres.title: Bombombres: green glyphs that hit
mech.nagate.bombombres.summary: All Kwapas have "Invocation de bombombre" (3 to 9 range, 3-turn cooldown, not within 3 range of another one): the Bombombre places a green glyph on its adjacent cells that deals about 120 damage in the summoning monster's element when walked on.

mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.title: Guild expedition: 100% resistances removed by killing the Royal Blops
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.summary: In the guild expedition version described by the page, the Blop Multicolore has 100% resistances in all elements; killing a Blop Royal removes the 100% resistances of the corresponding element (e.g. Blop Royal Reinette = earth).
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.notes.0: Each Blop Royal can give an ally 100% resistance in its element for 1 turn.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.unknownAspects.0: The page (flagged for revision) only describes this mechanic for the guild expedition; not confirmed for the classic dungeon.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.unknownAspects.1: Classic dungeon mechanics limited to the spell list and the Elitiste achievement.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.sequences.0.label: Order suggested by the page (expedition)
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the Royal Blops (Coco, Griotte, Indigo, Reinette) while staying out of their 6 range.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.resistances-.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Then hit the Blop Multicolore in the elements whose resistances have been removed.

mech.blop-multicolore-royal.blopagation.title: "Blopagation": area poison and Insoignable
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.blopagation.summary: The Blop Multicolore applies Insoignable for 1 turn to his enemies; in the expedition, every 3 turns the spell also applies a 2-turn poison in each element to all characters and summons.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.blopagation.unknownAspects.0: Values differ between the dungeon section (old) and the expedition section.

mech.blop-multicolore-royal.glyphe-blanc.title: White glyph of the summoned Blops: death at end of turn
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.glyphe-blanc.summary: The Blops summoned by the Royal Blops place a one-cell white glyph that removes 2 MP; a character who ends their turn in it dies immediately.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.glyphe-blanc.notes.0: Ending your turn in a white glyph = immediate death.
mech.blop-multicolore-royal.glyphe-blanc.unknownAspects.0: Described in the guild expedition section; applicability to the classic dungeon not specified.

mech.minotoror.resistances-terre.title: No invulnerability; very resistant except to earth (-20%)
mech.minotoror.resistances-terre.summary: The Minotoror has no invulnerable state and no unlock mechanic. He has 40 to 60% resistance to neutral, fire, water and air, but -20% to earth: an earth character can take him down very quickly, and the guide then advises focusing him first.
mech.minotoror.resistances-terre.notes.0: The Minotot (next dungeon), on the contrary, has 40% earth resistance and water and air weaknesses.

mech.minotoror.sabotage.title: "Sabotage": big melee hit with a 6-cell push
mech.minotoror.sabotage.summary: His only damage spell is melee (600 neutral, 1000 on critical) and pushes back 6 cells: pushback damage is added if an obstacle is nearby. The guide advises avoiding his melee range, or at least not having an obstacle behind you.
mech.minotoror.sabotage.notes.0: Being pushed into a nearby obstacle = heavy pushback damage on top of the hit.

mech.minotoror.tofus-et-acolytes.title: Thrown Tofus and mini-bosses Déminoboule / Mominotor
mech.minotoror.tofus-et-acolytes.summary: Each turn, the Minotoror summons a thrown Tofu (99 HP, 11 MP, air hit) and can boost allied summons. He is accompanied by the Déminoboule and the Mominotor, who have more HP than him at loot 4. The Mominotor one-shots summons with "Malédiction du Mominotor" (6-turn cooldown): the guide advises making him waste this spell on a useless summon before summoning.
mech.minotoror.tofus-et-acolytes.notes.0: The Déminoboule mostly hits in melee with a big power penalty (up to -500 on critical): keep him at a distance.

mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.title: Guild expedition: remove his resistances by hitting him in line
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.summary: In the guild expedition, you must hit the Minotoror while in line with him: he then pulls himself to the attacker, deals about 900 neutral in an area and pushes back 2 cells, loses 10% resistances and gains 10% final damage for 2 turns (10 triggers per turn maximum; an off-line hit also counts). Each turn he boosts himself by 300 power and 2,000 vitality, as well as his nearby allies.
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.prerequisites.0: The attacker is in line with the Minotoror (guild expedition only).
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.notes.0: Do not group your characters in a cross around his landing cell.
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.unknownAspects.0: Rule specific to the guild expedition, not the classic dungeon.
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.label: Guide tips (expedition)
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill all the monsters first, moving the Minotoror away from his allies ("Toromachine" spell).
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Have a tank character who plays right after him remove his resistances by hitting him in line.
mech.minotoror.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.action: The other characters hit without being in line so they don't take the damage.

mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.title: Kill the Poupée Affamée first (feed it summons / AP)
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.summary: The Skeunk fights alongside the 4 Sadida dolls (Diamantine, Émeraude, Rubise, Saphira) and the Poupée Affamée. The latter revives all monsters every turn: kill it first by feeding it summons or boosting its AP; at 8 AP it explodes (fire damage to all characters). Then kill Rubise and Diamantine as a priority.
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.notes.0: Diamantine summons a Poupée Mortelle that one-shots in melee; Rubise turns you into a totem (0 AP, 0 MP).
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.notes.1: The page says it needs revision: information may be wrong or missing.
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.unknownAspects.0: No information on a possible invulnerable state for the Skeunk.
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.unknownAspects.1: Monster levels and HP not given.
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.sequences.0.label: Order recommended by the guide
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Feed the Poupée Affamée summons (1 AP per summon, 2 max per turn) and/or boost its AP up to 8 AP.
mech.skeunk.poupee-affamee.sequences.0.steps.2.action: After it explodes, kill Rubise and Diamantine, then the rest in any order.

mech.skeunk.soins.title: The Skeunk heals and revives his allies
mech.skeunk.soins.summary: The Skeunk plays like an Eniripsa: he can revive an ally or himself, heal, remove MP, hit with fire, debuff and boost his own AP.

mech.skeunk.succes-special.title: "Les fans et les enfants d'abord" achievement: forced doll order
mech.skeunk.succes-special.summary: For the special achievement, the Sadida dolls must be killed in the order indicated by a state above them, and all of them before the Skeunk takes any damage. The Poupée Affamée can be killed whenever you want, but it heals everyone to 100% on its turn.
mech.skeunk.succes-special.notes.0: Dealing damage to the Skeunk (for example via an area) before all dolls are dead fails the achievement.

mech.crocabulia.pas-d-invulnerabilite.title: No invulnerable state (classic dungeon)
mech.crocabulia.pas-d-invulnerabilite.summary: In the classic dungeon, the Crocabulia has no invulnerable state or special effect: she hits with fire, earth and air, pushes her enemies and boosts her allies (power, AP). The difficulty comes from the "Coquillettes Ula" effect shared by all monsters. The guide advises killing her last.
mech.crocabulia.pas-d-invulnerabilite.notes.0: Avoid ending your turn in the red glyph of "Souffle" if possible.

mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.title: "Coquillettes Ula" effect: one shell every 4 turns
mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.summary: All monsters (Crocabulia included) can summon a shell (Brutale, Protectrice, Soigneuse or Véloce), only one at a time and with a global 4-turn cooldown, i.e. on turns 1, 5, 9… Each shell boosts the monsters at the start of its turn (the Crocabulia more strongly) and dies on its own after 4 turns. If killed earlier, it explodes in a radius-8 circle (damage + penalties, stronger if it dies early).
mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.notes.0: Being within 8 range of a shell when it dies prematurely = hit and penalty (Unhealable, -4 MP, -20% damage, +20% damage taken depending on the shell).
mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.sequences.0.label: Strategy recommended by the guide
mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Soigneuse or Protectrice shell: kill it quickly, while staying more than 8 range away from it.
mech.crocabulia.coquillettes-ula.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Brutale or Véloce shell: ignore it and let its 4 turns expire.

mech.crocabulia.eruption-dragmatique.title: Dragmatique's "Éruption" effect
mech.crocabulia.eruption-dragmatique.summary: The Dragmatique starts each turn with a Magma Pressure of 3, which drops by 1 per spell cast; at the end of its turn it casts a fire eruption in a radius-2 circle that is stronger the higher the remaining pressure (230/190/120, nothing at 0).

mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.title: Guild expedition: invulnerable until she one-shots 3 shells
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.summary: In the guild expedition, the Crocabulia is invulnerable and summons a shell (55,000 HP) at the start of each turn. At the start of her turn, she one-shots the shells aligned with her (line or diagonal, infinite range); an exploding shell makes shells within 3 range explode, fully heals the monsters and one-shots nearby characters and summons. She must herself one-shot 3 aligned shells (over the whole fight) to lose her invulnerability.
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.prerequisites.0: The Crocabulia has herself one-shot 3 shells in line or diagonal with her (guild expedition).
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.notes.0: Character or summon within 3 range of an exploding shell = one-shot.
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.unknownAspects.0: Rule specific to the guild expedition, not the classic dungeon.
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.sequences.0.label: Guide tips (expedition)
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Stay 4 range or more from any shell.
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Move the shells away from the monsters so they don't get healed.
mech.crocabulia.expedition-coquilles.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill the monsters during the minimum 3 turns needed for the unlock.

mech.royalmouth.inimouth.title: Invulnerable (Inimouth): push him to make him vulnerable for 1 turn
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.summary: From the start of the fight, the Royalmouth puts himself in an infinite invulnerable state ("Inimouth" spell). Pushing him disables this state for 1 turn: he is vulnerable from the start of the turn of whoever pushed him until that character's next turn, and gains 4 MP for 1 turn (stackable).
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.vulnerabilityDuration: From the start of the pusher's turn until their next turn.
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.prerequisites.0: The Royalmouth has been pushed (moved) during a character's turn.
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.notes.0: Each push gives him +4 MP for 1 turn, stackable.
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.sequences.0.label: Make the Royalmouth vulnerable
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.sequences.0.steps.1.action: A character pushes the Royalmouth without dealing pushback damage to him.
mech.royalmouth.inimouth.sequences.0.steps.2.action: The team hits him until that character's next turn.

mech.royalmouth.dommages-poussee.title: Pushback damage on the boss: one-shots aligned characters
mech.royalmouth.dommages-poussee.summary: Dealing pushback damage to the Royalmouth kills the characters in line with him at that moment, and he boosts his allies by 100 damage for 1 turn (Berserkmouth). Pushing a character into him has the same effect.
mech.royalmouth.dommages-poussee.notes.0: Pushback damage on the Royalmouth = death of the characters aligned with him.

mech.royalmouth.aleamouth.title: "Aléamouth": summon every 3 turns, bonus then penalty
mech.royalmouth.aleamouth.summary: On turn 1 and then every 3 turns, he summons a dungeon monster and gains a bonus depending on the monster (Bouftonmouth +1 MP, Boufmouth de guerre -5% damage taken, Boufmouth légendaire critical, Boufmouth +200 power). When that monster dies, the bonus disappears and an equivalent penalty is applied to him until the end of the fight.
mech.royalmouth.aleamouth.turnConditions: Summon on turn 1 then every 3 turns.

mech.tofu-royal.donjon-classique.title: Classic dungeon: 30 MP and hits with a vitality penalty
mech.tofu-royal.donjon-classique.summary: For the classic dungeon, the guide only states that the Tofu Royal has 30 MP, hits earth in melee and air in an area at about 3 range, with a 60 vitality penalty.
mech.tofu-royal.donjon-classique.notes.0: Page flagged as needing revision: information may be wrong or missing.
mech.tofu-royal.donjon-classique.unknownAspects.0: No invulnerable state or mechanic described for the classic dungeon.

mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.title: Expedition: vulnerable for 2 turns if he uses no MP during his turn
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.summary: In the guild expedition, the Tofu Royal is invulnerable. To lift the invulnerability for two turns, he must use no MP during his turn. Each melee damage instance removes 1 MP from the target until the end of the fight (5 times per turn). The guide advises surrounding him to block him (careful, he can push).
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.prerequisites.0: The Tofu Royal used no MP during his turn (guild expedition).
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.unknownAspects.0: Rule specific to the guild expedition.
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.sequences.0.label: Guide tips (expedition)
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first (not invulnerable, each has an elemental weakness).
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Block the Tofu Royal by surrounding him with characters or summons, or remove his MP.
mech.tofu-royal.expedition-invulnerabili.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Get him out of his glyph before hitting him.

mech.tofu-royal.galiformation.title: Expedition: cyclic "Galiformation Royal" every 2 turns
mech.tofu-royal.galiformation.summary: From turn 2 and then every 2 turns, the Tofu Royal and all monsters receive a cyclic boost: turn 2 +50% final damage, turn 4 shield of 10% of the Tofu Royal's HP, turn 6 Untackleable (Intaclable), turn 8 heal of 10% HP, then back to the start of the cycle on turn 10. Each turn he also places a glyph (size-4 circle, 2 turns) that reduces ranged damage taken by monsters by 20% and heals them for 8% at the end of the turn.
mech.tofu-royal.galiformation.turnConditions: Boosts on even turns from turn 2 (8-turn cycle).
mech.tofu-royal.galiformation.notes.0: The Tofuzmo and the Vilain Petit Tofu (12 MP) are the most dangerous monsters.

mech.maitre-corbac.resistances.title: No invulnerability, but very high resistances (earth the weakest)
mech.maitre-corbac.resistances.summary: The Maître Corbac has no invulnerability or special mechanic; he has low HP for his level but between 25% and 55% resistance in each element. Earth is his least resisted element (25%), hence the advice to bring an earth character and kill the monsters first.
mech.maitre-corbac.resistances.notes.0: The guide advises killing the monsters first, because of these resistances.

mech.maitre-corbac.carapace-d-ailes.title: Carapace d'Ailes: reflects 400 damage for 2 turns
mech.maitre-corbac.carapace-d-ailes.summary: On turn 3 and then every 4 turns, he curls up for 2 turns: he loses 12 AP and 5 MP, reflects 400 damage (800 on critical) on each attack taken and deals air life-steal damage to everyone at the start of his turn. The effects can be debuffed; otherwise, avoid hitting him during the shell and deal with the monsters.
mech.maitre-corbac.carapace-d-ailes.turnConditions: Cast on turn 3 then every 4 turns; lasts 2 turns.
mech.maitre-corbac.carapace-d-ailes.notes.1: Hitting him during Carapace d'Ailes without debuffing him makes you take the 400 damage reflect.

mech.maitre-corbac.corbac-invoque.title: Summoned Corbac: no point killing it
mech.maitre-corbac.corbac-invoque.summary: The Maître Corbac can only have one summoned Corbac at a time, but he resummons it as early as the next turn if it dies. The guide therefore advises ignoring it.
mech.maitre-corbac.corbac-invoque.notes.0: The Corbac can debuff one character per turn: no point boosting yourself.

mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.title: Boss access: defeat the 3 unique monsters of the Library
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.summary: Since the rework of 21 January 2025, you must find and defeat 3 unique monsters hidden in the 16 rooms (Rono le Renarbo, Horace le Corbac Apprivoisé, Kapotie le Buveur) to obtain 3 alterations, then talk to Virgil again in the first room to face the Capsaloocke, then the Maître Corbac.
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.notes.0: Each unique monster exists only once: if it is already in a fight, you must wait for it to respawn.
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.sequences.0.label: Access as described by the guide
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Defeat Rono le Renarbo, Horace le Corbac Apprivoisé and Kapotie le Buveur (one feather each).
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Go back and talk to Virgil in the first room and use the key or the keyring.
mech.maitre-corbac.acces-plumes.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Defeat the Capsaloocke (mini-boss), then face the Maître Corbac.

mech.maitre-corbac.modulation.title: Scaling: all monsters get stronger beyond 4 characters
mech.maitre-corbac.modulation.summary: The number of monsters is the same with 4 or 8, but all monsters (not just the boss) gain HP and damage per additional character; at loot 8, they have double HP and damage.

mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.title: No invulnerability; at low HP he fully heals then splits in two
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.summary: Papa Nowel has no invulnerable state. When his HP gets low (about 20-25%), he heals for 100% and enters the "Fragilisé" state, then splits: legs (Papa Nowel, half the HP) and torso (Demi Papa Nowel, summon). Killing the legs is enough to end the fight; ideally, finish him before the reconstitution.
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.notes.0: The reconstitution threshold is given as approximate (about 20 or 25% of his HP).
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.sequences.0.label: Guide strategy
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first (order doesn't matter).
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Bring Papa Nowel down to about half his HP in one turn, then finish him the next turn before he reconstitutes.
mech.papa-nowel.reconstitution-separatio.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If he has split, focus the legs (Papa Nowel); ignore the torso.

mech.papa-nowel.os-melee-attirance.title: Melee one-shot and in-line pull at infinite range
mech.papa-nowel.os-melee-attirance.summary: Infantophagie kills the target in one hit in melee (once per turn), and Papa Nowel keeps this spell for the whole fight. He can pull 3 cells in line with no range limit, and gains range with each MP-removal attempt. Avoid being in line with him.
mech.papa-nowel.os-melee-attirance.notes.0: After the split, it is the legs (Papa Nowel) that keep the one-shot and the pull.

mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.title: 200% resistances: push him to 14 AP to weaken him in one element
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.summary: According to the guide (page needing revision), Silf has 200% resistance everywhere. The recommended technique: first kill his allies and summons, then remove his AP (each AP lost adds one to him) or boost him up to 14 AP; he then casts his spell and you must hit him several times with cheap spells in one single element.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.notes.0: The resistance drop only applies to one element: choose it and keep it until the end.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.unknownAspects.0: The spell cast at 14 AP is not named or precisely described.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.unknownAspects.1: The page is flagged as needing revision and is undated: mechanic possibly outdated.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.unknownAspects.2: The guide mentions other techniques without detailing them.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.sequences.0.label: Technique described by the guide
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Remove his AP (or boost his AP) until he reaches 14 AP.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.resistances-.sequences.0.steps.3.action: When he casts his spell, hit him 4 times with cheap spells in a single element, then keep going in that element.

mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.rasbouls-min.title: Summoned Rasbouls Mineurs that fully heal
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.rasbouls-min.summary: Silf summons Rasbouls Mineurs (75% resistance except -75% in a random element) able to restore all of an ally's HP, including the Rasboul's. Kill them or keep them at a distance.
mech.silf-le-rasboul-majeur.rasbouls-min.unknownAspects.0: The number of summons per turn is contradictory on the page (one per turn in the boss description, up to 2 per turn in the achievement section).

mech.damadrya.sangsuc.title: Sangsuc: erosion, and the monster is healed if you end your turn next to it
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.summary: From the start of the fight, all characters are under Sangsuc for the whole fight: 20% erosion and 50 life-steal damage at the end of each turn; ending your turn in melee range of a monster heals it for about 150 HP (or gives it a shield if it is already at full HP). Otherwise the guide considers the boss simple.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.unknownAspects.0: No invulnerability or particular resistance is mentioned.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Know that the fight has no particular mechanic: just hit.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The guide states: no particular strategy, the boss is fairly simple.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Do not end your turn in melee range of an enemy monster.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Sangsuc: a character who ends their turn in melee with a monster heals it for about 150; if the monster is at full HP, it gets a shield equal to 100% of its level.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Account for the erosion that builds up at the end of each turn.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Sangsuc, active on all characters for the whole fight, applies 20% erosion and 50 life-steal damage at the end of each character's turn.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Do not stay in line within 2 range of Damadrya.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Urticaire hits all cells in line within 2 range for 100 and removes 50 power for 1 turn.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Beware of the Bourgeons: they rush at you and explode on contact.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Bourgeonnement summons a bud with 20 MP that explodes in melee with you (80 damage).
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.6.action: "On lui pèlera le bourgeon" achievement: kill Damadrya quickly, first.
mech.damadrya.sangsuc.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: No ally may take a Bourgeon explosion more than once, which is hard to avoid given their 20 MP.

mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.title: Rascasse: +50% resistance to the element that hits him (debuffable)
