mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.summary: For 2 turns, each attack received gives the Rat Blanc 50% resistance to the element used, stacking up to 100% (two damage lines are enough). The effect can be debuffed: on cast to prevent it, or at 100% to bring it back to 0%.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.notes.0: Always hitting with the same element makes him immune to that element after two damage lines: vary elements or debuff him.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: They let you remove the Rat Blanc's resistances or stop him from gaining them via Rascasse.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the Aloevée Rat first (except for the "Premier" achievement), and beware of the Capoei Rat in melee.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Aloevée Rat heals; the Capoei Rat can hit quite hard in melee for its level.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.3.action: When the Rat Blanc casts Rascasse, debuff him immediately.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: For 2 turns, each attack taken gives him +50% resistance to the attack's element (5-turn cooldown, debuffable).
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Otherwise, switch elements after each damage line.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: After two lines in one element, he reaches 100% resistance and can no longer be damaged in that element.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If he is already at 100% in an element, debuff him.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: His gained resistances then drop back to 0%.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not heal a character under "Peste Blanche" if they have useful boosts; heal them if they have penalties.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: If the target is healed, they lose all their buffs and debuffs (4-turn state, 6 on critical).
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.7.action: "Premier" achievement: focus the Rat Blanc as fast as possible with debuffs, moving him away from the Aloevée Rat.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The Aloevée Rat, which flees, can be kept busy by giving it a summon to hit.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Guild expedition: place the Chak Rat next to the Rat Blanc before the Chak Rat's turn, 3 turns in a row, without killing all the monsters first.
mech.rat-blanc.rascasse.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: The Rat Blanc must be hit 3 times by his allies to lose his 100% reflect and his damage reduction.

mech.rat-blanc.peste-blanche.title: Peste Blanche: being healed removes all your buffs and debuffs
mech.rat-blanc.peste-blanche.summary: The Rat Blanc applies the "Peste Blanche" state for 4 turns (6 on critical): if the target is healed, they lose all their buffs and debuffs. This removes boosts, but can also be used to remove penalties.

mech.rat-noir.resistance-terre-kackisoig.title: 50% earth resistance and healing via Kackisoigne: play fire or air
mech.rat-noir.resistance-terre-kackisoig.summary: The Rat Noir has 50% earth resistance, and Kackisoigne fully heals the targeted ally if it takes earth or neutral damage. The guide advises against earth in the final room and recommends fire and air, where he has a 20% weakness.
mech.rat-noir.resistance-terre-kackisoig.unknownAspects.0: The guide does not mention an invulnerable state for the classic dungeon (only the expedition section states there is none).

mech.rat-noir.peste-noire.title: Peste Noire: do not heal the target
mech.rat-noir.peste-noire.summary: The target of Peste Noire (6 turns), if healed, takes air damage equal to 50% of the Rat Noir's current HP (75% on critical). Life steal does not count as healing.
mech.rat-noir.peste-noire.notes.0: Healing a character under Peste Noire can deal thousands of damage to them (2,000 if the Rat Noir has 4,000 HP).

mech.rat-noir.kackitu.title: Kackitu: instant death on earth or neutral damage
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.summary: In melee, Kackitu marks the enemies around the Rat Noir for 1 turn: a marked entity that takes earth or neutral damage dies. 7-turn cooldown: stay at a distance, or offer him a summon (ideally one with lock) as a target.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Bring characters who hit fire or air, not earth or neutral.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Rat Noir has 50% earth resistance and a 20% fire and air weakness; Kackisoigne fully heals the targeted ally if it takes earth or neutral damage.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stay at a distance from the Rat Noir.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Kackitu can only be cast in melee (size-1 cross): an entity with this state dies if it takes earth or neutral damage (1 turn, 7-turn cooldown).
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Option: give him a summon (preferably with lock) next to him so he wastes Kackitu on it.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: With a 7-turn cooldown, you are then safe for a good while.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.4.action: If a character has the Kackitu state, keep them away from any source of earth damage that turn.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: They die if they take earth or neutral damage during the state.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Never heal a character under "Peste Noire"; use life steal to heal.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: If healed, they take 50% of the Rat Noir's current HP as air damage (2000 if the Rat has 4,000 HP). Life steal does not count as healing.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not hit a monster under "Kackisoigne" with earth or neutral.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.7.action: "Blitzkrieg" achievement: boost up and start on him with the character who plays right after him, to burn his 4,400 HP in one turn.
mech.rat-noir.kackitu.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Applied poisons take effect before his turn and validate the achievement if they kill him.

mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.title: Étourderie Mortelle: do not use AP under the poison
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.summary: According to the guide (page needing revision), on his first turn the Dragon Cochon poisons all players for 2 turns: using even a single AP makes you lose a huge amount of HP, or even kills you. You must wait or debuff yourself. He only hits in melee (with a push) and removes MP at range.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.turnConditions: Cast on his first turn; 2-turn poison.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.notes.0: His melee attacks push: against an obstacle, pushback damage is added.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.unknownAspects.0: The page is flagged as needing revision and is undated: mechanic possibly outdated.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.unknownAspects.1: No information on a possible invulnerability of the boss in the classic dungeon.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring debuff spells (for example Jouvence, Lait de Bambou).
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: They let you remove the Étourderie Mortelle poison cast on the first turn (page flagged as needing revision).
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.2.action: On the Dragon Cochon's first turn: stop using any AP as soon as Étourderie Mortelle is cast.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: This spell puts a 2-turn poison on all players: using even 1 AP makes you lose a huge amount of HP, or even kills you outright.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Wait for the 2 turns of poison to end, or debuff yourself to play normally again.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Stay out of his melee range and remove his MP.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Dragon Cochon only hits in melee: you can avoid being hit for the whole fight by removing his MP.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: It removes MP, most often all MP, which can prevent you from staying away from him.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If you are next to him, do not stand with your back to an obstacle.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: He pushes when he hits; pushed into an obstacle, you take even more damage. He hits very hard in melee, especially on critical hits.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.7.action: "Faut pas pousser les cochons dans la confiture d'orties" achievement: never be in melee with the Dragon Cochon and kill him first.
mech.dragon-cochon.etourderie-mortelle.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: He is the only one who deals pushback damage; also be careful not to deal any yourself to your allies.

mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.title: Souffle du Koulosse: transformation into a Boufcoul (-100 AP)
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.summary: The Koulosse deals no damage himself. From turn 2, he transforms a character into a Boufcoul (in line, 5 range, with line of sight, up to 3 times per turn): the target loses 100 AP until the Koulosse's next turn and can only move; a targeted summon dies. The effect is debuffable.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.notes.0: His pull (10 cells, in line up to 8 range) can bring you back into his line; it is the only spell usable on turn 1.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring classes with debuff spells (Pandawa, Sadida, Enutrof, Eniripsa…) and vary elements (2 water/fire characters, 2 earth/air).
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Souffle du Koulosse, Calumet de la Paix and Bise du Boufcoul are debuffable. The Koulosse and the Boufcoul are weak to water and fire, the Bouftous des Cavernes to earth and air.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.2.action: During placement: position yourself opposite the Koulosse.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.2.position: Starting cells farthest from the Koulosse
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He has a huge amount of initiative and his pull (10 cells, in line up to 8 range) is the only spell he can use on turn 1.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Throughout the fight: never be in line with him, and hide behind obstacles.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: From turn 2, Souffle du Koulosse (in line, 5 range, line of sight required, 3 times per turn) transforms you into a Boufcoul: -100 AP, you can only move until his next turn.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Keep him at a distance: remove his MP, push him back, and if possible remove his range.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: All his spells have modifiable range: without range, he can only cast his spells in melee and becomes nearly harmless.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If an ally is transformed into a Boufcoul: debuff them, or place them out of the Koulosse's range.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Souffle's effects can be debuffed by an ally. A summon targeted by this spell is killed outright.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If he summons a Boufcoul (critical hit, 10%): focus all attacks on it, or stop it from getting near the Koulosse.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The Boufcoul can make the Koulosse invisible and give him 5 MP (melee spell). If the Koulosse is already invisible, debuff him before he plays.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Kill the Bouftous des Cavernes and the summons, then the Koulosse (safest method).
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The Koulosse deals no damage himself. He can only have 2 summons: if you can tank the 2 summoned Bouftous, leaving them alive prevents a Boufcoul summon. With only water/fire characters, you can focus the Koulosse first.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "À la cool" achievement: no ally may be transformed; killing him before his turn 2 removes all constraints.
mech.koulosse.souffle-boufcoul.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: The Souffle cannot be cast on turn 1; after that, he must never be in line (and in line of sight) with your characters, while also watching out for the 8-range pull.

mech.koulosse.invocation-boufcoul.title: Summons: Bouftous des Cavernes, and a Boufcoul on critical hit
mech.koulosse.invocation-boufcoul.summary: From turn 2, he summons Bouftous des Cavernes (2 summons maximum at the same time). On a critical hit (10%), he summons a Boufcoul, which can make its allies invisible and give them 5 MP: kill it immediately, or debuff the Koulosse if he has become invisible.
mech.koulosse.invocation-boufcoul.notes.0: Leaving 2 summoned Bouftous des Cavernes alive prevents him from summoning more (and therefore a Boufcoul).

mech.koulosse.retrait-po.title: Keep him at a distance, out of his line, or remove his range
mech.koulosse.retrait-po.summary: All his spells have modifiable range and require line of sight: staying at a distance, hidden behind obstacles and out of his line, or removing his range, makes him nearly harmless. Since he has a lot of initiative, position yourself opposite him at the start.
mech.koulosse.retrait-po.unknownAspects.0: The guide mentions no invulnerability or particular resistance for the classic dungeon Koulosse (the 100% resistances concern the guild expedition).

mech.moon.resistances-totems.title: 100% resistance per element, removed by placing the totem on its glyph
mech.moon.resistances-totems.summary: According to the dungeon section (dated 2015), Moon is no longer invulnerable but has 100% resistance in all elements. His summon Darkli Moon summons totems in 4 colours (red fire, green air, blue water, yellow earth) and places a glyph of the same colour. Placing a totem on the glyph of its colour removes Moon's 100% resistance in that element. Totems cannot be moved by pushing: you must hit them in line with a spell of their element to pull them next to the caster.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.notes.0: Hitting the Darkli Moon swaps places with it and gives Moon 100 power.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.notes.1: Totems have 100% resistance in their element: you cannot kill them while pulling them.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.notes.2: Glyph sometimes unreachable (two glyphs on the same cell, glyph on the map edge).
mech.moon.resistances-totems.notes.3: Further up, the page still says "Moon is invulnerable": outdated line, contradicted by the update described right after.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.unknownAspects.0: Dungeon information dated 2015; not rechecked for Dofus 3.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.unknownAspects.1: The page contradicts itself (invulnerable / 100% resistances) before clarifying the update.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.sequences.0.label: Method described by the guide
mech.moon.resistances-totems.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Get in line with a totem and hit it with a spell of its element to pull it (stops at an obstacle).
mech.moon.resistances-totems.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Repeat until the totem is on the glyph of its colour.
mech.moon.resistances-totems.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit Moon with the element in which he lost his resistances.

mech.moon.expedition-totems.title: Guild expedition: 4 totems on their glyphs to remove 200% resistances
mech.moon.expedition-totems.summary: In the guild expedition, Moon has 200% resistance everywhere. He summons 4 totems (500 HP, 100% resistance in their element) and 4 coloured glyphs; all 4 totems must be on their glyph for him to lose his resistances at the start of his next turn. Every 5 turns (turns 6, 11…), he kills and resummons the totems at their starting positions.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.turnConditions: Totems resummoned on turns 6, 11, etc.; 5 turns maximum to place them.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.notes.0: At the end of their turn, each character swaps places with the nearest totem; the totem then places a black glyph that kills (one-shots) characters who start their turn on it.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.unknownAspects.0: Rule specific to the guild expedition.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.sequences.0.label: Strategy recommended by the guide (expedition)
mech.moon.expedition-totems.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the 4 totems on turn 1 (500 HP) to avoid place swaps and black glyphs until turn 6.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the monsters (the Gloutovore as a priority).
mech.moon.expedition-totems.sequences.0.steps.3.action: From turn 6, pull each totem by hitting it in line with its element, then place a character on the glyph so they swap places with the totem at the end of their turn.
mech.moon.expedition-totems.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Once all 4 totems are placed, hit Moon until he dies before the next resummon.

mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.title: No invulnerability; Moissonnage gives him +20% vitality (stacks 5 times)
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.summary: Halouine has no invulnerable state. In melee, his Moissonnage spell gives him 20% vitality (25% on critical) for 3 turns, stacking 5 times and debuffable. When a bonus expires at the start of his turn, he loses those HP; if the bonus is greater than or equal to his remaining HP, he dies before playing.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.notes.0: He can pull 5 cells in line to then use Moissonnage in melee: keep him at a distance and remove his range.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.notes.1: Debuffing him when he has low HP can kill him at the start of his turn.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring debuff spells if possible (Sadida's Puissance Sylvestre, Pandawa's Souillure, Eniripsa's Mot interdit).
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: They remove Moissonnage's vitality bonus and the invulnerability of resurrected monsters. Halouine has no invulnerable state.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Throughout the fight: keep Halouine at a distance, removing his range and MP.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Moissonnage (melee only) gives him +20% vitality for 3 turns, stacking 5 times. Without range, he can no longer use Râttirance (pulls 5 cells in line).
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Focus the Cauchemarakne first, without ending your turn in its glyph.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The glyph removes up to 4 MP; the Cauchemarakne also removes 10% resistance and applies Weakened in melee.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Then kill the Lanverne, ideally before Halouine's turn 3, then finish with the Champêtrouille (the Chauffe-Soutrille before it at loot 6 and above).
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: From turn 3, then every two turns, Halouine resurrects the last allied monster that died: better if it is a low-threat monster.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Finish off each resurrected monster as soon as it loses its invulnerability (or debuff it to finish it immediately).
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: It comes back with 1% of its HP and is invulnerable for only 1 turn (2 on critical); any attack then finishes it.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.6.action: When Halouine is alone: hit him from range, killing the monsters he resurrects every two turns.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: At range, he cannot boost his vitality.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.7.action: If he has boosted himself: remove as much HP as possible, then debuff him when only his bonus vitality remains.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: When a bonus expires at the start of his turn, he loses those HP (about 660 at loot 4); if he has that amount or less, he dies before playing.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "Dernier" achievement: finish Halouine last, as in the strategy above.
mech.halouine.moissonnage-vitalite.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: The guide advises finishing him last anyway.

mech.halouine.plantes-zombies.title: Plantes Zombies: resurrects the last dead monster, invulnerable for 1 turn
mech.halouine.plantes-zombies.summary: From turn 3, then every two turns, Halouine resurrects the last allied monster that died with 1% of its HP. The resurrected monster is invulnerable for 1 turn (2 on critical); this invulnerability can be debuffed.
mech.halouine.plantes-zombies.notes.0: He always resurrects the last allied monster that died: choose which monster to finish last.

mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.title: Invulnerable: kill the 5 Marionnettes for 2 turns of vulnerability
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.summary: The Maître des Pantins is invulnerable for the whole fight and never moves. On turn 1 he summons 5 Marionnettes of different colours; when they are all killed and he is alone, he becomes vulnerable at the start of his turn for 2 turns. He can resummon the missing Marionnettes from turn 5 and then every 4 turns.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.turnConditions: Resummon possible from turn 5 then every 4 turns.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.prerequisites.0: No Marionnette is alive on the map.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.notes.0: Each Marionnette has 200% resistance in the element of its colour (White air, Blue water, Grey neutral, Red fire, Green earth): bring at least one character of another element.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.notes.1: If Marionnettes are missing when he can resummon, he resummons the missing ones: you have to start over.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.notes.2: Start-of-turn effects (poison, glyph) still hit him on the turn he becomes invulnerable again.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.sequences.0.label: Guide strategy
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.sequences.0.steps.1.action: During placement, stand on the cells out of the Marionnettes' reach on turn 1.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Damage all the Marionnettes, then finish them all on the same turn (before turn 5).
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Boost up and set up damage (poisons, summons) on the turn of the last kill.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.invulnerabilite-.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Kill the Maître des Pantins during his 2 turns of vulnerability.

mech.maitre-des-pantins.bunraku.title: Bunraku: remove the state by hitting the targeted ally
mech.maitre-des-pantins.bunraku.summary: Every 3 turns, the Maître des Pantins applies the Bunraku state to a character; at the start of his next turn, a Petite Marionnette (allied to your team but hostile, with your stats) appears next to that character. That character only needs to take damage from an ally to remove the state.
mech.maitre-des-pantins.bunraku.notes.0: The Petite Marionnette hits according to your characteristics and explodes when it dies (50% of its HP as damage): do not end your turn next to it.

mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.title: Invulnerable: control the Pantin and cast "Dénouement" on the Dramak
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.summary: The Dramak is invulnerable for the whole fight. He summons a Pantin on turn 1 and then every 3 turns. By hitting the Pantin down to its 10% HP threshold, the nearest character takes control of it (the Pantin is then invulnerable for 2 turns); that character casts the Pantin's "Dénouement" spell (up to 2 range) on the Dramak, who loses his invulnerability for 2 turns.
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.turnConditions: Pantin summoned on turn 1 then every 3 turns.
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.notes.0: The Dramak cannot be carried, pushed or pulled, and does not lock.
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.sequences.0.label: Method described by the guide
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the Pantin down to 10% of its HP.
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.sequences.0.steps.2.action: The character nearest the Pantin takes control of it.
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.sequences.0.steps.3.action: With the Pantin, cast "Dénouement" on the Dramak (2 range max; the Pantin dies).
mech.dramak.invulnerabilite-pantin.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Hit the Dramak during his 2 turns of vulnerability.

mech.kharnozor.boost-mort-monstres.title: +710 vitality and +10% final damage for each monster that dies
mech.kharnozor.boost-mort-monstres.summary: The Kharnozor is unmovable (infinite). Each time a monster dies, he gains 710 vitality and 10% final damage dealt, with no time limit.
mech.kharnozor.boost-mort-monstres.notes.0: The monsters also have "Don osseux": when one of them dies, the others gain 5% resistance to its element (infinite).
mech.kharnozor.boost-mort-monstres.unknownAspects.0: The page gives no focus order for the boss fight.

mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.title: Hit from 2 range or less: he pulls you and retaliates with "Mort sûre"
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.summary: If you hit the Kharnozor from within a 2-range radius around him, you are pulled next to him and he retaliates with "Mort sûre" (350 earth in melee, plus Unhealable and Gravity for 2 turns on a Deafened target) for each hit received.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.notes.0: Hitting him up close triggers a retaliation on every hit: stay more than 2 range away.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Do not rely on movement spells against him.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Kharnage puts him in the unmovable state (infinite).
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Hit the Kharnozor from more than 2 range, never closer.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Réflexe Primitif: if you hit him within a 2-range area around him, you are pulled next to him and he retaliates with Mort sûre for each hit received.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Avoid being next to him, especially in the Deafened state.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Mort sûre deals 350 earth in melee; on a Deafened target (Cri déchirant: radius-7 circle, -3 AP), it adds Unhealable and Gravity for 2 turns.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Beware of straight lines up to 6 range.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Emplafonnement (in line, 6 range) deals 350 neutral and the Kharnozor pulls himself to the target, pushing it back 6 cells.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Keep in mind that each monster killed makes him stronger.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Each time a monster dies, he gains 710 vitality and +10% final damage, with no time limit.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Special achievement "Les yeux aussi gros que le ventre": end each turn in line of sight of at least one enemy.
mech.kharnozor.reflexe-primitif.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Enemies must have at least one ally in line of sight at the start of their turn; watch out for the map's obstacles.

mech.reine-nyee.resistances-polarisees.title: Polarised resistances: 30% earth, 40% air, -20% fire and water
mech.reine-nyee.resistances-polarisees.summary: The Reine Nyée has no described invulnerability mechanic; her resistances are very polarised (30% earth, 40% air, -20% fire and water), so she is easy to kill with fire/water and hard with earth/air.

mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.title: Trégénaire Eggs and "Dévouées" Trégénaires
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.summary: On turn 1 and then every two turns, she summons an Egg (800 HP) that drains 35 HP from all characters at the start of each turn but heals you for half the damage you deal to it; it hatches into a Trégénaire after 2 turns. The Trégénaire heals the Queen for 130 HP per turn; if the Queen takes damage, the Trégénaires become "Dévouées" (+2 MP, +50 power) and try to explode on contact (200 neutral in an area). The guide considers this mechanic minor.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.turnConditions: Egg summoned on turn 1 then every 2 turns.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.notes.0: Avoid hitting the Queen while a Trégénaire is alive and the Queen is not the target.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.notes.1: Main danger: the Néfileuse puts you in a Cocoon (100 AP/MP removed for 2 turns) and the Arapex one-shots a character in a Cocoon; hitting the cocooned ally removes the state.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: prefer characters who hit water or fire.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Reine Nyée has -20% to water and fire (30% earth, 40% air); the Dardalaine and the Néfileuse are also weak to fire.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stand far from the Dardalaine and the Néfileuse, remove their MP or block them with summons.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Most of their spells can only be cast in line.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Focus the Néfileuse first, from range.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: She pulls (5 cells, in line up to 6 range) then turns you into a Cocoon (-100 AP, -100 MP for 2 turns), leaving the target at the mercy of the Arapex.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.4.action: If an ally is in a Cocoon: deal one damage line to them with a weak spell. Otherwise, keep the Arapex away from them.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Direct damage from an ally removes the Cocoon. The Arapex instantly kills a character in a Cocoon with Exécution (2 range, no line of sight, every 3 turns).
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If the Néfileuse cannot be killed right away, destroy her Webs.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Web (400 HP) places a glyph that removes 100 MP and applies Gravity and Unshakeable; killing it removes these effects.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not hit the Reine Nyée while monsters or Trégénaires are still alive.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: If she takes damage, the Trégénaires become "Dévouées" (+2 MP, +50 power) and come to explode on contact (200 neutral in an area).
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Then kill the Dardalaine, from range only.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: She reflects neutral damage when hit in melee, and Sécrétion acide removes 200 power.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.8.action: If needed, hit the Trégénaire Eggs to heal yourself, without wasting time focusing the Trégénaires.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: You are healed for half the damage dealt to the Egg (800 HP, summoned on turn 1 then every two turns).
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Finish with the Arapex, then the Reine Nyée, keeping your characters spread apart.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: Alone, she is no longer dangerous, but she still hits in an area.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.10.action: Special achievement "On ne peut la Nyée": destroy each Egg (800 HP) before the start of the Queen's next turn.
mech.reine-nyee.oeufs-tregenaires.sequences.0.steps.10.rationale: She summons an Egg on odd turns (1, 3, 5…).

mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.title: Malédiction Pirate: one-shot at 30% HP or less
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.summary: At the start of each turn, the Chouque's passive targets the nearest character who is not "Maudit" and all "Maudit" characters (state applied for 2 turns by his melee sabre hit, not debuffable): minimised random effects and 110 water life-steal damage. A character hit while at 30% of their HP or less is killed outright and a pirate appears on their cell.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.notes.0: His Coup de Sabre Maudit also summons a pirate next to a target at 50% HP or less: stay above 50% HP.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.notes.1: Place a tank character (more than 30% HP) as the nearest non-Maudit character.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring a healer and avoid a team that plays water.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Healing classes are an asset for staying above the HP thresholds; the Chouque has 36% water resistance.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep the Chouque, the Nakunbra and the Ricanif at a distance: no monster within 6 cells of you.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Chouque has 5 MP and can swap places with an allied monster once per turn to get closer.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Put the Gravity state on the Chouque, or on the monsters near him.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: He cannot swap places if he or the targeted monster is under Gravity.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Keep all characters at 50% of their HP or more.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Malédiction Pirate instantly kills a character hit at 30% HP or less; the Nakunbra kills a target at 50% or less in melee, and the Chouque's Coup de Sabre summons a pirate on a target at 50% or less.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Make a "tank" above 30% HP the character nearest the Chouque, and keep your best attackers away.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.5.position: Tank closest to the Chouque, attackers far away
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: At the start of each turn, the passive targets the nearest non-"Maudit" character and all "Maudit" ones: minimised random effects and 110 water damage.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Focus the Ivremor first, without staying in its red glyph.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: It hits from range, stacks intelligence and its glyph deals fire damage at the start of the turn.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Kill the Nakunbra in a single turn, and never end your turn in line with it.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: It gains 1 MP for each damage instance taken; if it starts its turn in line with characters, it can pull them all.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Once all monsters are dead, finish the Chouque from range.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Alone, he can no longer swap places and hits almost only in melee.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Special achievement "Saute-pirate": finish in less than two turns each monster the Chouque swaps places with, ideally before his next turn.
mech.chouque.malediction-pirate.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: He can only swap with one ally per turn and has low initiative; the Chouque is killed last.

mech.chouque.teleportation-spectrale.title: Swaps places with a monster; blocked by the Gravity state
mech.chouque.teleportation-spectrale.summary: Once per turn, the Chouque swaps places with an allied monster (which gains 200 power for 2 turns) to get closer. He cannot do so if he or the targeted monster is in the "Pesanteur" (Gravity) state; once all monsters are dead, he can no longer swap.
mech.chouque.teleportation-spectrale.notes.0: The Chouque has 5 MP: stay more than 6 cells away from any monster if you have no Gravity.

mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.title: 53% resistances except air and fire
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.summary: The page (flagged as needing revision) states that the Abraknyde Ancestral has 53% resistance everywhere except agility (air) and fire, and mainly recommends the fire element because he can inflict an agility penalty.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.notes.0: "Reconstitution Abraknydienne" spell: heals himself for 2,000 HP (5-turn cooldown, from turn 4).
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.notes.1: Summons an Arakne Majeure from turn 3 (5-turn cooldown).
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.unknownAspects.0: Page marked "needs revision": resistance values and spells to be confirmed.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: mainly bring characters who hit fire.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He has 53% resistance everywhere except agility (air) and fire; fire remains the best element because he can inflict an agility penalty (page flagged as needing revision).
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Beware of Branche Paralysante: each AP used under this poison costs HP.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: End-of-turn poison for 3 turns: 28 neutral (56 on critical) per AP used, cast up to 8 range; it is debuffable.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Avoid staying within 2 range of him.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Morsure Sylvestre (up to 2 range) removes 2 AP, deals 200 neutral and removes 100 power for 2 turns.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.action: From turn 3, expect the Arakne Majeure, and from turn 4 a 2,000 HP heal.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Arakne Majeure summon (5-turn cooldown, from turn 3); Reconstitution Abraknydienne heals him for 2,000 HP (5-turn cooldown, from turn 4).
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Special achievement "Distance respectueuse": only hit when no enemy, summons included, is within 3 range.
mech.abraknyde-ancestral.resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Watch out for enemy summons: Champa, Arakne Majeure and Tronknyde.

mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.title: "Prends ma place" passive: swaps with an adjacent character; Gravity/Rooted = damage
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.summary: At the start of each turn, Choudini swaps places with a character or summon next to him (clockwise priority, only one per turn). An adjacent character in the Gravity or Rooted state takes 180 fire damage instead of being swapped; if Choudini himself is under Gravity or Rooted, he deals 180 fire damage to all entities around him.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.notes.0: Fleeing AI and spells with 12 range or more: range removal is of little use.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.notes.1: The guide advises killing the monsters first (each has 60% resistance in one element).
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: vary your team's elements.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Each monster has 60% resistance in one element (Bozoteur neutral, Graboule air, Pirolienne fire, Roukouto water, Tivelo earth).
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.2.action: From turn 1, focus the monsters and ignore Choudini, starting with the one you kill fastest (the guide prefers the Roukouto).
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The monsters are dangerous and easier to kill than Choudini, who has a fleeing AI. The Roukouto removes power.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Under "Reste assis": limit the MP you use, or debuff yourself (for example Lait de Bambou).
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: 2-turn poison: earth damage for each MP used; it hurts a lot from 5 MP used in the turn.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.4.action: If you are next to Choudini, expect him to swap places with you at the start of his turn.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: "Prends ma place": only one swap per turn, clockwise priority. A character under Gravity or Rooted takes 180 fire damage instead of being swapped.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Anticipate Vinriktus: the target swaps places with the nearest ally, whatever the distance.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The swap does not happen if the target is under Gravity or Rooted; an ally in one of these states is skipped in favour of the next one.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not rely on MP or range removal.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The spells of Choudini and the monsters have 12 range or more: they will always be able to reach you.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Choudini alone: have the characters without "Reste assis" chase him; those who have it move by teleportation or hit with long-range spells.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: He is not very tough once caught.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Special achievement "Chacun son tour de magie": if Choudini moves an ally with Détriktus, move that ally before his next turn (swap, pull, push, Pandawa carry) or finish him.
mech.choudini.prends-ma-place.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: An icon above him signals it. Unmovable, unshakeable, rooted characters or characters stuck against a wall avoid the constraint.

mech.choudini.vinriktus-reste-assis.title: Vinriktus (swap between allies) and Reste assis (poison per MP)
mech.choudini.vinriktus-reste-assis.summary: Vinriktus makes the target swap with the nearest ally, whatever the distance (except under Gravity/Rooted states). "Reste assis" applies a 2-turn poison that deals earth damage for each MP used: limit your movement or debuff yourself.

mech.wa-wobot.mekawapace.title: "Mékawapace": +30% resistances for 2 turns (turn 3 then every 5 turns)
mech.wa-wobot.mekawapace.summary: From turn 3, then every 5 turns, the Wa Wobot gains 30% resistance in all elements for 2 turns; this bonus cannot be debuffed. He can be pushed or pulled, but not carried or teleported.

mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.title: Wobots Tamponneurs: bounce the boss between two bumpers to one-shot him
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.summary: The Wa Wobot summons Wobots Tamponneurs (static, 150% resistances) by pulling a target (Mékattwaction) or by transforming the Black Wo Wabbits' Cawottes. When a bumper takes indirect pushback damage, it pushes back everything touching it by 6 cells and the pusher is teleported symmetrically. Two bumpers in line within 6 cells of each other make the pushed entity bounce indefinitely; the Wa Wobot also loses 500 pushback resistance on each bounce, which lets you kill him in one turn.
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.notes.0: The pushing character must not be in the Gravity state (applied by the Black Wo Wabbit) to be teleported symmetrically.
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.notes.1: If the symmetrical teleport is impossible because of an obstacle, all Wobots Tamponneurs in line with that character are one-shot ("Entewwement" effect).
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.notes.2: The guide recommends the common spell Liberation for classes without a push.
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.sequences.0.label: Overall guide strategy
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the monsters first (Black Wo Wabbit then Tiwobot) while the boss summons bumpers.
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place two Wobots Tamponneurs in line within 5 cells of each other, using only push/pull spells.
mech.wa-wobot.wobots-tamponneurs.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Place the Wa Wobot between them then push him into one of the two: he bounces until he dies.

mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.title: "Garde-Bouclier": -50% resistances if hit from range with no free adjacent cell
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.summary: When hit from range, the Mantiscore teleports to an adjacent cell (usually moving away); when hit in melee, he does not move. If all 4 adjacent cells are unavailable, he loses 50% resistances but gains 200 power for 2 turns, and enters the Dérèglement state which prevents him from teleporting for those 2 turns. He has no invulnerable state.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.prerequisites.0: The 4 cells adjacent to the Mantiscore are occupied or unavailable at the time of a ranged hit.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.notes.0: The 200 power bonus comes with the resistance loss: he hits much harder during those 2 turns.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Mort Sûre instantly kills a character hit a second time after the spell's cooldown (blue skull above the targeted character).
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill all the monsters while keeping the Mantiscore at a distance.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He has no invulnerable state; the danger comes from his melee.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit the Mantiscore from range to make him back off.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Garde-Bouclier: when hit from range, he teleports to an adjacent cell, usually away from the attacker. In melee, he does not move.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Do not get hit in melee two turns in a row, especially in the Sursis state.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Darmoclès applies Sursis; on a target already in Sursis, it deals 300 fire and heals him for 600 HP.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.5.action: On turns 1, 6, 11… hide behind map blocks or static summons.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Provocaspion pulls all enemies 3 cells (every 5 turns) and gives him power per enemy next to him.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Option: hit him from range when his 4 adjacent cells are unavailable.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: He then loses 50% resistance but gains 200 power for 2 turns, and the Dérèglement state prevents him from teleporting during those 2 turns.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Once the monsters are dead, focus the Mantiscore until he dies without letting him attack you in melee.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: That way he does not heal.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Special achievement "À portée de dard": kill all the monsters, then attack the Mantiscore in melee only.
mech.mantiscore.garde-bouclier.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: He must take no ranged damage; in melee, Garde-Bouclier does not trigger.

mech.mantiscore.sursis-provocaspion.title: Sursis state (600 HP heal) and pull every 5 turns
mech.mantiscore.sursis-provocaspion.summary: In melee, "Darmoclès" puts the target in the Sursis state; if he hits it again with this spell while it is in Sursis, he deals more and heals himself for 600 HP. "Provocaspion" pulls all enemies 3 cells on turns 1, 6, 11, etc. and gives him power per adjacent enemy.
mech.mantiscore.sursis-provocaspion.notes.0: Hide behind obstacles or static summons on pull turns; avoid being hit in melee two turns in a row.
mech.mantiscore.sursis-provocaspion.notes.1: Kill the Léolhyènes first: their "Mort Sûre" spell can one-shot a character.

mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.title: 200% resistances: 200% weaknesses via the barrels next to him
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.summary: Gourlo has 200% resistance in every element; vulnerabilities are not enough. He summons about one barrel per turn (0 MP, 100% resistance in a random element). A barrel summoned more than 3 turns ago gives, on its turn, 200% weakness in its resistance element to the entities next to it for 3 turns: a single barrel touching Gourlo is enough.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.prerequisites.0: A barrel summoned more than 3 turns ago, of the desired damage element, next to Gourlo.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.notes.0: Gourlo gains 200 agility for each barrel summoned.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.unknownAspects.0: Undated page: values (200%, 3-turn delay) to be rechecked on the current version.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.sequences.0.label: Method described by the guide
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill all the monsters accompanying Gourlo.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep the barrels whose resistance matches your damage element, kill the others.
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Place a barrel next to Gourlo (4 barrels around him, or 1 barrel and the 3 other sides blocked).
mech.gourlo-le-terrible.tonneaux-faibles.sequences.0.steps.4.action: On the barrel's turn, Gourlo receives 200% weakness in that element: hit him with that element.

mech.nelween.etat-debut-combat.title: Start-of-fight state: healing an ally costs them 1 AP or 1 MP
mech.nelween.etat-debut-combat.summary: According to the guide (page needing revision), Nelween casts a state at the very start of the fight that makes an ally you heal lose 1 MP or 1 AP and minimises their random effects. She also removes AP and resistances, steals life and gives spell reflect to her allies.
mech.nelween.etat-debut-combat.unknownAspects.0: The page says it needs revision: very brief boss description, with wording broken across several lines.
mech.nelween.etat-debut-combat.unknownAspects.1: State name, duration and values not specified.

mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.title: "Peau de Silex": 70% resistances around him; summon every 3 turns
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.summary: The guide (undated) lists the "Peau de Silex" spell, which gives 70% resistances to the Craqueleur Légendaire and to monsters within 2 range of him. He summons a dungeon monster on turn 1 and then every 3 turns.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.unknownAspects.0: Undated page; old spell list ("Peau de Granite: ???").
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.unknownAspects.1: Duration of "Peau de Silex" and casting conditions not given.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.unknownAspects.2: The guild expedition section ("Couche Rocailleuse") does not concern the classic dungeon and is not included.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Identify the monsters within 2 range of the Craqueleur Légendaire.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Peau de Silex gives them, as well as him, 70% resistances.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Pierre Étourdissante (melee only) hits fire and removes 100 AP for 1 turn.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not stay within 2 range of him.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Frappe du Craqueleur Légendaire hits in a 2-range-radius circle, allies and enemies alike.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Expect a new summon on turn 1 and then every 3 turns.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Invocation Montagnarde summons a dungeon monster. Peau de Topaze also reduces the damage taken by one of his allies by 1,000 for 3 turns.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Special achievement "De véritables craqu'": while an enemy summon is alive, hit only it; or kill the Craqueleur Légendaire before he plays.
mech.craqueleur-legendaire.peau-de-silex.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: No enemy may take damage while enemy summons are alive; killing him before his first turn removes the constraint (undated page).

mech.draegnerys.audacieux-intrepide.title: "Audacieux" (turn 1) then "Intrépide" (turn 4) states on all monsters
mech.draegnerys.audacieux-intrepide.summary: In this dungeon, all monsters grow stronger over the turns: "Audacieux" state on turn 1 (+3 AP, +2 MP, +50 power, +200 vitality), then "Intrépide" on turn 4 (+6 AP, +4 MP, +100 power, +200 vitality, change of appearance), both infinite; some spells gain effects under Intrépide.
mech.draegnerys.audacieux-intrepide.turnConditions: Audacieux from turn 1; Intrépide from turn 4 onwards.
mech.draegnerys.audacieux-intrepide.unknownAspects.0: The guide does not explicitly say whether Draegnerys himself receives these states (it says "all monsters").

mech.draegnerys.pepiniere.title: "Pépinière": 2 Dragoeufs on turn 1, then 1 every 2 turns
mech.draegnerys.pepiniere.summary: Draegnerys summons two Dragoeufs from the dungeon on turn 1, then one Dragoeuf every 2 turns; he can also buff an ally (Somatotropine: +2 AP, +2 MP, vitality and power for 2 turns).
mech.draegnerys.pepiniere.unknownAspects.0: No "Fight principle" section and no strategy for the boss on the page.

mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.title: "Awmuwe Woyale": -30% damage taken (and a shield if he is alone)
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.summary: Every 5 turns, the Wa Wabbit and the nearest allied monster reduce damage taken by 30% for 2 turns (can be debuffed); when he is the only one alive, he also gains a shield worth 200% of his level. He has strong neutral, earth and fire resistances and is weak to water and air; he has a lot of HP and a fleeing AI.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: if possible, bring at least one character who hits with air or water.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Wa Wabbit is weak to water and air, and has strong neutral, earth and fire resistances. He has a lot of HP.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Spread your characters apart from each other.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Grand Pa Wabbits hit and hinder in a size-2 circle.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Ignore the Wa Wabbit at the start of the fight.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: He has a fleeing AI, stays at the back of the map and only deals heavy damage on critical hits (240 neutral).
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Focus the Wo Wabbit first, then the Grand Pa Wabbits one after the other.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Wo Wabbit has less HP and his summons get in the way; the Grand Pas (about 1,200 HP) take longer to kill.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Debuff yourselves after "Abrutissement" (for example Mot de Jouvence, Lait de Bambou).
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: This spell removes 150 power from everyone for 1 turn, every 3 turns.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not start or end your turn in a Cawotte Woyale's glyph.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: You become Insoignable (unhealable) for 2 turns; each Cawotte also gives the Wa Wabbit +10% critical.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Once all the monsters are dead, attack the Wa Wabbit.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: When alone he gains effects (Awmuwe Woyale shield, stronger Abrutissement), but he is no longer dangerous enough; it takes a few turns because of his HP.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Special challenge "Mené à la cawotte": never hit the Cawotte; if possible kill the Wo Wabbit before the Wa Wabbit's first turn, then put everything on him.
mech.wa-wabbit.awmuwe-woyale.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: He summons his Cawotte on turn 1, and as long as it is present, only the Wa Wabbit may take damage. He plays after the Grand Pa Wabbits.

mech.wa-wabbit.cawotte-abrutissement.title: Cawotte Woyale (Insoignable glyph, +10% critical) and Abrutissement
mech.wa-wabbit.cawotte-abrutissement.summary: His Cawotte Woyale places a glyph that heals monsters and makes characters who start or end their turn in it Insoignable (unhealable) for 2 turns; each Cawotte gives him +10% critical (his only damage spell hits much harder on a critical). Every 3 turns, "Abrutissement" removes 150 power from everyone for 1 turn (300 plus water damage if he is alone); the malus can be debuffed.
mech.wa-wabbit.cawotte-abrutissement.notes.0: The guide advises ignoring the Wa Wabbit and killing the Wo Wabbit first, then the Grand Pa Wabbits, and debuffing the Abrutissement malus.

mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.title: 94% air resistance, 12% weakness elsewhere; Blotection
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.summary: Like every Royal Blop, he has 94% resistance in his own element (air) and 12% weakness in all the others; he can give an ally 100% air resistance for 3 turns (Blotection) and summons a random Blop from the dungeon (Blovocation). Bring characters who hit in other elements.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.notes.0: If he summons a Gloutoblop (about 4.5%), never let it reach melee: it one-shots (it can also devour its allies).
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.notes.1: The fight gives a piece of the key to the Antre du Blop Multicolore Royal.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring at least 2 characters of different elements, and do not rely on air.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Blop Coco Royal has 94% air resistance and 12% weakness in all other elements.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.2.action: On turn 1: if possible kill the Blop Coco before it plays; otherwise let it flee and kill it at the end.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Blops have a lot of range and a fleeing AI, but 50% weakness in the opposite element.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not end your turn on the white glyphs.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Blyphe: 60 damage and 1 MP lost for anyone who ends their turn on it.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Then kill the Blopignon, then the Tronkoblop.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Blopignon hits at range, deals the most damage and has little HP; the Tronkoblop heals its allies.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If he summons a Gloutoblop, never let it reach you in melee.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Gloutoblop kills outright in melee and grows with every entity it eats (about a 4.5% chance).
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The targeted monster gains 100% air resistance for 3 turns (6 on a critical).
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Focus the Blop Coco Royal until it dies, killing its Tronkoblop, Blopignon or Gloutoblop summons and ignoring the others.
mech.blop-coco-royal.resistance-element.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: It hits at short range and is not very dangerous. Finish with the Blop if it is still alive.

mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Blyphe: 60 damage and 1 MP lost for anyone who ends their turn on it.
mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Then kill the Blopignon, then the Tronkoblop.
mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Blopignon hits at range, deals the most damage and has little HP; the Tronkoblop heals its allies.
mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.5.action: If he summons a Gloutoblop, never let it reach you in melee.
mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Gloutoblop kills outright in melee and grows with every entity it eats (about a 4.5% chance).
mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The targeted monster gains 100% water resistance for 3 turns (6 on a critical).

mech.blop-indigo-royal.resistance-elemen.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: It hits at short range and is not very dangerous. Finish with the Blop if it is still alive.

mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.title: 10% water weakness, 70% elsewhere; "Tartinade" glyphs at -15%
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.summary: Each Royal Jelly has 10% weakness in its own element (water for this one) and 70% resistance in the others. From turn 2, the jellies place glyphs of their colour (Tartinade): a jelly of another colour that starts its turn in one loses 15% resistance in that element for 3 turns, stackable. Place the resistant Royal Jellies in the glyph matching the colour of your attack element.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.notes.0: Each Royal Jelly summons a jelly on turn 1 (4 more enemies if you face all 4).
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.notes.1: Jellies have no pushback resistance: pushback damage is an alternative.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: avoid a single-element team; hit the Gelée Royale Bleuet with water.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: It has 10% water weakness and 70% resistance in the other elements.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.2.action: On turn 1: expect a Gelée Bleuet to be summoned next to it.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Each Royal Jelly summons a Jelly on turn 1 (summoned jellies have 20% less HP).
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Without a water character, compare with your spells that hit in water even outside your element.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Against 10% weakness, they can deal more damage than your own-element spells against 70% resistance.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.4.action: From turn 2: place the Gelée Royale Bleuet in the glyph of a jelly whose colour matches your attack element.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Tartinade: a jelly of another colour that starts its turn in this glyph loses 15% resistance in that element for 3 turns, stackable.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Do not start your turn in the blue glyph.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: A character who starts their turn there takes 65 water damage; a Bleuet jelly is healed for 20 HP there.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If your damage is low, push it against an obstacle to deal pushback damage.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Against all 4 Royal Jellies: each character handles the one matching their element, then everyone focuses the last one.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: With 3 or more elements, this is the guide's strategy. Royale Bleuet Os also removes 2 AP from the target.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Special challenge "Privé de dessert": never touch the summons, not even with area spells or pushback.
mech.gelee-royale-bleuet.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Their glyphs are then used to strip more resistance from the Royal Jellies.

mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Each Royal Jelly has 10% weakness in its own element (fire for the Fraise) and 70% resistance in the others; the guide advises against playing the whole team in the same element.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Start of the fight: expect a Gelée Fraise to be summoned on turn 1.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Each Royal Jelly summons a Jelly on turn 1 (Invocation de Gelée Fraise, 5-turn cooldown); the main danger of the fight is the number of enemies.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If you have fire: hit the Gelée Royale Fraise directly with fire.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: With good elemental coverage there is no need to kill the summons: thanks to their -10% resistances, the Royal Jellies go down very quickly. mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Without fire: kill the summons first, then place the Gelée Royale Fraise in the glyph (Tartinade) matching the colour of your attack element.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: From turn 2, the jellies place glyphs of their colour; a jelly of another colour that starts its turn in one loses 15% resistance in that element for 3 turns, stackable.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Do not stay in the Fraise's red glyph and do not let it start its turn there.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Gelée Royale Fraise's red glyph deals 65 fire to characters who start their turn in it and heals Fraise Jellies that start theirs in it for 65 HP.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.6.action: If it is left alone and you lack damage: put it against an obstacle and deal pushback damage to it.
mech.gelee-royale-fraise.resistances-tar.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Jellies have no pushback resistance; you must first place the Jelly against an obstacle.

mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.title: "Bénédiction Moonesque": nearby allies healed for 50% of damage
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.summary: From the start of the fight, all monsters receive Bénédiction Moonesque: when one takes damage, its allies in a size-2 circle around it are healed for 50% of that damage. The guide advises focusing the monsters one by one and keeping them more than 2 cells apart.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Stay at a distance from the Kanniboul Ebil and out of his lines.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He only hits in a line (Bouboule, up to 6 modifiable range, 1 cast per turn): far from him he can do nothing and nobody gets the Maudit state.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Ignore the Poupée Aycetroy and stay away from it.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He resummons it the next turn if it dies; it hits in a size-2 circle around itself at the end of every turn (45 neutral, +50 power per turn). On turn 1 it can swap places with a character, then not again before turn 5.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Never hit the Poupée while an ally is Maudit.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: All damage taken by the Poupée is sent back to the Maudit character (except the hit that finishes it off).
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Kill the Kanniboul Sarbak first, or reduce its range.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: It is the most dangerous: Sarbakanniboul applies a poison that deals damage based on the AP used. While poisoned, use few AP.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.5.action: With 6 or more characters: focus the Kanniboul Eths first while staying at range.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: In melee, Éternuement Collatéral makes its target intercept all damage taken by the Kanniboul Eth (debuff the Kanniboul Eth, not the character).
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Focus the monsters one by one and do not hit a monster within 2 cells of another.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Bénédiction Moonesque: allies in a size-2 circle around the monster hit are healed for 50% of the damage taken.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Then kill the Kanniboul Jav, and the Kanniboul Tam last.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The Jav is more dangerous at range than the Ark; the Tam only hits in an area around itself.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Once all the monsters are dead, focus the Kanniboul Ebil, preferably with air.
mech.kanniboul-ebil.benediction-moonesqu.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: He has little HP, 30% earth resistance and 10% air weakness.

mech.kanniboul-ebil.poupee-maudit.title: Poupée Aycetroy and "Maudit" state (damage sent back)
mech.kanniboul-ebil.poupee-maudit.summary: The Kanniboul Ebil summons the Poupée Aycetroy on turn 1 and resummons it the next turn if it dies (only one at a time). It gains 50 power per turn and hits around itself, also hurting itself. The character hit by "Bouboule" enters the Maudit state: all damage taken by the Poupée is sent back to them (except the hit that finishes it off).
mech.kanniboul-ebil.poupee-maudit.notes.0: Ignore the Poupée and stay out of the Kanniboul Ebil's lines (he only hits in a line).
mech.kanniboul-ebil.poupee-maudit.notes.1: Kanniboul Eth (loot 6+): its melee target intercepts all the damage it takes; debuff the Eth, not the target.

mech.mawabouaino.fondu-dechaine.title: "Fondu Déchaîné": Chocomatose glyphs when enemies die
mech.mawabouaino.fondu-dechaine.summary: When an enemy dies, a dark red glyph appears on its cell; walking through it (ally or enemy) gives the Chocomatose state: +300 power and +3 AP for 2 turns (does not stack). While a player is in Chocomatose, all monsters except the boss gain "Mowfal", which teleports them next to an enemy anywhere. When the boss dies, the glyphs and the state disappear.
mech.mawabouaino.fondu-dechaine.unknownAspects.0: No "Fight principle" section and no dedicated boss strategy on the page.

mech.bworkette.resistances.title: Very resistant; weak point water (18%), avoid fire (48%)
mech.bworkette.resistances.summary: The Bworkette is a tank with high resistances in all elements for her level. Her lowest resistance is water (18%); she has 48% in fire. The guide advises at least one water character and avoiding fire characters.
mech.bworkette.resistances.notes.0: She has only 10 MP dodge: MP reduction lets you keep her at a distance.

mech.bworkette.reconstitution.title: Heals 50% of her HP (Reconstitution Bwork) every 6 turns
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.summary: The Bworkette heals herself for 100 HP twice per turn via Mot Croisé (which also hits in a size-3 cross area) and for half of her max HP once every 6 turns via Reconstitution Bwork. The guide advises killing her last, leaving a low-HP monster alive so she wastes her Reconstitution on it, then killing her within the following 6 turns (erosion / heal reduction if damage is lacking).
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.notes.0: Mot Croisé reaches up to 9 range thanks to its size-3 cross area: spread your characters out.
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.sequences.0.label: Strategy described by the guide
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill the Bwork Mage and Bwork Archer first while keeping the Bworkette at a distance, with characters spread out.
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Leave one monster on low HP so she uses Reconstitution Bwork on it.
mech.bworkette.reconstitution.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Finish off that monster, then kill the Bworkette within the 6-turn cooldown.

mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.title: The more HP it loses, the harder it hits (Tchaiste)
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.summary: Every turn, the Chest casts Tchaiste: earth damage equal to 30% of its missing HP in a size-4 inverted circle (characters within 3 range are not hit) and +30 damage for its allies in the area. So do not damage it until it is the target: kill the monsters first, then kill it in a single turn right after its turn, or stand within 3 range while blocking it in with summons.
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.notes.0: Fleeing AI: it backs off after Tchaiste and only moves forward if it can reach someone in melee.
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.sequences.0.label: Strategy described by the guide
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Ignore the Chest (do not touch it, not even with area spells) and kill the monsters.
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Never end your turn within 4 range of it (it has 3 MP and hits in melee with AP steal).
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.degats-pv-manq.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Once it is alone, buff up and kill it between two of its turns, or stand within 3 range while blocking it.

mech.coffre-des-forgerons.expedition-inv.title: Guild expedition: invulnerable while monsters are alive
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.expedition-inv.summary: In the guild expedition only, the Chest is invulnerable until all monsters are dead (it loses the state at the end of its next turn). Killing a monster makes it teleport onto the character and kill them in one hit; to avoid this, leave the monsters at 10% HP or less at the start of its turn: it kills them itself (and gains 1 MP, 5% damage and 10% size per monster).
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.expedition-inv.expectedStateChange: Invulnerability removed at the end of the Chest's turn following the death of the last monster.
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.expedition-inv.prerequisites.0: Applies only to the guild expedition, not the normal dungeon.
mech.coffre-des-forgerons.expedition-inv.unknownAspects.0: The rest of the expedition section (tips, spells) was not included.

mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.title: One-shots in melee under Coraillement Magistral
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.summary: Under Coraillement Magistral (+12 AP and +400 power for 4 turns, but he loses his 3 MP at the end of the turn), the Corailleur can cast Frappe de Corail Magistrale (16 AP), which kills any character in melee, even an invulnerable one. At range he is harmless: never go next to him, and kill him from range after the monsters.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.notes.0: Even an invulnerable character is killed; the guide only mentions an AI bug on turn 1 (he does not use the spell on an invulnerable character in melee).
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.notes.1: Coraillement lasts 4 turns with a 5-turn cooldown: one turn out of five he gets his MP back but cannot one-shot.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Placement phase: place all characters far from the Corailleur Magistral.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He is completely harmless at range and only dangerous in melee.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Never go next to the Corailleur Magistral.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Under Coraillement Magistral (+12 AP, +400 power for 4 turns), Frappe de Corail Magistrale (16 AP) deals 20,000 air in melee and kills even an invulnerable character.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Their spell Décapsulage reduces a character's resistances by 100% for 2 turns; this malus can be debuffed (Mot de Jouvence, Lait de Bambou…).
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Then kill the Crustorails and the Corailleur (any order).
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Corailleur Magistral has a lot of HP (2000 to 2900): the guide advises dealing with the monsters first.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Keep your distance even when he gets his MP back.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Coraillement Magistral makes him lose his 3 MP for 4 turns, but with its 5-turn cooldown he has one turn with his MP (without being able to use his one-shot spell).
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Once the monsters are dead, kill him from range, preferably with earth or air.
mech.corailleur-magistral.frappe-os.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: He has very low resistances and a weakness to earth and air.

mech.corailleur-magistral.resistances.title: Low resistances, weak to earth and air
mech.corailleur-magistral.resistances.summary: Unlike the other bosses of Otomai Island, he does not have at least 100% resistance everywhere: he has very low resistances and a weakness to earth and air, but a lot of HP (2000 to 2900).

mech.shin-larve.resistances.title: Resistant to neutral/earth/fire, large water and air weaknesses
mech.shin-larve.resistances.summary: The Shin Larve has good neutral, earth and fire resistances but strong water and air weaknesses; with 2000 to 2900 HP, she is hard to kill without a water or air character.

mech.shin-larve.enlisement.title: Enlisement: +4 AP but −6 MP for everyone (turn 2 then every 3 turns)
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.summary: On turn 2 and then every 3 turns, Enlisement removes 6 MP from characters and gives 4 AP to all entities for one turn. The guide advises positioning yourself the turn before (turns 1, 4, 7...) with range and line of sight to make use of these AP. She also summons a random larva on even turns; the Larve Saphir, which heals a lot, must be killed first.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.turnConditions: Enlisement on turn 2 then every 3 turns; summon on even turns from turn 2.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.notes.0: She has only 2 MP and only hits in melee.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: if possible, bring water or air characters.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Shin Larve has good neutral, earth and fire resistances but large water and air weaknesses, with 2000 to 2900 HP.
