mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Turn 1: buff up, then position yourself with range and line of sight on the next turn's target, away from the larvae.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: On turn 2, Enlisement removes 6 MP from characters and gives 4 AP to all entities for one turn: you will not be able to move.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Turn 2: use the bonus AP for maximum damage.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: With several water/air characters, the Shin Larve can be killed on turn 2; otherwise, use it to kill as many larvae as possible.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.4.action: With no (or only one) water/air character: kill the monsters first, the Larve Saphir as a priority.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: The Larve Saphir can heal one of its allies for up to 200 per turn. With 4 characters, hit the nearest larva.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.5.action: On even turns, watch the summon: if it is a Larve Saphir, kill it quickly.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Shin Larve summons a random larva on every even turn (2, 4, 6…). Exception: if you are finishing off the Shin Larve on turn 2, focus on her.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Reposition on turns 1, 4, 7… before each Enlisement.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: She casts Enlisement on turn 2 and then every 3 turns.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Once the monsters are dead, hit the Shin Larve while staying out of her melee range.
mech.shin-larve.enlisement.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: She has only 2 MP and only hits in melee (Déglutition: 120 neutral, -3 AP, pushes back 4 cells).

mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.title: 80% resistances, reduced by monster deaths (Kwayauté) and pushback
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.summary: The Kwakwa has 80% resistance in all elements. Each monster or summon that dies permanently removes 40% resistance in that monster's element, but gives him 40 pushback damage (stackable). In addition, like all monsters of the area (Kwapoussée), each instance of pushback damage he takes removes 10% resistance in all elements for 3 turns and gives him 10 pushback damage. Strategy: kill the Kwak and the Bwak of the element you hit with (80% removed), then focus the Kwakwa.
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.notes.0: His pushback damage increases with each death: avoid being in line with him and moving along the walls (Kwakoukas Kwayal pushes back 4 cells).
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.sequences.0.label: Strategy described by the guide
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Start far from the Kwakwa (fleeing AI: he backs off if he cannot hit).
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the Kwak and the summoned Bwak of your chosen attack element (with characters of another element if possible).
mech.kwakwa.kwayaute.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit the Kwakwa in that element; use pushback to remove an extra 10% resistance.

mech.kwakwa.kwarmee.title: Summons 4 Bwaks from the start, resummoned only when all are dead
mech.kwakwa.kwarmee.summary: From the start of the fight, the Kwakwa summons 4 Bwaks (one per element, 20% less HP); he can only resummon them once all 4 are dead (5-turn cooldown).

mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.title: Immobile (0 MP), no invulnerability, summons one Kipik per turn
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.summary: The Sapik has 0 MP, cannot be moved and has no invulnerable state. He summons a Kipik de Sapik at the start of each turn (5 at most) and hits with water at infinite range with line of sight. The guide advises killing the monsters out of his line of sight (Kwakus and Kitsou Nakwatus first, the latter being able to give him 2 MP), killing the Kipiks as they appear, then finishing him without going into melee.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.notes.0: The Kitsou Nakwatus gives 2 MP every 3 turns to its allies, including the Sapik.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Position yourself and play out of the Sapik's line of sight.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He has 0 MP and cannot be moved; his spell Enguirlandage hits at infinite range but needs line of sight.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the Kwakus and the Kitsou Nakwatus first, preferably with fire.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: They are the most dangerous; the Kitsou Nakwatus gives 2 MP every 3 turns to its allies, and so to the Sapik. All monsters have fire weaknesses (100% for the Kwakus).
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill each Kipik de Sapik as soon as it is summoned.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: He summons a Kipik at the start of each of his turns (5 at most): the longer the fight lasts, the more they block your movement and hit you.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Once the monsters are dead, hit the Sapik without going into melee.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: He has no invulnerable state; in melee, Câlin Kipik deals 80 air in a cross and removes 10 dodge.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.5.action: When low on HP: hide behind an obstacle or a summon.
mech.sapik.immobile-invocations.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Out of his line of sight, he cannot hit you at range.

mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.title: Prysmatic weakness: −10% resistances to him and his target
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.summary: The Rakoopeur has no invulnerable state. Each of his multi-element hits removes 10% resistance in all elements from his target and himself for 2 turns (stacks 3 times); on a critical hit the target loses 15% and he loses nothing. He can also teleport next to an ally to give it a shield (Camaraderie, from turn 1). The guide advises killing him last (Timangouste, Buffalourd then Grolours first) and ignoring the shielded monster.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Order recommended by the guide: Timangouste, Buffalourd, Grolours, then the Rakoopeur last.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Leave alone the monster that receives the Camaraderie shield and hit the others.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: On the first turn, the Rakoopeur teleports next to an ally and gives it a shield worth 200% of his level for 2 turns; it loses it on its own.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Then kill the Buffalourd, then the Grolours, avoiding a monster that shares damage.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The Grolours' Empressement shares damage between its allies in a size-1 cross: focus a monster not affected by the sharing.
mech.rakoopeur.faiblesse-prysmatique.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: He has no invulnerable state. His multi-element hits (Serpe boomerang up to 4 range, Serpette up to 6 range) remove 10% resistance from his target and himself for 2 turns, stacking 3 times.

mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.title: No special mechanic; random spell that can summon a monster
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.summary: The Kankreblath has no special mechanic (34% earth resistance, 26% water). His spell "Sfvc%$*$R ?" (from turn 2, 3-turn cooldown) makes him invisible, teleports him or summons a random monster from the area within 6 range. The guide advises killing the monsters first (Pyrasite as a priority), then the boss, killing his summons as soon as they appear.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: if possible, bring one or two water characters.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: 3 monsters in the dungeon have water weaknesses and the other two have 0%; only the Kankreblath resists water (26%) and earth (34%).
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stay at a distance from all enemies.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: All monsters hit at short range or in melee; the Kankreblath hits in areas (size-6 line, size-3 circle).
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill the Pyrasite first, preferably with water.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: It is the most dangerous monster (damage, poison, MP and power buff for its allies); it has 20% water weakness.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.4.action: From turn 2, immediately kill any monster summoned by the Kankreblath if it is dangerous or close.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Sfvc%$*$R ? (from turn 2, 3-turn cooldown) has a 1 in 3 chance of summoning a random monster from the area within 6 range, often near you.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Continue with the Céglumen and the Sakarien, then the Cafarcher and finally the Mirgrillon.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The Cafarcher hits up to 6 range, whereas the Mirgrillon only hits in melee.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Finish with the Kankreblath, killing his summons as soon as they appear.
mech.kankreblath.sort-aleatoire.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: He has no special mechanic; his random spell can also make him invisible or teleport him.

mech.boostache.lourd-enracine.title: Cannot be moved (Lourd and Enraciné) and resummons dead monsters
mech.boostache.lourd-enracine.summary: According to the old (undated) page, the Boostache is in the Lourd and Enraciné states for the whole fight (cannot be carried or pushed) and can resummon a dead monster from the dungeon (L'Enfer des Zombies) every turn; he also summons Ashi-magari that remove 100 MP in melee.
mech.boostache.lourd-enracine.unknownAspects.0: Undated page in the old format: spells may have changed since.
mech.boostache.lourd-enracine.unknownAspects.1: No overall strategy and no resistance/invulnerability information given.

mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.title: No invulnerability; −2 MP and −6 range for the whole team on turn 1, then every 4 turns
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.summary: The Scarabosse Doré has neither an invulnerable state nor any particular mechanic. On the first turn and then every 4 turns, Brouillard Empoisonné removes 2 MP and 6 range from all characters for one turn; he heals his allies (every 3 turns) and summons a Scarafeuille Immature every 5 turns. He has 24% resistance everywhere: kill him last, after the Scarafeuilles (exploiting their weakness element) and the Immatures.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.turnConditions: Brouillard Empoisonné on turn 1, then every 4 turns.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: build a team that hits in different elements.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Each Scarafeuille has 100% resistance in its own element and 50% weakness in the opposite element.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stay as far from the enemies as possible.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Most enemy spells only hit at short range. On turn 1 and then every 4 turns, Brouillard Empoisonné removes 2 MP and 6 range from the whole team for one turn.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If you have the damage: kill the Scarafeuille Noir before its 2nd turn.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: It can only make itself (and its allies) invisible from turn 2.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Kill the Scarafeuilles, starting with those weak to your element.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Use their 50% weakness to kill them quickly.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Kill the Flammèches and the Scarafeuilles Immatures as soon as they are summoned.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Flammèches have very little HP; the Scarabosse summons an Immature every 5 turns, which turns into a Scarafeuille after 2 turns.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Keep the Scarabosse Doré for last and keep killing his summons.
mech.scarabosse-dore.brouillard.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: He has no invulnerable state, but a lot of HP and 24% resistance everywhere, and heals himself every 3 turns.

mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.title: Expedition: invulnerable unless he starts his turn on a black glyph
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.summary: In the guild expedition, the Chafer Rönin is invulnerable; he loses this state for 2 turns if he starts his turn on one of the 8 fixed black glyphs placed at the start of the fight. All entities have a 1% HP threshold that turns them into an invulnerable "Tas d'Os"; you win when all opponents are Tas d'Os placed in a glyph.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.vulnerabilityDuration: 2 turns without invulnerability after starting his turn on a black glyph.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.prerequisites.0: Guild expedition version of the fight (not the classic dungeon).
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.notes.0: Each attack on a Tas d'Os pulls it one cell towards the attacker: handy for placing it in a glyph.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.notes.1: A character in Tas d'Os dies at the start of their turn, unless they have been placed in a black glyph (they then come back with 50% HP).
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.notes.2: The Rib can turn you directly into a Tas d'Os with pushback damage.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Guild expedition, before entering: avoid playing air.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: All enemies except the Chafer Rönin have 50% air resistance or more, and most have weaknesses in the other elements.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Locate the 8 black glyphs placed at the start of the fight.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Their positions are fixed and identical on every attempt.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit each monster down to its 1% HP threshold.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: At this threshold, the entity becomes an invulnerable "Tas d'Os" that loses 100 AP and MP; a monster returns to normal and heals 100% at the end of its 2nd turn as a Tas d'Os.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Immediately place each enemy Tas d'Os in a black glyph (hitting it to pull it if needed).
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: In a glyph, it cannot be moved and skips all its turns. Each attack on a Tas d'Os pulls it one cell towards the attacker.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Make the Chafer Rönin start his turn on a black glyph.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He is invulnerable; if he starts his turn in a black glyph, he loses his invulnerability for 2 turns.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Find the real Chafer Rönin among his illusions by hitting them.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: At the end of each turn from turn 2, he creates illusions; hitting the right one makes them all disappear.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.7.action: If an ally becomes a Tas d'Os: place them in a black glyph before the start of their turn.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Otherwise they die at the start of their next turn; in the glyph, they return to normal and heal 50% of their HP.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Do not stay in melee with the Rib.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: If it deals pushback damage to you with Rip (1 cell), it removes 99% of your HP and turns you into a Tas d'Os.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.9.action: Win by putting all opponents as Tas d'Os in a glyph.
mech.chafer-ronin.expedition-invulnerabi.sequences.0.steps.9.rationale: The fight ends in your victory when all opponents are Tas d'Os in a glyph.

mech.chafer-ronin.bunshin-illusions.title: Bunshin: 4 illusions to find
mech.chafer-ronin.bunshin-illusions.summary: From turn 2, the Chafer Rönin creates 4 illusions of himself around him (this spell makes him skip his turn). Any attempt to cast a damage spell on an illusion makes it disappear; hitting the real one makes all the illusions disappear. Area spells or an end-of-turn poison (which reveals him) make the search easier.
mech.chafer-ronin.bunshin-illusions.notes.0: The guide considers the Chafer Draugrs (Hel glyph, 5-cell pushback) to be the real threat of the classic dungeon: kill them first.

mech.batofu.blocage.title: When blocked, the Batofu can no longer summon
mech.batofu.blocage.summary: The Batofu has a fleeing AI and a lot of MP; he summons Tofus (Tofu Noir, Tofu Fugace). If he is blocked (surrounded or stuck in a corner), he just hits and no longer summons. He strongly resists air (36%): favour fire and water.
mech.batofu.blocage.notes.0: The Tofus Fugaces die on their own at the end of their second turn: no need to kill them.
mech.batofu.blocage.notes.1: Kill the Tofukaz before its turn 2 (area invisibility); keep the Tofu Ventripotent (weak to water) for last.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before entering: bring at least one water character, and preferably fire and water rather than air.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Batofu has 36% air resistance; the very resistant Tofu Ventripotent has a big water weakness (-21%).
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill the Tofukaz before the start of its turn 2.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: On turn 2, it can make itself and its allies in a size-2 circle invisible.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Back off rather than advance to lure the Tofus.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: They have a lot of MP and a fleeing AI: if you back off, they use their MP to come to you and are easier to focus.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.4.action: As soon as possible, block the Batofu in a corner of the map (ideally with 2 summons) or surround him.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: When blocked, he only hits and can no longer summon; you can then focus him as soon as the Tofukaz is dead.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Then kill the Tofoune (and with more than 4: the Tofu Mutant and the Tofu Noir).
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Focus order recommended by the guide.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Do not kill the Tofus Fugaces; kill the summoned Tofus Noirs if the fight drags on.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The Tofus Fugaces die on their own at the end of their 2nd turn; the Tofus Noirs can erode.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Kill the Batofu before the Tofu Ventripotent, which should be kept for last.
mech.batofu.blocage.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: The Batofu will be quicker to kill; only hit the Tofu Ventripotent if nothing else is in range.

mech.bouftou-royal.expedition-soin-insoi.title: Expedition: full heal every turn, do not make him unhealable
mech.bouftou-royal.expedition-soin-insoi.summary: In the guild expedition, the Bouftou Royal heals 100% of his HP at the start of every turn; if he is put in the unhealable state, he removes that state and gains 1,000 power (infinite). So you must erode him or kill him in one turn.
mech.bouftou-royal.expedition-soin-insoi.prerequisites.0: Guild expedition version of the fight (not the classic dungeon).
mech.bouftou-royal.expedition-soin-insoi.notes.0: "Frisette" effect on everyone: +20% damage per enemy in line, -20% per ally in line; avoid lining up with your allies.

mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.title: Classic dungeon: heals his allies, fleeing AI
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.summary: The Bouftou Royal heals his allies up to 6 range (not himself), only hits in melee and backs off after hitting. He has a lot of HP and resistances: the guide advises keeping him at a distance, killing the monsters one by one (Bouftou Noir and Chef de Guerre first), then finishing him from outside his range.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.notes.0: Place a summon or a character next to him so he hits and then backs off.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Placement phase: place one character close to the Bouftou Royal (not a character with agility or lock), the others far away.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He has a fleeing AI: he hits this character and then backs off. If he is locked, he does not back off.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.2.action: After his hit, move far away from him.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He only hits in melee: keep him at a distance so he does not come and hit you every turn.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If he gets too close, place a summon near him.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: He hits the summon and then backs off.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Kill the monsters one by one, Bouftou Noir and Chef de Guerre Bouftou first.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: He heals his allies up to 6 range (Guérison Bouftou, 200 HP); these two monsters are the most dangerous.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Once he is alone, focus him while staying at least 7 cells away from him.
mech.bouftou-royal.soigneur-fuyard.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He has 5 MP; he cannot heal himself.

mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.title: Expedition: invulnerable at range, must be hit in melee
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.summary: In the guild expedition, the Tournesol Affamé cannot be moved and is invulnerable at range: you must hit him in melee, while he one-shots in close combat. The guide advises killing all the monsters first while staying at range, then hitting him in melee and moving out of his range afterwards, or killing him in one turn.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.prerequisites.0: Guild expedition version of the fight (not the classic dungeon).
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.notes.0: If he kills a summon, he gains 4 MP and a shield worth 20% of his HP for 4 turns (effects can be debuffed).
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.notes.1: He can teleport next to an ally or swap places with it: do not let any enemy near you.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.notes.2: Each monster has 100% resistance in one element; MP reduction is useful since he cannot be moved.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.unknownAspects.0: Page with no update date (published 2018): values may predate Dofus 3.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Guild expedition, before entering: bring MP reduction.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The Tournesol Affamé cannot be moved, but you can remove his MP to keep him at a distance.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Kill all the monsters while staying strictly at a distance from all enemies.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He one-shots in melee and can teleport next to an ally or swap places with it: a monster close to you can cost you a character.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not summon near the enemies.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: If he one-shots a summon, he gains 4 MP and a shield worth 20% of his HP for 4 turns (can be debuffed).
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.4.action: On even turns, move away from his summons.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Appel des Champs summons a monster within 4 range, onto which he can teleport. Soin Feuillu also gives him 4 MP for one turn every two turns.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Once the monsters are dead, hit him in melee, then move back out of his range.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He is invulnerable at range: you must hit him in melee. At range, he is completely harmless.
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Alternatively, prepare to kill him in one turn (for example full buff on turn 1, kill on turn 2).
mech.tournesol-affame.expedition-invulne.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Alternative suggested by the guide with a good melee team. With a Rogue, detonate bombs placed in melee range of him.

mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.title: Expedition: 100% resistances, reduced by hitting the Pichons
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.summary: In the guild expedition, Mob l'Éponge has 100% resistance everywhere and his monsters are invulnerable for the whole fight; killing him is enough to win. Each damage line dealt to a Pichon removes 1% resistance from him (infinite) and sends 100% of that damage back to him in the Pichon's element (Orange fire, Blue water, Green earth, White air).
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.prerequisites.0: Guild expedition version of the fight (not the classic dungeon).
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.notes.0: Use area and multi-line spells on the Pichons; the controlled Pichon Kloune's "Klounerie" spell doubles the damage sent back.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.notes.1: He has 0 pushback resistance: killing him with pushback damage is an alternative (he heals himself every 4 turns).
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.notes.2: Pichon Orange's red glyph: removes 10 MP, applies gravity and deals heavy damage if you end your turn in it.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.unknownAspects.0: Page with no update date (published 2018): values may predate Dofus 3.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.unknownAspects.1: The classic dungeon has no boss mechanic described (only his spells).
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Guild expedition, before entering: avoid air, favour multi-line area spells, equip a Dofus Abyssal; loot 5 recommended.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The enemies have 50 to 66% air resistance; every line counts; the Dofus Abyssal gives 1 MP that the red glyph cannot remove.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep Mob l'Éponge at a distance, or block him between two monsters in a corner / lock him.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He is only dangerous within 2 range; his poison "Dégraissage" is cast at a minimum of 3 range with line of sight (watch out for the Pichon Bleu, which makes you unable to lock).
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit the Pichons (invulnerable), not the boss, with as many damage lines as possible and with area spells.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Each line on a Pichon removes 1% resistance (infinite) from Mob l'Éponge and sends 100% of the damage back to him in the Pichon's element, whatever the distance.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Without area spells: focus on a single Pichon, the closest one.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: It is better to lower his resistances in a single element than in several.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Never end your turn in the Pichon Orange's red glyph.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: It removes 10 MP, applies Pesanteur (no teleportation), deals huge damage and 30% erosion; get out of it with an MP gain or a rush.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Option: kill the Pichon Kloune, protect it, and use "Klounerie".
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Whoever kills it takes control of it; Klounerie doubles the damage Mob l'Éponge takes from the reflected damage.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Keep going until Mob l'Éponge dies.
mech.mob-l-eponge.expedition-resistances.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Killing him ends the fight in victory; no need to kill the monsters.

mech.kardorim.kardorib.title: Kardorib summoned on turn 1, then every 6 turns
mech.kardorim.kardorib.summary: Boss of the first dungeon, with simple mechanics: he hits in melee, summons a Kardorib on turn 1 (melee, pushes back 2 cells) that can be resummoned every 6 turns, and gains 1 MP every 3 turns from turn 2. He is weak to water and earth; the guide advises focusing him first.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Focus the Kardorim first, preferably with water or earth.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He has only 140 to 200 HP, 4 MP, and water and earth weaknesses.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Turn 1: expect him to move forward and summon his Kardorib.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: The Kardorib hits in melee and pushes back 2 cells (pushback damage if you are against an obstacle).
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.3.action: If the Kardorib gets in the way, kill it; otherwise keep it at a distance.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: It cannot be resummoned for 6 turns.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Stay out of the Kardorim's melee range.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: He only hits in melee and gives himself 1 MP for 1 turn every 3 turns from turn 2.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Once the Kardorim is dead, finish off the monsters.
mech.kardorim.kardorib.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He usually goes down in 1 to 2 turns.

mech.grozilla.lien-fusionnel-fission.title: Level 190 version: kill both bosses in the same global turn
mech.grozilla.lien-fusionnel-fission.summary: On the level 190 version only, if Grozilla or Grasmera dies, the survivor kills a random character at the start of each turn, with no possible counter. The only way to avoid this is to kill both during the same global turn; the guide advises balanced focus between them.
mech.grozilla.lien-fusionnel-fission.prerequisites.0: Level 190 Grozilla and Grasmera version (inactive on Somnambules, Épuisés, Fatigués).

mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.title: Level 190 version: stay within 2 range of each other on turns 6, 11, 16…
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.summary: On the level 190 version, Grozilla casts Atomes Crochus on turn 5 and then every 5 turns. If, at the start of his next turn (turns 6, 11, 16…), Grozilla is not within 2 range of Grasmera, Grasmera gets the Apocalypse state and can cast the spell that kills all characters (defeat).
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.turnConditions: Start of Grozilla's turn on turns 6, 11, 16, etc.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.notes.0: They can be pushed or pulled, but not carried or swapped; MP reduction and lock help keep them close.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Choose your strategy: at range (pushback / MP reduction) or block-and-lock both bosses side by side.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The guide offers these two strategies; they are harmless at range and cannot be carried or swapped, but can be pushed or pulled.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Keep Grozilla and Grasmera close to each other throughout the fight.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: This makes it easy to reposition them on turn 5 (level 190 version).
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.3.action: On turn 5 (then every 5 turns), place Grozilla within 2 range of Grasmera before the start of Grozilla's turn.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Version 190: Atomes Crochus is cast on turn 5; if on turns 6, 11, 16… they are not within 2 range, Grasmera enters the Apocalypse state and her spell kills all characters (defeat).
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Do not get hit by one and then by the other.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Tyrannisé + Météoroïde: damage equal to 50% of your current HP; damage from one + pull/rush from the other: your next turn is skipped.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Lock them (about 180 lock) or keep them at range to prevent their positioning spells.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Their rush and pull spells have a minimum range of 2: when locked, they cannot use them.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Hide behind obstacles in the ranged strategy.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: If Grasmera cannot pull herself onto an enemy, her AI often makes her pull herself onto Grozilla.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Spread the damage evenly and kill them both in the same global turn.
mech.grozilla.atomes-crochus-apocalypse.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Version 190: if one dies, the survivor kills a random character at the start of each turn, with no possible counter.

mech.grozilla.combos-tyrannise-meteoroid.title: State combos: 50% of current HP or turn skipped
mech.grozilla.combos-tyrannise-meteoroid.summary: All versions: Tyrannisation (Grozilla) applies the Tyrannisé state and Météore (Grasmera) the Météoroïde state. Being hit by one and then the other deals damage equal to 50% of current HP; taking damage from one and then the pull/rush of the other makes you skip your next turn. Locking them prevents these positioning spells (minimum range 2).
mech.grozilla.combos-tyrannise-meteoroid.notes.0: The guide recommends playing at range or locking/blocking them (~180 lock).

mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.title: Remove invulnerability (even turns only)
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.summary: The Count is invulnerable for the whole fight and the state can only be removed on even turns (2, 4, 6…). On an even turn, when you hit him, he is the one who teleports 180° relative to you: if this movement makes him swap places with an entity (ally or enemy), he loses his invulnerability. On an odd turn, it is instead you who are teleported 180° around him with each hit.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.expectedResult: Comte Harebourg loses his invulnerable state.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.turnConditions: Even turns only. On odd turns, each hit on the Count teleports the attacker 180° around him.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.notes.0: If the arrival cell of a rotation (yours on an odd turn, the Count's on an even turn) is inaccessible, the fight ends and all your characters are killed.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.notes.1: Swapping with an allied summon: all allies within a 3-cell area around the Count's starting position die.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.notes.2: The ally who swaps places with the Count (even turn) gains 100 damage for one turn: plan for them to hit right after.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.notes.3: The turn after he loses invulnerability, Contretemps teleports the target to its start-of-turn cell: be careful not to end up in his glyph.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.unknownAspects.0: Duration of the vulnerability not specified by the source.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Wait for an even turn (2, 4, 6…) and check the state displayed above the Count (since 3.6).
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: It shows who will be teleported when you hit him: you (odd turn) or him (even turn).
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Place an entity (preferably an ally) on the cell symmetrical to the Count relative to your character: in a straight line, on the other side of you, at the same distance as the Count.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: On an even turn, the Count rotates 180° around whoever hits him and lands on the other side of that character: he must land on this entity to swap places with it.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Check that this cell exists and is neither an obstacle nor off the map.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: If the rotation is impossible, the fight ends and all your characters die.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Do not use an allied summon for the swap.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: In that case, all allies within 3 cells of the Count's starting position are killed.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Hit the Count: he swaps places with the entity and loses his invulnerability.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: The ally who swapped places with him gains 100 damage for one turn: have them hit right after.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.action: To keep hitting him without him teleporting on every hit, use Stabilisation or another gravity spell on him.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: You then always know where he is so you can aim your spells despite the confusion.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.action: If you do not kill him this turn, choose where you leave him at the end of the turn.
mech.comte-harebourg.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: He starts his turn on this cell and places the Mi-temps glyph there (size 3 cross, center included): no ally must start their turn inside it, and Contretemps sends the target back to its start-of-turn cell.

mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.title: Glyphs from three different monsters
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.summary: Each monster killed leaves a brown glyph on its cell, then resurrects. Placing Tal Kasha on the glyphs of three different monsters permanently removes her invulnerability.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.expectedResult: Tal Kasha loses her invulnerable state for the rest of the fight.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.vulnerabilityDuration: Permanent (until the end of the fight)
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.notes.0: If you remove her MP, she swaps places with the responsible character (once per turn).
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.notes.1: Once vulnerable, she unlocks a teleport of up to 4 range: keep her away from the group.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.notes.2: With more than 4 players, 3 glyphs from 3 different monsters are enough even if there are more glyphs.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.notes.3: Killing a resurrected monster again moves its glyph to the cell where it last died.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.unknownAspects.0: The guide says in one place that Tal Kasha must "pass over" the glyphs, and elsewhere that she must "start her turn" on them: the exact condition is not settled.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Kill a monster: it drops a brown glyph on the cell where it died (it will resurrect on Tal Kasha's turn).
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Bring Tal Kasha onto that glyph; a counter (I to III) above her shows the number of glyphs validated.
mech.tal-kasha.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Repeat with two other different monsters until the counter reaches III.

mech.founoroshi.feux.title: Put out the 8 fires
mech.founoroshi.feux.summary: All monsters and the Founoroshi are invulnerable. You must put out the 8 fires on the map, each one requiring the "Extinction des feux" state obtained in a black glyph placed by the boss.
mech.founoroshi.feux.expectedResult: The monsters and the Founoroshi become vulnerable and stay that way; you also gain 15% damage per game turn.
mech.founoroshi.feux.vulnerabilityDuration: Until the end of the fight
mech.founoroshi.feux.turnConditions: An extinguished fire relights after 8 turns as long as the invulnerability has not been removed.
mech.founoroshi.feux.notes.0: For each fire put out, the Founoroshi gains 1 MP, 10% damage and 1 range for 4 turns.
mech.founoroshi.feux.notes.1: The "Extinction des feux" state does not stack: walking through two black glyphs only lets you put out one fire.
mech.founoroshi.feux.notes.2: The "Extinction des feux" state removes 3 range and 20 AP/MP dodge.
mech.founoroshi.feux.notes.3: Black glyphs still present at the start of the Founoroshi's turn disappear.
mech.founoroshi.feux.notes.4: Since 2.70, companions and non-static summons can also put out the fires.
mech.founoroshi.feux.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Walk into a black glyph (now displayed in blue) placed by the Founoroshi at the end of his turn to get the "Extinction des feux" state.
mech.founoroshi.feux.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Without this state, entering a fire's glyph does not put it out.
mech.founoroshi.feux.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Stand on the brown glyph to the right of a fire to put it out.
mech.founoroshi.feux.sequences.0.steps.2.position: Brown glyph one cell to the right of the fire
mech.founoroshi.feux.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Repeat until all 8 fires are out (one state = one fire).

mech.guerre.arsenal.title: Kill all accompanying monsters
mech.guerre.arsenal.summary: The Arsenal spell gives the monsters the "Compagnon de combat" state: as long as one remains, Guerre is invulnerable. She becomes vulnerable the turn after the last monster dies.
mech.guerre.arsenal.expectedResult: Guerre becomes vulnerable (and much more dangerous).
mech.guerre.arsenal.turnConditions: Vulnerable the turn after the last monster dies.
mech.guerre.arsenal.prerequisites.0: All monsters accompanying Guerre are dead.
mech.guerre.arsenal.notes.0: Guerre cannot be moved for the whole fight.
mech.guerre.arsenal.notes.1: Once vulnerable, she summons a weapon at each HP threshold (80, 60, 40 and 20%).
mech.guerre.arsenal.notes.2: Killing a weapon after Guerre has played again heals her and gives her resistances and MP (stackable): kill the weapon before her turn, or don't kill it.
mech.guerre.arsenal.notes.3: Weapons are invulnerable for one turn after being summoned.
mech.guerre.arsenal.unknownAspects.0: Duration of the vulnerability not specified (the source does not mention a return to invulnerability).
mech.guerre.arsenal.sequences.0.steps.1.target: Monsters with the "Compagnon de combat" state
mech.guerre.arsenal.sequences.0.steps.2.action: On the next turn, Guerre mounts her steed and becomes vulnerable; she puts one of your characters (or a summon) in the "Brave" state and targets it for 2 turns.

mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.title: Remove the 900% resistances (tentacles)
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.summary: The Kralamoure has 900% resistance in all elements. Hitting it in an element summons the matching tentacle on the next turn. Once all 4 tentacles are in place, the Primaire must swallow a summon that the other three hit on the same turn without killing it, then swallow another one the next turn: the Kralamoure then loses its resistances for 1 turn.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.expectedResult: The Kralamoure loses its 900% resistances for 1 turn.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.notes.0: The resistance penalty can be debuffed: do not use any debuff spell, or you have to start over.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.notes.1: On that same turn, the tentacles gain 1000 vitality and 2 MP and can kill in melee: keep them from reaching your characters.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.notes.2: Without resistances, the Kralamoure hits very hard (can kill two characters): kill it that turn or put the Primaire back in front of it.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.notes.3: If you don't finish it, reposition the tentacles and redo the setup (steps 5 to 7).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.label: Sequence recommended by the guide
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Turn 1: hit the Kralamoure with water (summons the Quaternaire tentacle).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Turn 2: hit with fire (summons the Tertiaire).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Turn 3: hit with earth (summons the Secondaire).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Turn 4: hit with air (summons the Primaire, to be summoned last because it kills in melee except on its first turn).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Place the Primaire in front of the Kralamoure and a summon in contact with it, hidden behind it (out of the Kralamoure's line of sight).
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.5.position: Primaire facing the Kralamoure; summon behind the Primaire
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Have the Primaire swallow the summon; on the same turn, the other three tentacles must hit one same summon without killing it.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.7.action: On the next turn, the Primaire must kill a summon again.
mech.kralamoure-geant.tentacules.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: In the guide's typical sequence, the Kralamoure loses its resistances on turn 7.

mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.title: Push back with the snowdrifts
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.summary: Missiz Frizz and her monsters are heavy and start invulnerable. An enemy pushed back by a snowdrift's effect (black glyph) loses its invulnerability for 1 turn.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.expectedResult: The pushed-back enemy loses its invulnerability for 1 turn.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.notes.0: The "Monogel" effect also acts like a snowdrift when an entity is pushed by a spell, but heals the pushed entity for 15% of its max HP.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.notes.1: Be careful not to push an ally into an obstacle when triggering a snowdrift (pushback damage).
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.notes.2: The Indéplaçable, Enraciné or Inébranlable states prevent being pushed by snowdrifts (also useful on Missiz to avoid healing her).
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.sequences.0.steps.1.action: At the start of each character's turn, snowdrifts (black glyphs) appear on the 4 adjacent cells.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Summons do not make snowdrifts appear.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Trigger a snowdrift by walking into it: you are pushed one cell and the entities around your landing cell (line and diagonals) are pushed back.
mech.missiz-frizz.congeres.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit the pushed-back enemy during the turn it is vulnerable.

mech.kimbo.glyphes.title: Even / odd glyphs
mech.kimbo.glyphes.summary: The Kimbo is not invulnerable but has 400% resistance in all elements. Hitting it with a pair of elements makes its Disciple place glyphs; if it starts its turn on one of them, it loses 400% resistance in that pair for 1 turn.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.expectedStateChange: Loss of 400% resistance in the chosen pair
mech.kimbo.glyphes.expectedResult: The Kimbo loses 400% resistance in the two chosen elements for 1 turn.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.notes.0: A character who starts their turn on one of these glyphs is killed: plan your positioning before the Disciple's turn.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.notes.1: Once its glyphs are cast, the Disciple also kills in melee.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.notes.2: If you don't finish it in 1 turn, reapply the state so the Disciple recasts the glyphs on the next turn.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.0.label: Earth / Water pair
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Hit the Kimbo with earth or water: it enters the Glyphe impaire state and the Disciple places glyphs on every cell at an odd distance from it.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Make the Kimbo start its turn on one of these glyphs.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Hit with earth or water during the turn it has lost its resistances.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: At the same time it gains 800% air/fire resistance.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.1.label: Air / Fire pair
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.1.steps.1.action: Hit the Kimbo with air or fire: it enters the Glyphe paire state and the Disciple places glyphs on every cell at an even distance from it.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.1.steps.2.action: Make the Kimbo start its turn on one of these glyphs.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.1.steps.3.action: Hit with air or fire during the turn it has lost its resistances.
mech.kimbo.glyphes.sequences.1.steps.3.rationale: At the same time it gains 800% water/earth resistance.

mech.merkator.mer-kantile.title: Mer Kantile: reduced ranged damage
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.summary: From the start of the fight until the end, Merkator takes 50% less damage at range, and he and all the monsters cannot be moved.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.notes.0: Merkator and all the monsters are in the Indéplaçable state for the whole fight.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.notes.1: From turn 7 (5-turn cooldown), Bouche-à-Bouche re-summons the last dead ally with 50% of its vitality.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.unknownAspects.0: The source gives no method to cancel Mer Kantile.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Stay far from Merkator during the monster phase.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: His spells have very little range (Sondage de Bronze in a line up to 3 range, Torpillage de Glace in melee): he is almost harmless at range.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Do not remove MP from the monsters without protection (Ataraxie, Bastion, Feca's Égide).
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Mer Veille effect: any MP removal attempt deals you about 500 fire life steal.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Kill the Eskoglyphe first, then the Harpo, and the Cyclophandre last.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: The Eskoglyphe gives MP to its allies; on turn 3, the Harpo is boosted and Moule Chote deals huge damage (get out of line of sight or within 5 range).
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.4.action: On odd turns (from turn 3), do not be in line with Merkator.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Marée Descendante: he pulls all characters in line up to 12 range into melee and removes 4 MP from them.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Optional: place summons near him, or push him back via Mer Cure.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: He will prefer to hit the summons; Mer Cure lets you move enemies despite the Indéplaçable state (not needed to succeed).
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Once he is alone: wear him down slowly at range, or hit him in melee to go faster.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Mer Kantile: he takes 50% less damage at range for the whole fight (and gains 2% final damage for each ranged damage instance).
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Under Baphe Thysca, avoid hitting him, or avoid getting hit afterwards.
mech.merkator.mer-kantile.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Each damage instance he takes increases Sondage de Bronze's base damage by 30 (stacks 5 times): this is the only time he is dangerous.

mech.meulou.fureur.title: Fureur: reduced first attack and power gain
mech.meulou.fureur.summary: Each character's first attack against the Meulou is reduced by 50%. Each damage line taken by the Meulou or an allied monster gives him 30 power (stackable, debuffable).
mech.meulou.fureur.notes.0: Every damage line counts: a 4-line spell gives 4 × 30 power. Avoid hitting him while he is not your priority target.
mech.meulou.fureur.notes.1: A Milimeulou that dies gives 2 MP and 200 power for 2 turns to all its allies: only kill it if necessary.
mech.meulou.fureur.unknownAspects.0: Duration of the power bonus: the page says 3 turns in two places and 4 turns in another.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Placement: start the fight as far as possible from the Meulou.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Starting cells farthest from the Meulou
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He has 7 base MP and hits very hard with life steal, only in melee. The more distance, the better.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Ignore the Meulou at first: stay at range and kill the monsters first, in the order Cocholou > Muloubard > Mulounoké.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: Each damage line he takes gives him 30 power. The Inébranlable Muloubard cannot be pushed back and reduces ranged damage 2 turns out of 4.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Do not kill the Milimeulous and do not summon (except in an emergency or if he already has 2 summons).
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: A Milimeulou that dies gives 2 MP and 200 power for 2 turns to its allies; a summon he kills is replaced by a Mulou (limit of 2 summons).
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Once the Meulou is alone, pick a method: keep him at range (push back, remove MP), tank him (only with healing and protection), or block him in a corner between 2 of his summons.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: For blocking, the guide often advises waiting for turn 9 and the 2nd Milimeulou, since the Mulou is more dangerous.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Each turn, each character first deals him one damage line to remove the reduction, then hits.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Fureur: each character's first attack is reduced by 50%; that line still gives him 30 power.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Hit with big single-line attacks, preferably in the fire element.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: His only weakness is fire (-5%) and each damage line boosts him by 30 power.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Counter Rage Reconstituante: leave him around 81% HP, or erode him, reduce his heals just before, or make him Insoignable.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Heal of 2000 HP (3000 on a critical) + 2 MP and 20 lock, from turn 2 then every 6 turns, only effective if he has 80% HP or less. With 2 characters in melee, he often prefers to hit.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.8.action: "Meulou y es-tu ?" achievement: never more than 3 damage lines per character per turn on an enemy, so avoid 3- or 4-line spells.
mech.meulou.fureur.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: One of the three attacks is already used to remove the 50% reduction; a 4-line spell fails the achievement.

mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.title: "Gravelines": invulnerable, removed by a critical hit or weapon hit with an ally in contact with her
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.summary: Armada and all the monsters accompanying her are permanently invulnerable. When a team character lands a critical hit or hits with a weapon, every character triggers "Gravelines" on their adjacent cells: if one of them is in contact with Armada, she loses her invulnerability for 2 turns. Only Armada is affected.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.prerequisites.0: At least one character in contact with Armada.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.prerequisites.1: A team character lands a critical hit or hits with a weapon.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.notes.0: The unlock only works on Armada, never on the monsters accompanying her.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.sequences.0.label: Make Armada vulnerable
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Place a character in contact with Armada.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Land a critical hit or a weapon attack with any team character.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.invulner.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: All characters then trigger "Gravelines" on their 4 adjacent cells.

mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.allies-i.title: Accompanying monsters invulnerable while Armada lives
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.allies-i.summary: The monsters accompanying Armada stay invulnerable: the only way to make them vulnerable is to eliminate Armada first.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.allies-i.expectedStateChange: The accompanying monsters lose the invulnerable state.

mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.tankafai.title: "Tankafair": avoid unlocking her during this effect
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.tankafai.summary: "Tankafair" lasts 2 turns (4-turn cooldown). If Armada is made vulnerable during that time, she gains shields (20% of her HP) for 1 turn and reduces the damage she takes for 2 turns. The guide advises waiting for the effect to end before unlocking her.
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.tankafai.notes.0: Flibs can accompany Armada and make the monsters invisible for 1 turn, which can waste one of the 2 vulnerability turns.

mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.allies-d.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.armada-l-invincible.allies-d.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -300 vitality and -50 power (infinite) per monster present with her. Alone in the fight, there is no penalty.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.invulnerab.title: Permanently invulnerable at range ("Eau Myope")
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.invulnerab.summary: Carter is invulnerable at range for the whole fight and this state cannot be removed. You must hit him in melee, so enter his green glyphs, or use damage interception (see dedicated mechanic).
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.invulnerab.notes.0: He has no MP and cannot be moved: you have to go to him.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.intercepti.title: Hit Carter at range via the brown glyph's interception
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.intercepti.summary: When Carter places his brown glyph "Ce qui est à toi est à moi", he intercepts the damage of the monsters inside the area at the moment it is placed. Hitting those monsters (at range or in contact) then deals the damage to Carter without going into contact with him.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.intercepti.prerequisites.0: Monsters accompany Carter and are inside the brown glyph's area at the moment he places it.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.intercepti.notes.0: Placing a monster yourself into an already-placed brown glyph does not work.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.intercepti.notes.1: Impossible if Carter is alone in the fight.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphes-ve.title: Two growing green glyphs: stacking penalties
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphes-ve.summary: From turn 1 Carter places a green glyph around himself whose radius grows by 1 each turn; on turn 2 he places a second one, offset by one radius. Being in a green glyph gives a power, resistance and range penalty for 1 turn, applied twice when you are in both glyphs; starting your turn inside also deals air damage.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphes-ve.unknownAspects.0: Contradictory values: the quick overview gives a total of -30% resistance and -6 range with both glyphs, the spell description gives -60% and -12 range.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphe-ble.title: Blue glyph: do not end your turn inside
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphe-ble.summary: From turn 2 then every 3 turns, Carter places a blue glyph (radius 3, 2 turns). Ending your turn inside makes you skip your next turn; if it overlaps the main green glyph, it also deals water damage.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphe-mar.title: Brown glyph: AP theft between allies
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.glyphe-mar.summary: The brown glyph (radius 2 then 3, 2 turns, from turn 1 then every 3 turns) makes a character who starts their turn inside steal 2 AP for 2 turns from all their allies around them (radius 2).

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.champignon.title: Champignon de Carter: finish it off to get boosted
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.champignon.summary: Each turn, Carter summons a Champignon de Carter (1 HP) if the previous one is gone. Eliminating it gives 300 power for 2 turns to the characters in contact with it.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.champignon.sequences.0.label: Guide's tip
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.champignon.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Gather as many characters as possible around the mushroom, then finish it off.
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.champignon.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Offset the green glyphs' power penalty.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.resistance.title: Very resistant to air and neutral
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.resistance.summary: Carter has 100% air resistance and 50% neutral; the guide recommends earth and water (10%), with fire at 30%.

mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.allies-de-.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.carter-le-pillard.allies-de-.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -1500 vitality (infinite) per monster present with him. Alone in the fight, he has no penalty.

mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.title: "Garde à vous": invulnerable for 2 turns if pushed or targeted by AP/MP removal
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.summary: The Chevalier is not invulnerable by default, but becomes so for 2 turns as soon as someone tries to push him or remove his AP or MP. So avoid these actions when you want to hit him.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.expectedStateChange: The Chevalier becomes invulnerable for 2 turns.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.notes.0: The Pandawa's carry/throw spells do not trigger the invulnerability: useful to reposition him.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.notes.1: Pushing him back or removing his MP to protect yourself makes him invulnerable; the guide suggests a tank in contact instead.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.1.action: If he is accompanied, prefer a ranged map and kill his allies first while pushing him back each turn.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: The guide states that the invulnerability caused by pushing does not matter while you deal with the monsters, and this way you avoid his big 2-range spell.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Never take pushback damage: no pushing between allies, watch out for the Verglasseurs.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: "Garde à vous": any character who takes pushback damage is one-shot. The Verglasseurs push back 2 cells in melee, and pull/push 3 cells in a line at 4 range.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.3.action: To move him away or position him without making him invulnerable, use the Pandawa's carry/throw.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: These spells do not apply the invulnerable state to him.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.4.action: When you want to hit him: do not push him and do not attempt any AP or MP removal.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Each of these actions makes him invulnerable for 2 turns.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.5.action: When he is alone, block him in contact with a tank character (for example a tank Pandawa).
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.5.position: Tank in contact with the Chevalier
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: No more need to push him or remove his MP to keep him from hitting the others.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Without a tank, stay out of range of "Tranchant absorbant" and account for "Saut".
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: Tranchant absorbant (up to 2 range) hits for 600 air + 600 water life steal; Saut teleports him up to 5 range every 4 turns, unless he is under Pesanteur.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Keep the other monsters away from the team.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: "Souffler n'est pas jouer" makes him swap places with a monster up to 14 range (3-turn cooldown, impossible under Pesanteur), which can put him in the middle of the team.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.8.action: Hit him with fire and water, avoid earth.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.invulnera.sequences.0.steps.8.rationale: Weaknesses: fire (-15%) and water (-20%); high earth resistance (50%).

mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.poussee-m.title: Any pushback damage kills the character
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.poussee-m.summary: For the whole fight, a character who takes pushback damage dies immediately. Watch out for the Verglasseurs (push spells) and for pushes between allies.

mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.distance-.title: Stay out of range of "Tranchant absorbant" (2 range)
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.distance-.summary: His most dangerous spell is cast up to 2 range: without a tank to block him, keep your distance. Account for "Saut" (teleport up to 5 range, every 4 turns) and his place swap with an ally, both impossible when he has the Pesanteur state.
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.distance-.notes.0: Keep the accompanying monsters away from the team: he can swap places with them ("Souffler n'est pas jouer", 14 range).

mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.allies-de.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.chevalier-de-glace.allies-de.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -2000 vitality and -50 power (infinite) per monster present with him. Alone in the fight, he has no penalty.

mech.wanted.crasper.reduction-armes.title: Immune to weapons ("Fantôme")
mech.wanted.crasper.reduction-armes.summary: Crasper is not invulnerable, but the damage he takes from weapons is reduced by 5000 for the whole fight: weapons deal 0, you must hit him only with spells.
mech.wanted.crasper.reduction-armes.notes.0: Hitting with a weapon: no damage.

mech.wanted.crasper.echange-fin-de-tour.title: Automatic place swap at end of turn
mech.wanted.crasper.echange-fin-de-tour.summary: At the end of each of his turns, Crasper automatically swaps places with an enemy located more than 4 range from him.
mech.wanted.crasper.echange-fin-de-tour.unknownAspects.0: The guide also advises staying more than 7 range from him without explaining the interaction with this place swap.

mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.title: Hanté state: poisons on AP and MP used
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.summary: "Lieu Hanté" (radius 5 area) applies the Hanté state (skull), erosion and two earth poisons triggered by AP and MP used. While Hanté, a target hit by "Crasse" also loses range and rolls minimum values.
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.notes.0: "Amical" (melee) removes the Hanté state but the poisons remain.
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.sequences.0.label: Handle the Hanté state
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: Limit the number of characters hit by the radius 5 area.
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Poisoned characters: spend as few AP and MP as possible (prefer spending AP to hit).
mech.wanted.crasper.hante-poisons.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Debuff the affected characters if needed.

mech.wanted.crasper.distance.title: Stay more than 7 range away
mech.wanted.crasper.distance.summary: Crasper only hits and applies Pacifiste in contact: the guide says to stay more than 7 range from him (6 MP + the melee cell) for the whole fight.

mech.wanted.crasper.allies-de-circonstan.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.crasper.allies-de-circonstan.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -1400 vitality (infinite) per monster present with him. Alone in the fight, he has no penalty.

mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reduction-melee.title: 2200 melee damage reduction: hit at range
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reduction-melee.summary: Culbutoeuf is not invulnerable, but he reduces the damage he takes in melee by 2200 for the whole fight. You must hit him at range, otherwise your hits do nothing.
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reduction-melee.notes.0: Even a heavily charged melee attack (Iop's Colère de Iop) is almost useless.
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reduction-melee.notes.1: Keep him from coming into contact: you can neither push him nor easily escape his melee.

mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.title: "Reste à ta place": Inébranlable for everyone, -2 MP, penalty on swaps/teleports
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.summary: Everyone (monsters and characters) is Inébranlable for the whole fight: no pushing or pulling. Characters lose 2 MP for the whole fight and take -50% resistance (infinite, stackable) for each place swap or teleport they undergo.
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.sequences.0.label: Guide's tips
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Have at least 6 MP per character (an Abyssal Dofus helps).
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: According to the guide, his spells work on the Inébranlable state.
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.sequences.0.steps.3.action: Beware of monsters that swap places (Granduk "Hiboumerang", Cycloïde "Cyclochette").
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.reste-a-ta-place.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Each swap undergone costs -50% resistance, stackable.

mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.du-fond-du-coeur.title: "Du fond du cœur": debuff the targets
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.du-fond-du-coeur.summary: This spell hits characters on his adjacent cells hard with fire and removes MP and power from them with erosion. The guide advises debuffing the affected characters as soon as possible.

mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.allies-de-circons.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.culbutoeuf.allies-de-circons.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -2000 vitality and -50 power (infinite) per monster present with him. Alone in the fight, he has no penalty.

mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.title: Invulnerable until a Germe de Dremoan appears (from turn 3)
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.summary: Dremoan is invulnerable from the start. He loses it for the rest of the fight as soon as he creates a Germe de Dremoan from a monster or a summon in the Zombi state. With monsters: kill one, Dremoan resurrects it as a Zombi then turns it into a Germe. Alone: cast a summon, which he will make Zombi then turn into a Germe. Impossible before his turn 3.
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.vulnerabilityDuration: Until the end of the fight
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.notes.0: Killing several monsters or summoning several times multiplies the Germes, which are very troublesome; one is enough.
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.notes.1: If he is accompanied, avoid summoning: the summons will also end up as Germes.
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.label: Make a Germe appear
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.action: If he is accompanied: kill only one monster.
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: He resurrects it as a Zombi ("Zombification putride") then turns it into a Germe ("Graine de Dremoan").
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.action: If he is alone: cast only one summon.
mech.wanted.dremoan.invulnerabilite.sequences.0.steps.2.rationale: He makes it Zombi ("Pourrissement accéléré") then turns it into a Germe.

mech.wanted.dremoan.mort-os.title: "Abominable Tragédie": one-shot around Dremoan and the Germes when he dies
mech.wanted.dremoan.mort-os.summary: When he dies, Dremoan kills all characters within a radius of 3 around him; the Germes die with him and each kills the characters within a radius of 2 around them. Move away before finishing him.
mech.wanted.dremoan.mort-os.sequences.0.label: Finish Dremoan
mech.wanted.dremoan.mort-os.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Before the final blow, place all characters more than 3 cells from Dremoan and more than 2 cells from each Germe.
mech.wanted.dremoan.mort-os.sequences.0.steps.1.position: Outside Dremoan's radius 3 / the Germes' radius 2

mech.wanted.dremoan.germes.title: Germes de Dremoan: explosion and heals after 4 turns
mech.wanted.dremoan.germes.summary: The Germes (1 MP, invulnerable, Lourds, Enracinés) are very troublesome (pulls, MP and range removal, poisons). After 4 game turns, they can explode if a target is 6 cells or less away (one-shot within a radius of 2, heavy neutral damage from 3 to 6) or heavily heal the monsters and Dremoan.
mech.wanted.dremoan.germes.notes.0: The guide advises killing Dremoan first (or second if a monster was used for the unlock).
mech.wanted.dremoan.germes.unknownAspects.0: The guide does not specify whether "4 game turns" counts from the Germe's summoning or from the start of the fight.

mech.wanted.dremoan.pourrissement.title: "Pourrissement accéléré": full immobilization (turns 3, 8, 13…)
mech.wanted.dremoan.pourrissement.summary: From turn 3 then every 5 turns, Dremoan removes 100 MP and applies the Pesanteur state to all characters for 1 turn: moving is impossible on those turns. The spell also turns summons into Zombis.

mech.wanted.dremoan.desenvoutement-soins.title: Debuffs himself every turn; heal and boost on turns 6, 11, 16
mech.wanted.dremoan.desenvoutement-soins.summary: Dremoan removes the effects on himself every turn (so the vulnerability applied by a Pandawa only lasts the current turn). On turns 6, 11 and 16, he heals himself for 3600 HP and gains 100 damage (infinite). He also poisons all characters with earth for the whole fight.
mech.wanted.dremoan.desenvoutement-soins.unknownAspects.0: Contradiction: debuff at the start of the turn (quick overview) or at the end of the turn ("Abomination" effect).

mech.wanted.dremoan.resistances.title: Fire weakness
mech.wanted.dremoan.resistances.summary: Dremoan has high resistances, except fire (0%): favour fire damage.

mech.wanted.dremoan.allies-de-circonstan.title: "Alliés de circonstance": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.dremoan.allies-de-circonstan.summary: Effect common to wanted bosses: -1500 vitality (infinite) per monster present with him (no penalty via the legendary hunt, where he is alone). Alone in the fight, he has no penalty.

mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.title: "Illutation": weapons useless, 100% neutral resistance
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.summary: Gadoo is not invulnerable, but he reduces the damage taken from weapons by 20 000: you must hit him with spells. He also has 100% neutral resistance.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.label: Steps to follow
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.1.action: Never hit Gadoo with a weapon: use only spells.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.1.rationale: "Illutation" reduces weapon damage by 20 000 for the whole fight: a weapon hits for 0.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.2.action: Do not hit him with neutral.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.3.rationale: Each earth hit gives him +5% fire/air resistance and +20 power for 1 turn, and he has 40% base earth resistance.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.4.action: Avoid the water element, except for very strong hits.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.4.rationale: Each water hit heals him for 100 HP (in exchange for -1% critical for 1 turn).
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.5.action: Do not leave characters grouped in a size 1 cross when he can cast "Croûte".
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.5.rationale: Croûte is cast as a size 1 cross area up to 10 range, every 3 turns.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.6.action: Quickly debuff any character hit by "Croûte".
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.6.rationale: The penalties trigger over 3 turns: -range, then -AP and Affaibli, then -MP, and finally the character skips their turn.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.7.action: Do not count on pushing or carrying to position him.
mech.wanted.gadoo.reduction-armes.sequences.0.steps.7.rationale: Gadoo can neither be pushed nor carried for the whole fight.

mech.wanted.gadoo.reactions-elements.title: Reactions to water and earth hits
mech.wanted.gadoo.reactions-elements.summary: Each water hit heals him for 100 HP (in exchange for -1% critical for 1 turn); each earth hit gives him +5% fire/air resistance and +20 power for 1 turn (in exchange for -5% earth/water resistance). The guide advises against both elements (earth at 40% base resistance), except for very strong water hits.

mech.wanted.gadoo.croute.title: "Croûte": debuff before the turn skip
mech.wanted.gadoo.croute.summary: "Croûte" (size 1 cross area, every 3 turns) applies penalties that trigger over 3 turns: range, then AP and Affaibli, then MP, and finally a turn skip. Quickly debuff the target and do not group characters in a cross.

mech.wanted.gadoo.allies-marecageux.title: "Alliés marécageux": penalty per accompanying monster
mech.wanted.gadoo.allies-marecageux.summary: Variant of the common effect: -300 vitality and -25 power (infinite) per monster present with him. Alone, no penalty.

mech.wanted.gein.invulnerabilite.title: Invisible and invulnerable: hit a Feu des âmes perdues 2 cells or less from him
mech.wanted.gein.invulnerabilite.summary: Gein is invulnerable and invisible except during his own turn. Any summon cast by a character is replaced by a "Feu des âmes perdues" (invulnerable skull with no AP/MP). Hitting a fire while Gein is within a radius of 2 around that fire makes him visible and vulnerable, but only for the turn of the character who revealed him; then he becomes invisible and invulnerable again and moves.
